findings.title: Brace-matching C function extractor copy-pasted into 110 test files (16 in this unit, three string-aware variants)
findings.problem: Each test defines its own function()/extract()/fn() that finds a signature and counts braces to the matching close; Grep finds a top-level definition in 110 files under tests/. The bodies are the same algorithm with cosmetic differences, and three files (cloud_history_browser, cloud_recovery, cloud_upload_ledger) carry a 26-30 line string/char-literal-aware version that the others lack, so a brace inside a string literal breaks some tests and not others.
findings.fix: Put one extractor (the string-aware one from test_cloud_history_browser.py) in a small tests/csource.py and import it, as tests already import mc_fixture via sys.path.insert(0, Path(__file__).parent); delete the local copies.
findings.justification: Adds one ~30-line module; removes 182 lines in the cited ranges of this unit alone and roughly 8 lines in each of ~94 further files, and gives every test the same literal-aware parsing.
findings.benefit: ~110 net lines in this unit (182 cited lines, minus ~30 for the shared module and ~2 import lines in each of 16 files), MEASURED from ranges; roughly 550 more repo-wide (~94 further files x ~6 net lines), INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Grep '^def (function|extract|fn|func|body|c_function)\(' in tests/: 110 files, one each. Read all 16 in this unit plus test_launch_driver_messages.py:27-34. String-aware variants: cloud_history_browser 17-46, cloud_recovery 19-46, cloud_upload_ledger 19-44. Shared import precedent: sys.path.insert in test_dash_card_tool.py:19, test_mc_card_write.py:22, test_mc_fingerprint.py:19, test_mc_card_view.py:9, test_mmce_save_versions.py:17, test_mmce_fingerprint_backup.py:16.

findings.title: Card-image backups (.mcd/.ps2) bypass the UPLOADED.TXT ledger, so every Drive sync opens one TLS session per already-uploaded snapshot
findings.problem: sync_tree consults the ledger only when psu is true (1544). Every already-uploaded WLE-*.mcd/.ps2 is therefore hashed in full (1302) and looked up on Drive (1310 -> drive_find_child -> cloudHttpRequest), and each request does DNS, TCP connect, CA parse, DRBG seed and a full TLS handshake with Connection: close (cloud_http.c:701, 715). This runs on the UI thread under dashLoadingBegin (dash_tools.c:360-363, 676-679) and in the IGR boot path (main.c:198); the default history depth is 10 per card (dash_store.c:260).
findings.fix: Delete the psu && condition at line 1544 so card images use the same ledger as .psu files (hash, ledger hit skips; miss validates and uploads with the known digest, then records the line). Update the assertion in tests/test_cloud_upload_ledger.py:51-53 and the UPLOADED.TXT paragraph in docs/NATIVE_CLOUD.md. Retention pruning only looks at WLE- names (mmce_backup.c:132), so an UPLOADED.TXT in card folders is harmless.
findings.benefit: One HTTPS session (DNS+TCP+TLS handshake+request) saved per old card snapshot per sync, e.g. 2 cards x 10 kept = 20 sessions per sync on the UI/IGR path (INFERRED; handshake time on the EE not measured). The 8 MB re-hash per image remains.
findings.evidence: Read sync_tree 1485-1579 and drive_upload_file 1270-1367: non-psu files skip the ledger, are validated (header-only, mc_card_export.c:218-222 -> source_info 173-203), hashed at 1302 and looked up at 1310. cloud_http.c request_open 694-726 calls tls_open (377-477) per request. Grep UPLOADED|upload_ledger: only cloud_google.c, docs/NATIVE_CLOUD.md:147-152, tests/test_cloud_upload_ledger.py (line 6 says the ledger must never be consulted for card images; no reason given; commit de11ede message gives none either). Grep 'WLE-' in mmce_backup.c: is_history name filter at 132. dash_store.c:260 default keep 10. The comment at cloud_google.c:1387-1388 itself states every Drive lookup is its own TLS session.

findings.title: Same file and POSIX helpers repeated across the C host harnesses (rd x3, slurp x3, spit x2, gen* stand-ins x2)
findings.problem: rd() is byte-identical in three harnesses; slurp()/spit() are identical in mc_ps1_card_host.c and mc_save_export_host.c, with a NULL-returning slurp variant in mc_save_formats_host.c; genLseek/genRead, genClose, genDclose/fileXioDread and genCmpFileExt are the same in dash_card_tool_host.c and mmce_save_versions_host.c (fileXioDread differs only in hisize). The path-mapping and fault-injection stand-ins differ and are not part of this finding.
findings.fix: Move rd, slurp, spit and the identical gen* stand-ins into one static-inline header in tests/ (for example host_io.h) included by these harnesses, and delete the copies.
findings.justification: Adds one header of ~60 lines; removes ~115 duplicated lines, so the harnesses cannot drift (mc_save_formats already behaves differently on read errors).
findings.benefit: ~65 net lines removed (MEASURED from ranges: 24 rd + 52 slurp/spit + 68 gen* lines deleted, minus a ~72-line header and ~8 include lines); no product change.
findings.evidence: Read all cited ranges side by side. Grep 'static .*(rd|slurp|spit)\(' in tests/: the six host files plus an unrelated slurp in test_app_packages.py:56. Script lead: mc_ps1_card_host.c 16% same as mc_save_export_host.c; mmce_save_versions_host.c 19% same as dash_card_tool_host.c.

findings.title: test_copy_pipeline.py and test_copy_psu_listing.py repeat the same ~40-line C define/typedef prefix and ~20 stubs

findings.justification: Adds one shared fragment of about the size of one copy; removes the second copy and the need to edit two files when filer_copy.c gains a dependency.
findings.benefit: ~45 lines removed (MEASURED: ~42 matching define/typedef lines plus ~15 identical one-line stubs, minus include/import lines); INFERRED less churn on filer_copy.c changes.

findings.title: test_cloud_tls_paths.py lines 22-65 test the host compiler's -ffile-prefix-map, not scripts/build_cloud_tls.sh
findings.problem: After checking the script text (16-20), the test writes its own one-line C file, compiles it with and without -ffile-prefix-map and compares objects; the shell escaping it exercises at line 59 is a Python re-implementation, not the script's. It therefore proves that gcc/clang implement the flag, which is toolchain behaviour, while the repo's own wiring is covered only by the text checks above it. The docstring itself calls it 'a portable host compiler smoke test, not a PS2 ELF reproducibility proof'.
findings.fix: Delete lines 22-65 and keep the text checks at 16-20 (or delete the file if those are judged not worth a CI step).
findings.benefit: 44 lines removed and five host compiles per CI run (MEASURED: 2 iterations x 2 compiles at 36-40 plus one at 60-63).
findings.evidence: Read test_cloud_tls_paths.py 1-67. Source text compiled: line 32 and 57 (test-written). Escaping: line 59 str.replace in Python. build_cloud_tls.sh is only read at line 13 and used in 16-20. compile.yml:240 runs the file.

findings.title: Tests assert that compile.yml runs themselves, which cannot fail in CI
findings.problem: Eighteen tests assert that the string 'python3 tests/<this file>.py' appears in compile.yml. When CI runs the test the line is necessarily there, so the assert can only fire when someone runs the file by hand after removing it from the workflow. In 15 of these files the compile.yml text is read only for this assert.
findings.fix: Delete the self-referencing asserts, and the compile.yml read in the 15 files where nothing else uses it.
findings.benefit: ~33 lines removed and one file read per run in 15 tests (MEASURED: 18 assert lines plus 15 read lines; grep -cw workflow is 2 in those 15 files).
findings.evidence: Grep 'in workflow' over the listed test files gives exactly these self-name asserts. Grep 'workflow' in test_cloud_upload_ledger.py: lines 15-16 only; in test_dash_card_tool.py: lines 23-24 only. test_dash_pause.py:22 reads and asserts in one line. Other files' workflow variable may have further uses, so only the assert line is cited there.

findings.title: cloudGoogleRecoverSnapshot copies a .mcd download to a stage file (8 MB write, 24 MB read) yet never checks the written file against the digest
findings.problem: The SHA-256 is computed on bytes as they arrive (cloud_http.c:863), not on the file written. For a .mcd, mcCardBackupNoEcc(download, stage) (1062) then writes an 8 MB copy and reads source and copy back (mc_card_export.c:315-337, each 64 KB chunk reopening the file), which only proves stage equals download; a bad write of the download is never caught. The .psu path (1166) already publishes its download by rename and has the same on-disk gap.
findings.fix: After the download, hash the written file with hash_local_file (move it above the recovery functions or forward-declare it) and compare it with snapshot->sha256 (and version->sha256 for .psu). For .mcd rename download to result directly, as cloudGoogleRecoverSaveVersion does; keep mcCardImportPcsx2 only for .ps2. Update tests/test_cloud_recovery.py: the source assertions at 58-59 and the harness stubs and counts that assume a .mcd.PART stage (111-112, 129-131, 186), adding a hash_local_file stub.
findings.justification: The added hash read replaces the .mcd copy-and-compare, so it is less I/O, and it verifies the bytes that are actually published instead of only stage==download.
findings.benefit: Per .mcd recovery: 8 MB write and 16 MB read less and ~512 fewer open/close calls (INFERRED: 8 MB / 64 KB = 128 chunks x 2 files x 2 passes); published file checked against Drive's digest. About 0 net lines.
findings.evidence: Read cloudGoogleRecoverSnapshot 982-1090, cloudGoogleRecoverSaveVersion 1092-1182, download_write cloud_http.c:840-869 (digest updated from the data pointer after genWrite), mcCardBackupNoEccImpl mc_card_export.c:298-351 and read_exact_at/write_exact_at 87-130 (open, seek, read/write, close per call; MC_EXPORT_IN = 64 KB at line 17). mcCardValidateNoEcc (218-222) only checks the 64-byte header and file size. tests/test_cloud_recovery.py:58-59 assert the current stage flow.

findings.title: cloudGoogleSyncBackupRoot fetches the Drive access token once and never refreshes it; a sync longer than the token lifetime aborts with HTTP 401
findings.problem: The access token is obtained once (1626) and its expires_in is ignored (389-400); every later Drive call reuses it. Google access tokens last about one hour, and the first 401 makes drive_find_child fail (739-743), which aborts the whole recursive sync (1518-1524, 1563-1567). A first sync of a large history reads each 8 MB image twice (hash at 1302, upload at cloud_http.c:805-815) plus TLS work, so it can pass the one-hour mark.
findings.fix: Remember Timer() when refresh_access_token succeeds and, at the top of each sync_tree entry, call refresh_access_token again when the token is older than about 50 minutes.
findings.justification: Without it a big first sync cannot finish in one run and fails after an hour of work with an opaque 'Drive list returned HTTP 401'. A timestamp check is about 5 lines, needs no retry logic, and touches only the long-running sync.
findings.benefit: Large first syncs complete in one run (INFERRED: at ~1 MB/s USB reads, two reads per 8 MB image is ~16 s, so roughly 225 images per hour before the token expires).
findings.evidence: Grep refresh_access_token over src/: called only at 858, 1026, 1134, 1626 (once per top-level operation). Grep '401' and 'expires_in' over src/: no 401 handling anywhere; expires_in is read only for the device code (611). sync_tree 1485-1579 has no token handling. Throughput figures are estimates, not measured.

findings.title: Optional git-ref argv mode in test_copy_short_io.py and test_cursor_sound_ticks.py that CI never uses
findings.problem: These tests read sources through 'git show <argv[1]>:path' when given an argument, so that the checks can run against an older revision. Only the tests' own docstrings document this (test_cursor_sound_ticks.py:8, test_launch_driver_messages.py:10). compile.yml runs all three with no argument (lines 67, 228, 227). In test_copy_short_io.py the mode also silently skips the seek checks at 95-98.
findings.fix: Delete the argv branch and read the working-tree file directly; git worktree or checkout already gives the same bisect ability.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines removed across three files and one less code path per test (MEASURED from ranges).
findings.evidence: Grep "git', 'show'|\"git\", \"show\"" in tests/: argv mode in test_copy_short_io:13, test_cursor_sound_ticks:22, test_launch_driver_messages:23 (plus test_device_input, test_home_focus, test_modal_animation, test_settings_save_prompt outside this unit). compile.yml lines 67, 227, 228 pass no argument. Grep for documented ref use in md/yml/html/sh/ps1: only USB-STABILITY-AUDIT-2026-10-08.md:95 (test_device_input).

findings.title: Asserts that long-removed helper names stay absent (test_copy_pipeline.py, test_copy_short_io.py)
findings.problem: test_copy_pipeline.py checks that copyPrepareTarget, copyLookupPath, copyVerifyTarget, copyPublishTarget, copyOpenTarget and three strings are not in filer_copy.c; test_copy_short_io.py checks the same for copyReadChunk/copyWriteChunk. findings.title: Drive history paging rejects page tokens over 240 characters although next_page_token keeps 255, and longer tokens are truncated silently
findings.problem: json_string stores nextPageToken into a 256-byte field (913-914, cloud_google.h:56) and truncates longer values without telling the caller. dash_tools passes it back (1273), and the request then refuses any token longer than 240 characters (892-895). A token of 241 characters or more shows 'Next page', but that page always fails with 'Invalid cloud-history pagination token'. Folders with more than 12 entries are affected. Whether Google issues tokens this long was not verified.
findings.fix: Delete the 240-character check at 892-895: append_url already bounds the URL, and the 2304-byte path has room (base path at most ~352 bytes + 11 + 3 x 255 = 1128). If Google tokens can be longer than 255, enlarge next_page_token and dash_tools' token[256] together.
findings.benefit: Paging works for every token that fits the buffer; 4 lines removed (INFERRED path arithmetic from the format string at 884-887 and drive_safe_id ids < 192 chars).
findings.evidence: Read cloudGoogleListBackupHistory 839-917, json_string 61-107 (copies at most out_size-1 and returns 1), include/cloud_google.h:54-59, dash_tools.c cloudBrowseHistory 1191-1355 (token[256] at 1194, copied from page->next_page_token at 1273). Path arithmetic: fixed format text 115 chars + encoded query <= 237 (id is alnum/-/_ only, 7 encoded fixed chars). Real Google token length is the unverified part.

findings.title: loadIcon is never called: TexIcon, FOLDER/WARNING and the whole of src/icon.c are dead with it

The FOLDER/WARNING index macros (launchelf.h:466-467) are used nowhere. loadIcon would also free() static arrays if it ever ran.

findings.benefit: ~2085 source lines removed (2055 of them a byte table). MEASURED: linker already discards .text.loadIcon (308 B) and icon.o .data (2048 B); TexIcon 80 B .bss stays in the shipped ELF (no -fdata-sections) and goes away.

findings.title: Eight static int[MAX_ENTRY] scratch arrays (64 KB .bss) where one shared array is enough

findings.fix: Replace the eight function-local static arrays with one file-scope static int[MAX_ENTRY] used by targets() callers; in case F_IMPORT_SAVES reuse it instead of declaring another sv_idx.

findings.title: get_CNF_string loops forever on a byte >= 0x80 at a line start or inside a comment line (UTF-8 BOM, non-ASCII comment): boot hang
findings.problem: With signed char, a byte >= 0x80 fails both '*tp > 0' tests: the skip loop at 118 stops on it, line 123 sends it to the comment branch, and the comment loop at 125 stops on it without advancing, so 'goto start_line' repeats forever. A LAUNCHSTATION.CNF saved by a PC editor with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) or with an accented character in a '#'/';' comment hangs loadConfig, which main_boot.c:64 runs at every boot before the UI exists. readSystemCnf parses disc SYSTEM.CNF with the same function.
findings.fix: In the comment-skip loop at line 125 test '*tp != 0' instead of '*tp > 0' so the rest of the line is skipped; a high byte at a line start then goes through the comment branch and is skipped too. No other line needs to change.
findings.benefit: Removes a boot-time infinite loop triggered by an ordinary PC-edited config file; one-token change (INFERRED: signed char is the MIPS ABI default, no -funsigned-char in ps2.yaml)
findings.evidence: Read config.c:111-159 and traced the loop for *tp == (char)0xEF: 118 exits (0xEF > 0 false), 120 not NUL, 123 true (< 'A'), 125 exits at once, goto 117. Callers via Grep get_CNF_string: config.c:950 (loadConfig) and main_startup.c:180 (readSystemCnf, called from main_actions.c:621). loadConfig callers: main_boot.c:64 and :69 only, inside performEarlyBootInitialization. ps2.yaml:631-634 cflags for the wLaunchELF target are -G0 and assembler includes only, no -funsigned-char; char signedness itself is the EE MIPS ABI default and was not measured (hence INFERRED). The app's own writer (configBuildSaveText) only emits ASCII key names at line starts and '# SMB shares' (smb_shares.h:26), so the trigger is an externally edited or copied file.

findings.title: wle_igr hdd_target_path reloads dev9/bdm/bdmfs/ata_bd/ps2hdd/ps2fs on every one of its 24 retries
findings.problem: For an hdd0:/hdd1: target, resolve_app_path calls hdd_target_path on each of up to 24 attempts and every call SifExecModuleBuffer's the whole HDD driver set again. ps2hdd_osd re-runs DelDrv/AddDrv and returns RESIDENT_END each time (hdd.c:359-378), so every retry leaves another resident ps2hdd. A second ata_bd registers DEV9 interrupt, DMA and power-off callbacks and calls sceAtaInit (bdm_connect_bd) before RegisterLibraryEntries fails and it exits NO_RESIDENT_END, so its freed image stays wired into dev9 and bdm. Trigger: a configured HDD path whose partition or ELF is missing, or a mount that fails once.
findings.fix: Load the HDD driver set once: move the six module loads out of hdd_target_path into main's prefix chain (extend the existing ata branch to hdd0:/hdd1: and start ps2hdd/ps2fs there), so the retry loop only splits the path and mounts pfs0:. bdmfs_fatfs is not needed for a PFS target and can be left out of that branch.
findings.benefit: Fixes repeated driver loads in the IGR path: up to 23 extra resident ps2hdd copies (27,549-byte IRX each, BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:174, plus cache) and dangling DEV9/bdm callbacks from freed ata_bd images, likely an IOP hang instead of the ExecOSD fallback (INFERRED). Net 0 lines.
findings.evidence: Read wle_igr.c:98-171: module loads at 122-134 sit inside hdd_target_path, which resolve_app_path calls in its retry loop (151-154, WLE_IGR_TRIES=24 at :63, usleep at :167). main's prefix chain (228-255) has no hdd branch. Read iop/ps2hdd_osd/hdd.c:303-378 (DelDrv/AddDrv, MODULE_RESIDENT_END) and iop/ata_bd/src/ps2atad.c:263-387 (SpdRegisterIntrHandler, dev9RegisterPre/PostDmaCb, Dev9RegisterPowerOffHandler and sceAtaInit before RegisterLibraryEntries at 378) plus sceAtaInit caching init in the first instance (1388-1396), so a reload cannot rediscover a late drive. ps2.yaml:466-483 embeds these modules in wle_igr. INFERRED: loadcore frees a NO_RESIDENT_END module image, dev9 keeps the last registered callback pointer, SDK dev9/bdm/fs reload behaviour.

findings.title: HDL info RPC stays 'ready' across IOP resets and after a failed load: HDD manager calls SifCallRpc on a stale or unbound client
findings.problem: Hdl_Inited (hdl_rpc.c:24,48) is set once and never cleared: clearIopModuleState only clears have_hdl_info (init.c:2998). After any IOP reset (stack switch MMCE/MX4SIO/UDPFS, mc1 with MX4SIO, DEV9 family change), dash_hdd hdlReady returns 1 without reloading hdl_info.irx and HdlGetGameInfo/HdlRenameGame issue blocking SifCallRpc through a client bound to the previous IOP session. Also loadHdlInfoModule ignores ID/ret and the bind result; when the module did not start, Hdl_Info_BindRpc spins 0x1000 binds x 0x10000 nop loops and still sets Hdl_Inited=1, so the call goes to a NULL server.
findings.fix: Clear Hdl_Inited in clearIopModuleState next to have_hdl_info; in loadHdlInfoModule skip the bind when ID < 0 or ret == 1; in Hdl_Info_BindRpc set Hdl_Inited only when client.server != 0; key dash_hdd's one-shot 'tried' to getIopResetGeneration() so the module is reloaded once per IOP session.
findings.justification: The checks replace an unconditional 'ready' latch that lets a blocking RPC reach a dead or absent IOP server (console freeze, INFERRED). Each is one condition on existing state; no new mechanism is added.
findings.benefit: Removes a likely hard freeze when the HDD manager is reopened after any IOP reset, and a ~3-5 s UI-thread spin when hdl_info fails (INFERRED: 2^28 loop iterations of 4 nops at 294.9 MHz plus 4096 bind round trips).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:2563-2574, 2965-3040; hdl_rpc.c:1-84; dash_hdd.c:419-449. grep Hdl_Inited over src: only hdl_rpc.c:24 (def), :48 (set), :57/:74 (checks), dash_hdd.c:419/425/436; nothing clears it. grep have_hdl_info: init.c:182, 2567, 2572, 2998 only. Callers: loadHdlInfoModule only from dash_hdd.c:434; HdlGetGameInfo dash_hdd.c:448 (UI), HdlRenameGame dash_hdd.c:281 (worker job). hdl_info imports atad/dev9/PoweroffShutdown (iop/hdl_info/imports.lst:2-47), so a missing dependency makes the load fail. INFERRED part: IOP sifrpc behaviour when the call carries a stale or NULL server pointer (SDK source not in repo).

findings.title: dash_sound.c keeps full EE copies of BGM.ADP and custom effects for the whole run only as audsrv sample IDs
findings.problem: After audsrv_load_adpcm has sent the sample to the IOP/SPU2, bgm_data (size+64 bytes) and each accepted custom_data[i] stay allocated until shutdown; the file's own comments (lines 40, 54) say audsrv only uses the buffer address as the sample ID. The copy is never reused either: dashSoundShutdown (296-301), run before every IOP reset (init.c:2193), frees it and dashBgmStart reads the file again. The shipped kit always installs BGM.ADP (scripts/package_apps.py:37,44), so every boot with music on holds it.
findings.fix: After a successful audsrv_load_adpcm, shrink the buffer in place to a few bytes (realloc to 16 bytes; newlib shrinks without moving) so the address stays allocated and unique as the ID and the rest returns to the heap. Do the same for each accepted custom effect in uploadSamples. Do not free the buffers outright: a reused address would collide with a live sample ID.
findings.justification: Two realloc calls (about 4 lines) release memory that has no use after upload: 284,720 bytes for the shipped music on every boot, and up to 1 MB + 2 MB with user files. Nothing else holds or reads these buffers.
findings.benefit: 284,720 B EE heap for the shipped BGM.ADP (MEASURED: res/music.sad 284,656 B in inventory, +64 pad from line 429); up to 1 MB + 8 x 256 KB with user sidecars (INFERRED from BGM_MAX_BYTES and SFX_MAX_BYTES). Rank 4, not 5, because the fix relies on INFERRED audsrv/newlib behaviour.
findings.evidence: Read dash_sound.c fully: bgm_data set at 471 and freed only at 247-248 (reload) and 299-300 (shutdown); custom_data kept at 148-149, freed at 110-118. init.c:2189-2193 calls dashSoundShutdown before every IOP reset, then dashSoundMaintain (dash_main.c:1484) re-inits and dashBgmStart re-reads (bgm_loaded=0). inventory/Launchstation.tsv:608 res/music.sad 284656 bytes; package_apps.py:37,44 ships it as BGM.ADP. INFERRED, not verifiable in the clone: audsrv_load_adpcm DMA-copies the buffer once and later calls pass only adpcm->buffer as an ID (as the file's comments at 40 and 54 state); newlib realloc shrinks in place.

findings.title: DashApp is 828 bytes and dashApps reserves DASH_MAX_APPS (512) of them for the whole run, plus a second full array per scan
findings.problem: dashLibInit mallocs sizeof(DashApp) * DASH_MAX_APPS once and keeps it, whatever the library size; every scan mallocs a second full-size fresh array and then memcpy's it into the first. A library of 50 apps uses about 41 KB of the 414 KB that stays reserved.
findings.fix: Size the array to the library: allocate for the loaded count plus a small headroom, and let dashLibApplyScan adopt the scan's fresh array shrunk with realloc instead of copying it into a second permanent buffer. dash_main.c:718-719 rebuilds the Apps and Home views right after the apply; check first which dialogs hold DashApp pointers across a scan (dash_lib.c:764-765).
findings.justification: Adds a realloc and a capacity check in the cache loader. The concrete problem is about 0.4 MB of EE RAM held for the whole session for empty slots; the change is a few lines and no new layer.
findings.benefit: sizeof(DashApp) = 256+64+160+40+24+24+256+1+1+2 = 828 B; 828 x 512 = 423,936 B reserved permanently. With 50 apps about 380 KB of EE RAM is returned (INFERRED; depends on library size). Scan peak also drops by the same amount.
findings.evidence: Read dash_internal.h:34-39 (DASH_PATH_MAX 256, DASH_TITLE_MAX 64, DASH_DESC_MAX 160, DASH_SHORT_MAX 40, DASH_MAX_APPS 512) and 690-702 (DashApp fields). grep DASH_MAX_APPS|sizeof(DashApp) over src: dash_lib.c:496 permanent malloc, :555 cache loader appends up to the cap, :889 scan fresh array, :928 memcpy into dashApps, dash_main.c:715-719 apply then rebuild views. The stated pointer-stability rule is at dash_lib.c:764-765. Saving depends on the user's app count (INFERRED).
