findings.title: tex_drawChar builds each glyph through a 16x32 temp image with run detection; it compiles to 10.5 KB
findings.problem: tex_drawChar zeroes a 16x32 u16 temp array, finds vertical runs of set font bits, sets every other pixel, ORs the gaps in by rows then by columns, and copies the whole block out. The result is a 2x2 pixel block for every set font bit. The measured function size is 10548 bytes (loops unrolled). The colour parameter is never used (always 0xFFFF), and tex_printXY's return value is never read ('not needed for anything').
findings.fix: Replace the body with a double loop over the 8x16 font bits that writes a 2x2 block of 0xFFFF straight into tex_buffer for each set bit; the buffer is already zeroed in make_icon. Drop the unused colour parameter and make tex_drawChar/tex_printXY static and void.
findings.benefit: ~40 lines removed; tex_drawChar is 10548 B of .text (MEASURED, sizes/wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv); a direct 2x2 write is well under 1 KB, so about 9-10 KB of ELF saved (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read makeicon.c:110-226: temp_image[2i][2j] set per set bit (133,140), row OR (146-148) and column OR (151-153) give 2x2 blocks; tex_buffer is memset 0 at 338 and characters step by 16 px / 32 rows (169, 182-184), so writing only set pixels is equivalent except for '\v'/'\t' overlaps, which folder names do not contain (callers filer_browser.c:1497, 2455). colour is only passed along at 199/212/220. Size from evidence/Launchstation/raw/sizes/wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv: '10548 FUNC GLOBAL .text tex_drawChar'. The size of the rewrite is INFERRED.

findings.title: prepareExploitSignerIop reboots the IOP without the teardown resetRuntimeDeviceState requires (FTP close, PAD close, mc poll drain, sound)
findings.problem: The exploit installer's signer reboot (init.c:838-874) only stops SMB/PCCF, closes the keyboard and unmounts. It skips what the file's own reset path documents as required: ftpSessionShutdown refusal (2172-2177; an FTP upload to the card is cut by the reboot), filerRootMcPollIdle (2182-2186; pending mcGetInfo leaves the pad dark), padPortClose/padEnd before setupPad (2197-2205; 'UI alive, controller dead'), dashSoundShutdown (2189-2193). The installer then needs pad input and writes to the card.
findings.fix: Run the signer reboot through the same path as every other reset: let Reset() take an optional IOPRP buffer (NULL = SifIopReset) and have prepareExploitSignerIop call resetRuntimeDeviceState with it, then check have_exploit_signer_iop/generation for a refused reset. This deletes the duplicated reboot/reload sequence at 845-874.
findings.benefit: Closes a card-corruption window (FTP write cut mid-file) and an intermittent dead-controller state after the signer reboot; ~25 duplicated reset lines removed (INFERRED from 845-874 vs 3053-3093).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:821-882, 2163-2221, 3048-3098; main_exploit_installer.c:1053-1057 and call sites 1963, 2289 (install flows that then write the card and show dialogs). ftp_session.c:70-83 ftpSessionShutdown closes FTP sessions before a reset; prepareExploitSignerIop never calls it (grep ftpSession in main_exploit_installer.c: none). dash_worker.c:153-164 iopResetHook is a no-op on the UI thread, so the missing iopResetNotify is harmless. pad.c:428-452 reopenPadPorts documents the stale-libpad failure. INFERRED part: that the stale pad and pending libmc request actually fail on this specific reboot (intermittent per the repo's own comments).

findings.title: copy() allocates a second 1 MiB buffer (buff2) that never overlaps any I/O
findings.problem: For a file of at least 1 MiB on the fast-device path, copy() allocates buff2 (another COPY_BUFFER_FAST_DEFAULT, 1 MiB) and alternates the two buffers per chunk. Each chunk is one read and then one write of the same buffer (copyChunkIo, filer_copy.c:67-76), and DashFileTransferChunk waits until the worker job is done (dash_ui.c:1463-1464) or the chunk runs inline (line 1563). No read ever overlaps a write, so the second buffer only doubles the peak heap.
findings.fix: Delete buff2, buffCount, buffIndex and copyBuff, and pass buff to the chunk.
findings.benefit: 1 MiB less peak heap during every fast-path copy of a file >= 1 MiB (0x100000, filer_copy.c:32; INFERRED); about 14 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:58-83 (copyChunkIo reads into c->buf, then writes the same c->buf), 1398-1436, 1557-1565, 1588-1592, 1696-1700; dash_ui.c:1452-1466 (dashWorkerSubmit, then while (!dashWorkerDone(id)) loadingDraw()). Grep for buff2 over src/Launchstation/src and include: only filer_copy.c. buffSize equals COPY_BUFFER_FAST_DEFAULT only when copyBufferSize (filer_copy.c:90-117) picks the 1 MiB default and the file is at least that large (hdd, smb, udpfs, mmce, ata, ilink, cdfs sources and destinations); a PSU restore can also reach it through psu_restore_buff.

findings.title: fbSortFiles insertion-sorts 388-byte FILEINFO structs on the UI thread: O(n^2) for folders up to 2048 entries
findings.problem: listDone (a worker completion callback, run on the UI thread by dashWorkerPump -> finish, dash_worker.c:221-229) sorts the whole listing with an insertion sort that moves whole FILEINFO structs (char[256] + title[66] + 64-byte sceMcTblGetDir, about 388 B). Average cost is n*n/4 moves: at the MAX_ENTRY cap of 2048 that is about 1.05 M struct copies (about 400 MB of memory traffic) plus as many fbCompare calls (Type sort, the default, runs several extension compares per call), all before the next frame. Large USB/HDD folders therefore stall the UI when opened, refreshed or re-sorted.
findings.fix: Replace the body of fbSortFiles with a qsort call (qsort is already linked: dash_card_tool.c:1766, dash_lib.c:599, dash_widgets.c:950) through a two-line wrapper that calls fbCompare. fbCompare already ends in a name tiebreak, so the order is unchanged except for names that differ only in case. Add #include <stdlib.h> to the host harness string in tests/test_browser_sort.py, which compiles the extracted function with -Werror.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: worst case drops from ~1.05 M moves of 388 B to ~n*log2(n) = ~22.5 k swaps at n=2048; ~0.1-0.25 s per open at n=500 and multi-second stalls near the cap go away. ~8 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c:220-278 (fbCompare, fbSortFiles) and 358-398 (listDone calls fbSortFiles when fb_sort != FB_SORT_STORED). dash_worker.c:1-22 and 221-258: completion callbacks run on the UI thread. FILEINFO layout read at include/launchelf.h:560-565; MAX_ENTRY = 2048 at launchelf.h:205; size of sceMcTblGetDir (64 B) and padding are INFERRED. grep qsort over src: used in dash_card_tool.c, dash_hdd.c, dash_lib.c, dash_widgets.c. tests/test_browser_sort.py extracts fbSortFiles by signature and includes only assert/stdint/stdio/string. Timing figures are INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: Power-button handler is lost when load_ps2dev9 reboots the IOP after the caller armed it, and is never armed in USB-only sessions
findings.problem: Each DEV9 loader calls setupPowerOff() and then reaches load_ps2dev9, which reboots the IOP when the Legacy Ethernet setting was toggled (dash_settings.c:1905 changes it live). Reset clears have_poweroff and done_setupPowerOff (3001, 3024) and nothing re-arms them, so the new HDD/ATA/network stack runs without poweroff.irx: a power-button press skips PFS CLOSEALL, HDD idle and DEV9 off. USB, MMCE, MX4SIO and iLink loaders never call setupPowerOff, so the USB STOP UNIT at 2614-2615 never runs from the button in those sessions.
findings.fix: Call setupPowerOff() once inside load_ps2dev9 after the variant-switch reset and before DEV9 is executed, and delete the seven caller calls at 921, 967, 1024, 2551, 2677, 2701, 2723 (all reach load_ps2dev9). Add the same single call in loadUsbModules if USB HDD STOP UNIT on the button is wanted.
findings.justification: Moving the call to the one place every DEV9 path passes after any reset fixes the ordering bug and removes six call sites; the optional USB call is one line for the documented emergency-park problem.
findings.benefit: Power-button shutdown again flushes HDD/PFS after a DEV9 family switch and stops USB disks; ~6 call lines removed (READ: 7 removed, 1 added).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:487-523, 908-990, 1010-1054, 2531-2558, 2637-2734, 2965-3098, 1740-1817. grep setupPowerOff() over src: init.c 921, 967, 1024, 2493, 2551, 2677, 2701, 2723 and main_actions.c:759 (explicit menu) only; no call in Reset, ensureCoreIoStackReady, loadUsbModules, boot code. grep legacy_net_drivers: set live at dash_settings.c:1905 with no reset; read at init.c:496 and 951. INFERRED part: what the console does on a power-button press when poweroff.irx is not resident (no callback, so closeAllAndPoweroff does not run).

findings.title: dash_browser.o keeps ~88 KB of one-shot scratch in .bss: eight static int[2048] index arrays and two 16 KB compare buffers
findings.problem: Each of opCopy, opExtractPsuTo, opImportSavesTo, opDelete, opSize and actionsMenu (three: sv_idx, psu_idx and a second sv_idx that shadows the first inside case F_IMPORT_SAVES) has its own static int[MAX_ENTRY] for targets(); all run on the UI thread one after another and never hold two of them live at once. activeHistoryFilesEqual adds two static 16 KB buffers used only by the rare active-card dedupe. Together 96 KB of the object's 104 KB .bss, reserved for the whole run.
findings.fix: Use one file-scope static int index array for every targets()/psuTargets()/saveFileTargets()/ps1SaveTargets() caller and delete the eight local statics (this also removes the shadowed sv_idx). In activeHistoryFilesEqual malloc one 32 KB block for the two halves at entry and free it at done.
findings.justification: The malloc needs one NULL check (returning -1, which callers already treat as 'could not compare'); it replaces 32 KB of permanent .bss used only by one rarely chosen menu action.
findings.benefit: MEASURED map: 8 x 0x2000 + 2 x 0x4000 = 96 KB; sharing saves 7 x 8192 = 56 KB and malloc saves 32 KB -> 88 KB .bss (of 106560 B). Rated 3 not 4: RAM headroom only, the browser already mallocs ~1.5 MB per listing.
findings.evidence: evidence/Launchstation/raw/link-raw/wLaunchELF.map:11459-11476 lists dash_browser.o .bss 0x1a040 with actionsMenu.sv_idx, actionsMenu.psu_idx, actionsMenu.sv_idx.228, opCopy.idx, opExtractPsuTo.idx, opImportSavesTo.idx, opDelete.idx, opSize.idx at 0x2000 each and activeHistoryFilesEqual.buf_a/buf_b at 0x4000 each; link/wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv gives .bss 106560 for dash_browser.o. extra-warnings-syntax-only.raw.log:1421-1422 reports the -Wshadow at 3045 vs 2698. Read every use: arrays are filled by targets()-style helpers and read only inside the same function; actionsMenu uses its arrays only for counts before the switch dispatches to the op functions.

findings.title: dash_info.c keeps four separate static 6.3 KB Sheet buffers (one per info screen)
findings.problem: dashShowTextLines, dashShowAbout, dashShowBuildInfo and dashShowSystemInfo each declare their own static Sheet (48 lines x 132 B + count = 6340 B), so 25,360 B of .bss is reserved although only one modal sheet can be on screen at a time. dashShowSystemInfo also keeps a static SysInfo copy of cached_console_info that it only reads.
findings.fix: Use one file-scope static Sheet for all four functions (each already resets s.n = 0 before filling it) and read cached_console_info directly instead of copying it into the static job.
findings.benefit: 19,020 B of .bss (MEASURED: wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv lists dashShowTextLines.s, dashShowAbout.s, dashShowBuildInfo.s, dashShowSystemInfo.s at 6340 B each; 3 x 6340 saved) plus 92 B for dashShowSystemInfo.job.
findings.evidence: Read dash_info.c in full: Sheet typedef 22-34, statics at 129, 147, 220, 347 (+ job 348). Sizes MEASURED in evidence/Launchstation/raw/sizes/wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv lines 129-132 (6340 each) and 3448 (job 92). No nesting: callers are top-level menu actions dash_main.c:479/483/487, dash_settings.c:3352, dash_files.c:566 and the exploit installer UI callback dash_exploit.c:119-125 (not a worker completion); sheetShow (54-124) only renders and polls input, it never opens another sheet.

findings.title: Hdl_Inited survives IOP reboots, so HdlGetGameInfo can call a stale hdl_info RPC client
findings.problem: clearIopModuleState (called by Reset, init.c:3066) clears have_hdl_info (init.c:2998) but nothing clears hdl_rpc.c's Hdl_Inited. After the HDD manager has loaded hdl_info once, any IOP reboot (stack switch, rebootIopAndReloadCoreStack) leaves Hdl_Inited=1, so dash_hdd.c hdlReady returns 1 without reloading the module and loadGameInfo calls HdlGetGameInfo -> SifCallRpc on a client bound to a server that no longer exists. Hdl_Info_BindRpc also sets Hdl_Inited=1 when its retry loop times out, and init.c:2571 ignores the result. Three flags (have_hdl_info, Hdl_Inited, the static 'tried' in hdlReady) track one state.
findings.fix: Make one flag the truth: set Hdl_Inited only when client.server != 0, clear it in clearIopModuleState next to have_hdl_info (or drop Hdl_Inited and let loadHdlInfoModule return the bind result), and delete the static 'tried' in hdlReady since loadHdlInfoModule is already idempotent through have_hdl_info.
findings.justification: Adds one reset line (or a return value); it fixes a reachable stale-RPC call after an IOP reboot and removes the redundant 'tried' flag, so the line count stays about even.
findings.benefit: Removes a possible EE hang or IOP crash on HDD manager use after an IOP reboot (consequence of calling a dead RPC server is INFERRED); ~4 lines net removed.
findings.evidence: Read hdl_rpc.c:24-83, init.c:2563-2574 (loadHdlInfoModule ignores Hdl_Info_BindRpc ret), init.c:2965-3004 clearIopModuleState sets have_hdl_info=0 only, Reset init.c:3048-3066 calls it. Grep Hdl_Inited over src: hdl_rpc.c:24,48,57,74 and dash_hdd.c:419,425,436 only; no reset. dash_hdd.c:421-449 hdlReady/loadGameInfo. The hang/crash on SifCallRpc to a vanished server is INFERRED, not tested on hardware.

findings.title: hdd_header_copy_buffer keeps 32 KB of .bss for a rare header-injection copy while a 2 MB heap buffer was just freed
findings.problem: The static 32768-byte copy buffer is used only by hddHeaderCopyOptionalPfsFile during InjectHddPartitionHeaderFromSource. That function memaligns the 2 MB hdd_header_buffer and frees it (1150) immediately before calling hddHeaderCopyOptionalPfsFiles (1155), so the 32 KB stays reserved for the whole session for no reason.
findings.fix: Delete the static buffer and HDD_HEADER_COPY_BUFFER_SIZE; free hdd_header_buffer after the PFS copy instead of before it and use its first 32 KB (or all of it) as the copy buffer.
findings.benefit: 32,768 bytes of EE .bss freed (MEASURED: BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:91 lists hdd_header_injector.o .bss 33,920; the copy buffer is 32,768 of it); no extra allocation; ~2 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Grep hdd_header_copy_buffer: hdd_header_injector.c:89,1045,1054 only. Read 1103-1160: memalign 1142, free 1150, copy 1155. evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:91 .bss figure.

findings.title: Artwork results for transient Home entries mark DASHLIB.CNF dirty, causing byte-identical library cache rewrites (idle and before every launch)
findings.problem: Home resolves recents/pins/favorites that are not in the library into home_tmp[] transients that start at DASH_ART_UNKNOWN on every homeRebuild (dash_home.c:69, dash_lib.c:444-452). When their art job ends, artDone sets art_dirty on UNKNOWN->NONE or ->FOUND (dash_art.c:397,422). That schedules a full DASHLIB.CNF rewrite after 6 s idle and before each launch (dash_main.c:647-648,1488-1489), but dashLibBuildCache skips TRANSIENT entries (dash_lib.c:626-627), so the file written is byte-identical. Transients without art have no slot, so every Home rebuild re-probes them and repeats the write.
findings.fix: In artDone, set art_dirty only when the app is not DASH_APP_TRANSIENT (the two assignments at dash_art.c:397 and :422).
findings.justification: Adds one flag test to two existing conditions. It removes a whole-file memory-card rewrite of an unchanged file per Home rebuild and from the launch path; no simpler change stops it because the dirty flag is the only trigger.
findings.benefit: One redundant DASHLIB.CNF write (whole library text, roughly 10-30 KB for 100 apps, INFERRED) avoided per Home rebuild with an art-less transient and before such launches; less worker time and card wear.
findings.evidence: Read dash_art.c:380-427 (art_dirty at 397/422), dash_home.c:60-113 (homeAdd -> dashLibResolve(path,&home_tmp[n])), dash_lib.c:444-482 (MakeTransient memset, UNKNOWN, TRANSIENT flag), dash_lib.c:612-640 (cache skips TRANSIENT), dash_store.c:659-724 (SaveCache only sets dirty; submitSave writes whole file, no content compare), dash_main.c:646-648 and 1486-1490. Grep dashArtTakeDirty: only dash_main.c:647 and :1488. Grep dashHomeRebuild callers: dash_apps.c:91,459, dash_main.c:719, dash_settings.c (6 sites). File size and store-on-card are INFERRED (store dir is beside the config or mc0:/SYS-CONF/, dash_store.c header).

findings.title: Classic editor leaks the whole text buffer on every inserted character: free() is swallowed into a comment
findings.problem: In both insert paths the line that should free the old buffer reads as one comment ('//memset(...); // 256 ...  free(TextBuffer[Active_Window]);'), so the next line overwrites TextBuffer[Active_Window] with a new malloc and the old block (TextSize+ins1+256 bytes) is lost on every typed char, Return, Tab or Paste. Typing 100 characters into a 100 KB file leaks ~10 MB; when malloc then returns NULL, strcpy at :374/:649 writes through NULL. The delete path (:387, :664) shows the intended separate free().
findings.fix: Put free(TextBuffer[Active_Window]) back on its own line in both places (or, simpler, realloc the buffer once instead of the TMP copy dance); if the classic editor is deleted (finding 1) this goes with it.
findings.benefit: Fixes an unbounded heap leak per keystroke in the classic editor (INFERRED arithmetic: TextSize+ins1+256 bytes per insert).
findings.evidence: Read editor_input.c:369-375 and 644-650: line 372 and 647 each contain the memset comment followed on the same line by the free() call, all after '//'. Line 373/648 assigns a fresh malloc to TextBuffer[Active_Window] without freeing. Compare delete case :386-389 / :663-666 where memset comment and free() are separate lines. Reachability of the classic editor: see finding 1 (main_actions.c:231,771, filer_browser.c:1554).

findings.title: HDD Manager reports 0 MB on drives over 1 TiB (2 TB HDDs): HDIOC_TOTALSECTOR read as signed int
findings.problem: scanRun stores HDIOC_TOTALSECTOR in an int and uses it only when > 0. The driver returns the u32 totalLBA through an int (iop/ps2hdd_osd/hdd_fio.c:1055,1087), so any drive above 2^31 sectors (1.5/2 TB, the APA maximum) comes back negative and size_mb becomes 0. Then free_mb is 0, Create says 'HDD full', the create-missing header path gets max 0 so pickSize returns -1, and the usage bar is hidden (hddScene needs size_mb > 0).
findings.fix: Read the value as u32, as libhdd already does (ee_libs/hdd/libhdd.c:269): u32 sectors = (u32)fileXioDevctl(...); size_mb = sectors / SECTORS_PER_MB. present/formatted are already checked before this line, so the error case is not reached.
findings.benefit: Partition creation and usage display work on 1.5-2 TB HDDs (common for HDL collections); one-line change, no size change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read dash_hdd.c:158-161 (int sectors, sectors > 0 test), 348-351 recomputeFree, 621-625 actCreate max_mb < 128 -> HDD full, 881 injectMatching pickSize max = free_mb, 505-506 pickSize returns -1 when max < min, 1213 usage needs size_mb > 0. iop/ps2hdd_osd/hdd_fio.c:1055 int rv, 1086-1088 rv = totalLBA; libapa.h:211 u32 totalLBA; hdd_blkio.c:119,259 totalLBA from sectorCount. libhdd.c:269 casts the same devctl to u32. grep HDIOC_TOTALSECTOR over the repo: only libhdd.c:269 and dash_hdd.c:159.

findings.title: Rename game fails for HDL titles longer than 39 characters: old title truncated into HddJob.a[40]
findings.problem: actRenameGame copies p->game.Name (up to 64 characters, include/hdl_rpc.h:12) into j->a, which is MAX_PART_NAME + 8 = 40 bytes, so dashStrCopy keeps 39 characters. The IOP looks the game up with strcmp(OldName, game->name) on the full title (iop/hdl_info/hdd.c:178), finds nothing and returns -3, and the user gets 'Game not renamed' for every title of 40+ characters.
findings.fix: Size HddJob.a for the longest string it carries (64 + 1, the HDL title limit, iop/hdl_info/hdl.h:4) instead of MAX_PART_NAME + 8.
findings.benefit: Fixes a functional bug in Rename game; +24 bytes per malloc'd HddJob, no ELF change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: dash_hdd.c:126 char a[MAX_PART_NAME + 8]; launchelf.h:202 MAX_PART_NAME = 32; dash_hdd.c:716 dashStrCopy(j->a, p->game.Name, sizeof(j->a)); dash_store.c:48-50 copies at most dst_size-1. hddJobRun 280-281 passes j->a as OldName to HdlRenameGame; src/hdl_rpc.c:69-82 strcpy into OldName[64]; iop/hdl_info/hdd.c:159-189 renames only on strcmp(Packet->OldName, game->name)==0, else -3; hdl.h:4,9 name[64+1]. The other users of j->a (partition names <= 32) are unaffected by a larger buffer.

findings.title: SMB/NFS editor passes sizeof(buf) as dashModalKeyboard max_len: 1-byte stack overwrite, and edit[96] truncates the 127-char share path
findings.problem: dashModalKeyboard's max_len is a string length: kbInsert (dash_widgets.c:345) inserts while strlen < max_len, so the result can hold max_len chars plus the NUL. smbedEditField (693), the port field (3380-3381) and NFS uid/gid (3411) pass sizeof(buf), so a full-length entry writes the NUL one byte past edit[96], buf[8] or buf[12] on the stack. Other callers (3359-3360) pass sizeof-1. edit[96] is also smaller than smbed.folder[128] (398): a share/export path is cut to 95 chars at 692 though 3395 promises 127.
findings.fix: Pass sizeof(edit) - 1 and sizeof(buf) - 1 at the three dashModalKeyboard calls, and declare edit as 128 bytes (the size of smbed.folder, the largest field edited there).
findings.benefit: Closes a 1-byte stack overwrite reached by typing 8 chars in Port, 12 in UID/GID or 96 in a share field; share paths of 96-127 chars become enterable. 0 lines; +32 bytes of stack in smbedEditField (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read dash_widgets.c 341-350 (kbInsert: if len >= max_len return; else insert), 442-469 (modalKeyboard caps max_len to 255, passes it to kbUsb and kbInsert) and 653-656 (dashModalKeyboard). Read dash_settings.c 392-407 (smbed: host[80], folder[128], uid/gid[12]), 688-700, 3355-3420. Same-file caller with the length convention: 3359-3360 (sizeof(edit) - 1); also dash_editor.c:552. Reachable: SMB and ETH are default defines of the wLaunchELF target (brief: ps2.yaml:624,627); rows are on the SMB/NFS share editor pages.

findings.title: Save library and All saves re-read everything after actions that change nothing (ctLibToCard returns 1, ctSaveMenu Export returns 2)
findings.problem: ctLibToCard returns 1 ('may have changed') after copying .psu files to a card image, although it writes only to that image and its WLE-Safety/ copy, never to a library .psu. All three callers (marked-saves menu, Apply set, single-file menu) then break out and ctLibScan reopens, mallocs and fully parses every .psu again (up to 500, each up to 8.5 MB, ctLoadPsu 685-696) on the UI thread. In All saves, a single-save Export via ctSaveMenu returns 2 and the caller rescans every card image (up to 64), while the batch Export correctly returns 0 (2048-2050).
findings.fix: Return 0 from ctLibToCard (the library is unchanged, so the list and marks can stay). In dashCardAllSaves rescan only after Copy, Move or Delete, e.g. let ctSaveMenu return -1 after ctExportPsu (dashCardTool ignores the return value).
findings.benefit: Removes one full re-read of the library per copy: e.g. 100 saves x 300 KB = 30 MB at about 1 MB/s USB is about 30 s of loading screen (INFERRED). All saves: one rescan of up to 64 images per single export avoided.
findings.evidence: Read dash_card_tool.c 2465-2535 (ctLibToCard: dest is a card image picked with DASH_PICK_FILE; writes via ctPutSave; return 1 at 2534), 2644-2711 (ctLibApplySet/ctLibFileMenu return its value), 2713-2825 (loop 'read again after anything that may have changed the files'; break at 2783 and 2816 reruns ctLibScan), 2353-2459 (ctLibScan calls ctLoadPsu per file, which reads the whole file at 685-696 and mcCardSaveFromPsu copies it, mc_card_write.c:892-937). ctSaveMenu 1509-1543 returns r=2 after ctExportPsu; dashCardAllSaves 2269-2270 breaks on >=0 and 2207-2210 rescans; ctAllBatch returns 0 for export at 2048-2050. Callers on the UI thread: dash_browser.c:2985, 2991. Transfer rate is an estimate.

findings.title: Text keyboard writes one NUL past the buffer when callers pass the buffer size as max_len (classicKeyboard, three SMB/NFS settings fields)
findings.problem: kbInsert lets the text grow to max_len characters and then moves the terminator to buf[max_len], so the buffer must hold max_len+1 bytes. classicKeyboard forwards the classic keyboard() max unchanged; the classic keyboard capped text at min(max,33), so choose_custom_output_path sized name[36] for keyboard(name, 36), and from the dashboard (override installed for the whole dashboard, dash_exploit.c:159-160) typing to 36/36 writes name[36]. dash_settings.c passes sizeof(edit[96]), sizeof(buf[8]) for the SMB/NFS port and sizeof(buf[12]) for the NFS UID/GID: typing 8 port digits writes buf[8] on the stack.
findings.fix: Pass max - 1 from classicKeyboard to dashModalKeyboard, and pass sizeof(...) - 1 at dash_settings.c:693, 3381 and 3411, as every other dashModalKeyboard caller already does.
findings.benefit: Closes a reachable one-byte stack overwrite in four keyboard prompts (exploit installer output name, SMB/NFS share fields, port, UID/GID); four one-token edits, no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read kbInsert dash_widgets.c:341-350 (guard len >= max_len, memmove len-cur+1 bytes) and modalKeyboard:442-591 (no other bound; orig clamp only lowers max_len to 255). Classic keyboard gui.c:249,308 caps at i < max && i < 33; gui.c:163-164 forwards to keyboardOverride. dashClassicUiInstall(1) at dash_main.c:1358 and :353/:675; dashExploitInstaller dash_exploit.c:150-166 runs ShowExploitInstaller with it installed; main_exploit_installer.c:1539 -> choose_custom_output_path, name[36] at :962, prefilled by build_default_signed_name(name, sizeof(name)) :979, keyboard(name, 36) :981. Grep of all dashModalKeyboard/dashModalFilename callers: only dash_settings.c:693, 3380-3381, 3411 pass the full buffer size; others pass size-1 or smaller (dash_browser 1132/1151/2380/2383, dash_card_tool 2553, dash_hdd 617/680/711, dash_editor 552/1468, dash_settings 2248/3144/3359). config.c:1552 keyboard(title_tmp[72], 72) is only reached with the override off (dash_main.c:398, 456, 668).

findings.title: Listing a missing folder or empty device root waits the whole 2-3 s retry budget every time (readGENERICWithFirstOpenRetry, ATA, MX4SIO)
findings.problem: Every usb/mass (2000 ms), iLink (3000 ms) and CF (2000 ms) listing goes through readGENERICWithFirstOpenRetry, and listDir repeats the loop for ATA and MX4SIO (750 ms, 2000 ms at a root). The retry is not limited to a first open: a missing sub-folder fails Dopen on every pass, and an empty root opens but is_root forbids the early break, so both run the full budget, polling with 100 ms busy spins. Example: booted from USB without a THEMES folder, the awaited 'Looking for themes' job (dash_settings.c:2913-2922) blocks 2 s per USB theme root; the library scan's default mass:/APPS/ and mass:/BOOT/ cost 2 s each when missing.
findings.fix: Retry only on the first open of a device unit per IOP session, keyed the same way as waitUsbTargetReady (filer.c:913-944), so later listings of a missing folder or empty root return at once; replace the three 100 ms spin loops with DelayThread(100000).
findings.justification: The per-unit mask check adds about four lines but removes repeated multi-second modal stalls on common layouts (missing THEMES/APPS/BOOT folders, empty sticks); it reuses the mask pattern already in this file rather than adding a mechanism, and replacing the spins removes six lines.
findings.benefit: Up to 2 s (iLink 3 s, ATA/MX4SIO 0.75 s) per listing of a missing folder or empty root; 2-4 s off the theme list when booted from USB (INFERRED from the loop budgets).
findings.evidence: Read filer.c:345-381 (non-root: return only when Dopen succeeds, else loop until budget; root: break needs n>0), listDir 1960-1993 (mass/usb budget 2000), 2206 (ilink 3000), 2216 (cf 2000), ATA 1994-2043, MX4SIO 2069-2189. dash_themes.c:960-995 themeRoots builds <LaunchElfDir>THEMES/ and getDir()s it; called from dash_settings.c:2893 inside a job awaited with dashWorkerAwait (2911-2926). dash_lib.c:779-801 scanRun -> scanDir -> getDirComplete (704) for dash_store.c:29-33 defaults. mapMassPathToFatFsPath('mass:/APPS/') gives 'usb0:/APPS/', not a simple root. git log -S on the retry loop: from the initial import 944a2fc.

findings.title: JPEG and PNG box downscale do a 64-bit division per source pixel (software __udivdi3 on the R5900)
findings.problem: The inner loops compute dx = (u64)x * dw / sw for every source pixel. The R5900 has no 64-bit divide, so each one is a call to compiler-rt __udivdi3, which is linked into the ELF. The viewer decodes on the UI thread (dash_image.c:108-119) and art and theme images decode on the worker (dash_art.c:343, 513), so a large image (up to 2048x2048 PNG, or a JPEG after the 1/8 prescale) costs millions of library divides.
findings.fix: Step dx with an accumulator instead of dividing (add dw per pixel, advance dx when it reaches sw; dw <= sw so at most one step), or at least drop the u64 casts in these per-pixel and per-row lines: the products stay below 2^23 (x < 8192, dw <= 640), so 32-bit hardware DIVU is exact.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: about 4.2M __udivdi3 calls for a 2048x2048 PNG (roughly 50-100 cycles each, 0.7-1.4 s at 295 MHz); the accumulator removes them, which shortens the frozen viewer open and art/theme jobs. No source lines added with the cast variant.
findings.evidence: Read dash_jpeg.c:129-146 (dy per row line 130, dx per pixel line 140) and dash_png.c:155-201 (lines 156, 169, 181, 194). Bounds: DASH_PNG_MAX_DIM 2048 (dash_png.c:16); JPEG sw <= 1024 after the scale loop dash_jpeg.c:95-98 with max_w 640; callers pass DASH_VW/DASH_VH 640x448 (dash_image.c:111,115), ART_MAX_DIM 128 (dash_art.c:29,343). __udivdi3 (536 B) and __udivmoddi4 (1660 B) are in the shipped ELF (sizes tsv lines 416, 1266) and are pulled from libclang_rt.builtins-mips64el (experiment-fdata archive-members line 181), which shows the target lowers 64-bit division to a library call. The per-call cycle count is not measured and the disassembly of these objects was not inspected.

findings.title: dashApps always reserves 512 x 828 B (414 KB) of heap for the library, whatever its size
findings.problem: dashLibInit mallocs DASH_MAX_APPS (512) DashApp entries of 828 B each and keeps them for the whole session; dashLibApplyScan then memcpys the scan result (itself a full 512-entry buffer) into that array and frees the result. A typical library of a few dozen apps uses a small part of the 423,936 B block.
findings.fix: After dashLibLoadCache has parsed the cache, shrink dashApps with realloc to max(dashAppCount, 1). In dashLibApplyScan, free the old array and adopt j->sc.fresh (realloc'd to nfresh) instead of memcpy, then clear j->sc.fresh before scanFree.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: (512 - n) x 828 B of heap returned, e.g. about 382 KB with 50 apps; the 414 KB memcpy on every applied scan goes away. Peak heap during a scan is unchanged (the scan still allocates its 512-entry buffer).
findings.evidence: sizeof(DashApp) = 256+64+160+40+24+24+256+1+1+2 = 828 B (include/dash_internal.h:34-37, 690-702); DASH_MAX_APPS 512 (dash_internal.h:39). grep dashAppCount writes: only dash_lib.c cacheKv 555-579, LoadCache 591, ApplyScan 929 (and dashLibRemove shrinking); dash_main.c:1312-1318 appends only under the unbuilt DASH_AUTOTEST. dashLibLoadCache is called once (dash_main.c:1292). Screens re-resolve their pointers after a scan (dash_main.c:715-719 rebuilds Apps and Home), so swapping the array keeps the existing contract stated at dash_lib.c:762-765.

findings.title: dashToolsPrepareMmceStatus can reboot the IOP on the UI thread while another worker job is running
findings.problem: Opening the MMCE backups page with a backup path set and MMCE not loaded waits only for its own status job (dash_tools.c:496), then calls loadMmceModules (502). If MX4SIO owns the SIO2 stack, loadMmceModules -> switchStorageDriverStack -> resetRuntimeDeviceState reboots the IOP (init.c:2272-2274); resets are refused only on the worker thread (init.c:2168) and the park hook ignores UI-thread resets (dash_worker.c:155-156). A queued or running save/art/listing job then loses the IOP mid-RPC. dash_worker.c:15-17 requires waiting for the whole queue first, and dashToolsSyncAllMmceCards does exactly that (624) before the same load (631).
findings.fix: Drop the mmce_status_job condition so line 496 always calls dashWorkerAwaitAll; it returns immediately when nothing is queued (dash_worker.c:342-343).
findings.benefit: Closes an IOP reboot under a running worker job (hung or failed RPC, possibly a DASHBOARD.CNF write left truncated after its O_TRUNC open, dash_store.c:157-160; INFERRED). No lines added.
findings.evidence: grep dashToolsPrepareMmceStatus: only caller dash_settings.c:935 (openPage P_MMCE_BACKUP). Read init.c:2369-2387 (loadMmceModules -> switchStorageDriverStack), 2266-2284 (reset when stack mode != DEFAULT), 2161-2187 (resetRuntimeDeviceState: refused only if iopResetBlocked, set to dashWorkerOnThread at dash_worker.c:135; iopResetHook returns for non-worker threads, dash_worker.c:153-156). Jobs that can be in flight on the settings screen: dash_store.c:651 saves, dash_settings.c:2680 card check, dash_art.c:461. Whether a job overlaps in practice depends on timing (INFERRED); the MX4SIO-active precondition is required for the reset path.

findings.title: qrcodegen.c is built with its 53 assert() calls live (no NDEBUG), pulling __assert_func into the ELF
findings.problem: The wLaunchELF target defines no NDEBUG (ps2.yaml:614-630), so every assert in the vendored QR library is compiled, including the ones in getModuleBounded/setModuleBounded that -O2 inlines into the module loops (qrcodegen_encodeSegmentsAdvanced is 9508 bytes). qrcodegen.o is the only object that pulls libc assert.o (__assert_func), which in turn pulls fiprintf. qrcodegen.c is the only file under src/ or ee_libs/ that uses assert.
findings.fix: Add NDEBUG to the wLaunchELF defines in ps2.yaml (no other src/ or ee_libs/ file uses assert), or put #define NDEBUG before #include <assert.h> in qrcodegen.c. Leave the library code itself unchanged.
findings.benefit: MEASURED: qrcodegen.o .text 19,492 B, libc assert.o 100 B pulled only by it. INFERRED: removing ~53 assert sites (compare/branch/4-arg call, plus expression strings), several duplicated by inlining, saves an estimated 2-5 KB.
findings.evidence: Grep 'assert\(' over src: 53 in qrcodegen.c, none elsewhere (ee_libs: 0). Grep NDEBUG ps2.yaml: none; BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:107 records wLaunchELF compile flags '-O2 -Wall -ffunction-sections'. evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv:67 qrcodegen.o .text 19492 .rodata 472; link/wLaunchELF-archive-members.tsv:101 libc_a-assert.o (100 B) extracted by qrcodegen.o for __assert_func, :82 fiprintf extracted by assert.o. sizes/ds34-wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv: qrcodegen_encodeSegmentsAdvanced 9508, initializeFunctionModules 3532, drawFormatBits 1892. The byte saving was not measured.

findings.title: Exploit install deletes or creates the update folders before the first MagicGate bind, so a bind failure loses the old install
findings.problem: install_selected_ps2_updates calls prepare_needed_folders (1967), which deletes the existing B?EXEC-SYSTEM folders when the user chose Delete (1650-1654) and creates empty folders (1666), before any payload is bound to the card. The first SecrDownloadFile bind comes later, in install_system_xlf_targets (1901) or bind_custom_payload_to_memory_card (1575, 1602). If that bind fails (bind_payload_to_memory_card returns -ENODEV/-EINVAL/-EIO, 1327-1352), the install returns with the old exploit folders gone and empty folders without icon.sys left on the card.
findings.fix: Bind first, touch the card second. In the stock path sign the needed payloads into memory with sign_payload_to_memory before prepare_needed_folders (the custom path already pre-signs with prepare_custom_signed_payloads). In the custom path move the two bind_custom_payload_to_memory_card calls ahead of prepare_needed_folders. Binding works on an in-RAM buffer and does not use the card's file system, so only the order changes.
findings.justification: Fixes a real data-loss path on the memory card. Nothing new is added; the stock path only holds its signed buffers (under 42 KB) until the writes finish instead of signing one at a time.
findings.benefit: A failed MagicGate bind no longer deletes a working exploit install or leaves empty folders (shown as corrupted data by the browser, INFERRED). RAM: under 42 KB held briefly (SYSTEM.XLF 13896 + XSYSTEM 13896 + 2 x ~7 KB KERNEL, MEASURED from exploits/).
findings.evidence: READ: install_selected_ps2_updates 1944-2015 (custom sign 1953-1961, prepare_magicgate_signer 1963, prepare_needed_folders 1967, then binds at 1901 via sign_payload_to_memory 1358-1390 -> bind_payload_to_memory_card 1381, and at 1575/1602). prepare_needed_folders 1642-1672 runs wipe_existing_update_folders 1651 then ensure_mc_folder 1666. bind_payload_to_memory_card 1320-1356 only calls SecrDownloadFile on the RAM buffer. Runs on the UI thread from dash_exploit.c:160. INFERRED: how often a bind fails; the MagicGate Test mode (2282-2298) and its failure messages (2097-2120) exist because binds do fail on some cards/consoles. Sizes: ls -l exploits/.

findings.title: configSysconfFileExistsOnPort probes mc1: without the mc1AccessRefused guard; the HDD header editor can trigger an IOP reset that evicts MX4SIO
findings.problem: configGetPreferredSysconfPort always opens mcN:/SYS-CONF/<file> on both ports. genOpen of an mc1: path calls ensureMemoryCardPortAccessible(1), which resets the IOP when the MX4SIO stack owns slot 2. On the worker the reset is refused, but actSystemCnf runs EditHddPartitionHeaderSystemCnf on the UI thread, and its temp-path search calls configBuildSysconfPath, so editing an HDD partition SYSTEM.CNF with MX4SIO loaded resets the IOP mid-edit. init.c:2250-2254 states implicit config discovery must never do this; getIpConfig and configStampMcFolderIcon already guard mc1.
findings.fix: In configSysconfFileExistsOnPort return 0 for port 1 when mc1AccessRefused(), like main_startup.c:104 and config.c:412 do.
findings.justification: Adds one condition to an existing early return. It is the guard the codebase already uses at main_startup.c:104 and config.c:412 for the same rule, and it stops an unrequested IOP reset (driver teardown) during an HDD header edit.
findings.benefit: Prevents an unrequested IOP reset and MX4SIO eviction on the UI thread; effect of that reset on the later raw-sector header write is INFERRED
findings.evidence: Read config.c:229-275, 311-314. genOpen (filer_fileops.c:531-556) calls ensurePathMemoryCardAccessible (14-17) -> ensureMemoryCardPortAccessible(1) (init.c:2238-2244) -> resetRuntimeDeviceState(TRUE) when isPathDeviceStackLoaded("mc1:/") is false, which is the case while MX4SIO runs (init.c:3110-3112). Reset refused only when iopResetBlocked() is true (init.c:2168), set to dashWorkerOnThread (dash_worker.c:135). UI-thread caller: dash_hdd.c:956-966 actSystemCnf (comment: 'on the UI thread') -> hdd_header_injector.c:847 hddHeaderBuildTempPath -> 784 configBuildSysconfPath. Existing guards: main_startup.c:104, config.c:412, smb_shares.c:89,108. Whether the HDD header write still succeeds after the reset was not traced.

findings.title: Classic colour editor (colorEditor) loses every change: settingsDraw's colorField call resets classic_col each frame
findings.problem: colorEditor edits classic_col[i] through the pointer colorField returns, then calls dashRenderScene() every frame (1574). That runs settingsDraw (dash_main.c:1210), whose ST_COLOR rows call colorField again (3986), and its classic branch (1445-1452) rewrites classic_col[i] from the unchanged setting->color. Each Left/Right/swatch step is undone before the next frame, so on OK c equals orig and classicColorStore (1551-1552) never runs: the 8 classic colour rows (788-795) cannot be changed.
findings.fix: In colorEditor, edit a local DashColor copy for classic colours (copy *c into a local and point c at it when classic is set) and pass that value to classicColorStore on OK instead of reading classic_col. Theme colours keep editing dashTheme directly. Adjust tests/test_classic_settings_persistence.py if classicColorStore takes the colour as an argument.
findings.justification: Adds about two lines (the local copy and the pointer switch). settingsDraw has to keep refreshing classic_col to show the current values, so the editor needs its own copy; this is smaller than tracking which row is being edited.
findings.benefit: Makes the 8 classic colour settings editable from Settings again; adds about 2 lines (INFERRED from the cited code path, not run on hardware).
findings.evidence: Read dash_settings.c 1425-1584 (classic_col, classicColorStore, colorField, colorEditor loop) and 3906-3994 (settingsDraw draws rows item_top..item_top+ITEM_ROWS, includes the focused row, calls colorField for ST_COLOR). Read dash_main.c 1186-1222: dashRenderScene calls screens[section]->draw() unless scene_override is set; grep dashPushSceneOverride shows only browser, exploit, editor, hex and hdd scenes push one, never Settings. colorEditor's only caller is settingsInput at 3791 for ST_COLOR rows.

findings.title: dashLaunchApp rewrites DASHAPPS.CNF before every launch even when the Recent list did not change (or Recent is off)
findings.problem: dashLaunchApp calls dashStorePushRecent unconditionally, and dashStorePushRecent marks the lists dirty even when the path is already recent[0]. settleBackgroundWork (dashStoreFlushWait) then writes the whole DASHAPPS.CNF and reads it back (dashWriteFile, dash_store.c:148-175) and the launch waits for it. Relaunching the top app, the common case, costs a store-dir (often memory card) write each time. It also records Recent when dashCfg.recent_count is 0 (Recent off), which dashLaunchHook (:263) honours.
findings.fix: In dashStorePushRecent return before dashStoreSaveLists when idx is 0 (already first). In dashLaunchApp call dashStorePushRecent only when dashCfg.recent_count > 0, as dashLaunchHook does.
findings.justification: Adds one early return and one condition. Without them every relaunch of the most recent app waits on a full DASHAPPS.CNF write plus read-back on the store device (mc0:/SYS-CONF or beside the ELF). Two conditions are the smallest way to skip that write.
findings.benefit: One DASHAPPS.CNF write + verify read and the launch wait for it saved per launch of the top Recent app or with Recent set to 0 (INFERRED from the call path; time not measured).
findings.evidence: Read dash_main.c:592-682 (push at :649, settleBackgroundWork :652 -> dashStoreFlushWait dash_store.c:670-681 -> dashStoreFlush(1) -> submitSave(SAVE_LISTS) :622-657 -> saveRun -> dashWriteFile :148-175, which always truncates, writes and reads back). dashStorePushRecent :843-861: idx==0 leaves the list unchanged but still calls dashStoreSaveLists (:716-720 sets save_dirty). recent_count 0 means Recent off: dash_settings.c:968 options {0,4,8,12,16}, dash_home.c:104-111 shows only recent_count entries; grep dashLists.recent: no other reader.

findings.title: opBackupActiveMmce compares the new backup with the previous one on the UI thread after the progress overlay is closed
findings.problem: After mcCardBackupActiveMmce has written and verified the image, dashLoadingEnd() is called (1589) and only then activeHistoryFilesEqual reads the whole new backup and the previous history image in 16 KB reads (2 x 8 MB for a standard card), with no dashLoadingStatus/frame in the loop. On a USB destination this is several seconds with the screen frozen on the finished overlay and input ignored; when the card is unchanged the just-written 8 MB file is then deleted. The selected-card path in mmce_backup.c:565-577 compares the source with the newest history before writing anything.
findings.fix: Smallest: move dashLoadingEnd() below the compare and call dashLoadingStatus("Comparing with previous backup", done, total) once per chunk in activeHistoryFilesEqual so frames keep drawing. Optional, saves the write: compare the source with the newest history first, as mmce_backup.c does; needs hardware testing because mcCardBackupActiveMmce keeps the synthetic source open on purpose (mc_card_export.c:250-253).
findings.justification: Adds about two lines (the status call and its counters); removes a multi-second unresponsive period on the UI thread, which the target rules forbid.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: ~16 MB read with no frame per repeat backup (seconds on USB 1.1) becomes a progress bar; the optional reorder also saves an 8 MB write + 16 MB verify read when the card is unchanged.
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c:1555-1623 and 1400-1447. dash_ui.c:1406-1426 (dashLoadingStatus draws only while loading_active) and 1527-1533 (dashLoadingEnd clears it): nothing is drawn during the compare. mc_card_export.c:239-296 writes then re-reads the whole image; source_info_fd (173-203) sizes are page*pages_per_cluster*clusters (8 MB for a standard card). mmce_backup.c:550-577 compares before writing. Only reached when an earlier history file exists (newest > 0 at 1596). USB throughput and resulting seconds are INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: mcDir: a 128 KB libmc directory table is reserved in .bss for the whole run but used only during readMC/readXFROM
findings.problem: static sceMcTblGetDir mcDir[MAX_ENTRY + 1] (2049 x 64 B = 131,136 B) receives mcGetDir/xfromGetDir results and is copied entry by entry into the caller's FILEINFO array in the same function; nothing reads it afterwards, yet it stays reserved for the whole session, including while copy, cloud TLS or image code needs heap.
findings.fix: Allocate the table with memalign(64, limit * sizeof(sceMcTblGetDir)) at the start of readMC/readXFROM, free it after the copy loop (a failed allocation is handled like a failed read), and delete the static table; update tests/test_listing_complete.py:248 and tests/test_mc_detect_retry.py:16, which match the declaration text.
findings.justification: Adds an allocate/free pair (about six lines) to return 128 KB of permanently reserved RAM to the heap outside memory-card listings; memalign keeps the 64-byte alignment the SIF transfer needs. Peak memory during an MC listing is unchanged, which is why this is rated below the RAM threshold.
findings.benefit: 131,136 bytes of .bss no longer reserved outside MC/XFROM listings (MEASURED: BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:83, 131136 .bss mcDir); peak during a listing unchanged.
findings.evidence: Grep -n 'mcDir' over src/Launchstation: filer.c:488 (definition), 509, 534-538 (readMC), 581, 590-594 (readXFROM); tests/test_listing_complete.py:248 and tests/test_mc_detect_retry.py:16 match the source line. limit is at most MAX_ENTRY + 1 (507, 580). Size from evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:83.

findings.title: Card contents keeps 82 KB of list buffers (ct_saves, ct_titles, ct_details, ct_items) in .bss for the whole run
findings.problem: ct_saves (30,000 B), ct_titles (24,000 B), ct_details (24,000 B) and ct_items (4,048 B) are static, but ct_titles/ct_details/ct_items are used only inside dashCardTool (1577-1622) and ct_saves only while a card dialog runs; ctDropSave (451) and dashCardNewBlank (1486) fill all 250 entries just to read the count. The sibling views already malloc their lists per call (2195-2206, 2729-2736). ctResize, ctSplitGameId and dashCardNewBlank each hold their own static sb[512]/root[1024] pair although they never run together.
findings.fix: Allocate the title/detail/item arrays (and the saves list) in dashCardTool on entry and free them on return, as dashCardAllSaves does; call mcViewListSaves with max 0 and NULL in ctDropSave and dashCardNewBlank (allowed, mc_card_view.c:327); give ctResize/ctSplitGameId/ctGameCard a heap list; keep one file-scope sb/root pair.
findings.justification: Replaces static arrays with per-call allocation. The concrete problem is 82 KB of EE RAM reserved for the whole run for a rarely opened dialog; the two sibling views in the same file already work this way, so it adds only the malloc/free lines (about +10 net).
findings.benefit: 82,048 B of .bss returned to the heap while no card dialog is open, plus 3,072 B from sharing sb/root (MEASURED, raw/sizes/wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv); peak use while the dialog is open is unchanged.
findings.evidence: Symbol sizes from evidence/Launchstation/raw/sizes/wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv: ct_saves 30000, ct_titles 24000, ct_details 24000, ct_items 4048, ctResize.sb/root, ctSplitGameId.sb/root, dashCardNewBlank.sb/root 512/1024 each; dash_card_tool.o .bss 109,504 (BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:91). grep -n ct_saves|ct_titles|ct_details|ct_items over src/Launchstation: only dash_card_tool.c (45-48, 451, 1005-1022, 1102, 1180-1187, 1231-1254, 1486, 1566-1622). At 451 and 1486 only n/found are used afterwards. mcViewListSaves accepts max 0 with out NULL (mc_card_view.c:327) and still sets *total.

findings.title: Google Drive link/sync/browse/recover and 'back up all MMCE cards' block the UI thread; frame redrawn only once per file
findings.problem: These paths call blocking card and HTTPS work directly on the UI thread behind dashLoadingBegin. The overlay is redrawn only when a progress callback fires: once per file before hashing, validating and uploading it (cloud_google.c:1529-1561) and once per card before a full-verify backup (mmce_backup.c:774-781); uploads (cloud_http.c:805-815) and Drive recovery downloads report nothing, and each cloudLink poll is a full TLS round trip (304). The screen shows a frozen frame with a stopped spinner and ignores input for the whole of each step. dashToolsCheckUpdates already runs the same kind of HTTPS on the worker through updateRun (883-921) so frames keep presenting.
findings.fix: Route these calls through the existing worker path used by updateRun (dashWorkerSubmit plus dashWorkerAwait(id, title, 0)). Prepare the network and device stacks on the UI thread first (ensureDashboardIpNetworkReady, ensurePathDeviceStackReady, loadMmceModules), as dashToolsCheckUpdates does at 947, because IOP resets are refused on the worker (init.c:2168). dashLoadingStatus already forwards worker-side progress to dashWorkerStatus (dash_ui.c:1408-1411), so the existing callbacks keep working.
findings.justification: Each call site needs a small argument struct and run function (about 20 lines in total, INFERRED), but it removes multi-second frozen frames from user-started backups, uploads and downloads, and it reuses the worker and await code that already exists instead of adding a new mechanism.
findings.benefit: Frames and the spinner keep running during uploads, downloads and card backups. Frozen time per 8 MB card INFERRED at several seconds (SHA-256 plus validation read plus TLS upload on the EE). About -20 lines net (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read dash_tools.c:213-378, 616-712, 883-921, 1191-1355. grep 'progress(' in cloud_google.c: only 1532 (per file, total 0). grep cloudHttpProgress: set only in self_update.c:202 (updater), called at cloud_http.c:1189 and 1256 (downloads); cloudHttpUploadFd (cloud_http.c:776-823) has no callback. mmce_backup.c:774-776 and 952-954 call progress once per .mcd. dash_ui.c:1406-1426: overlay draws only when dashLoadingStatus is called. dash_worker.c:298-338: dashWorkerAwait keeps presenting frames. Durations are not measured.

findings.title: Development-only #ifdef blocks that no build defines: DASH_AUTOTEST, DASH_THEME_TOUR, WLE_BOOT_DIAGNOSTICS
findings.problem: None of the three macros is set by ps2.yaml or configure_ds34.py; they guard a demo library and button-replay script (DASH_AUTOTEST), a theme slideshow (DASH_THEME_TOUR) and six 'Boot check N' drawMsg prints (WLE_BOOT_DIAGNOSTICS). docs/dashboard.md:601-604 and docs/themes.md:436 describe the first two as dev aids to enable by hand.
findings.fix: Delete the blocks and include/dash_autotest.h, plus the doc paragraphs, unless the owner still uses these emulator aids; the boot-check prints at least are leftover debug output.
findings.benefit: ~115 source lines removed; no ELF change since the code is never compiled (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep DASH_AUTOTEST|DASH_THEME_TOUR|WLE_BOOT_DIAGNOSTICS over src/Launchstation (excluding docs): only the #ifdef sites listed, pad.c:284-325, dash_autotest.h; no ps2.yaml/scripts/workflow mention (brief section 2 and lead cond-macros-undefined.tsv agree). Docs: docs/dashboard.md:601-604, docs/themes.md:436, docs/plans/2026-10-18-tester-follow-up.md:49.

findings.title: 18 swapKeys if/else pairs differ only in the button glyph digit
findings.problem: Every tooltip is written twice, once with '\xFF1'/'\xFF0' and once with them swapped, depending on swapKeys. gui_neutrino.c:497 already shows the shorter form (swapKeys ? '1' : '0' passed to one format). Moot if finding 1 is applied.
findings.fix: Compute the OK and cancel glyph characters once per draw and use a single sprintf with %c for each tooltip.
findings.benefit: ~90 lines removed (18 pairs x ~6 lines, minus ~2 lines per file for the glyph variables, INFERRED); small .rodata saving from fewer format strings.
findings.evidence: Counted pairs while reading: config.c 4 (1728-1739, 1742-1749, 1751-1758, 1760-1767), config_advanced.c 3, config_startup.c 5 (incl. 224-233), config_network.c 3, config_screen.c 3. Grep 'swapKeys \?' over src shows the compact form at gui_neutrino.c:497. Rated 2 because finding 1 removes all of it.

findings.title: Feature #ifdefs in dash_devices.c/dash_files.c test macros every build always defines
findings.problem: MMCE, MX4SIO, ILINK, XFROM, DVRP, EXFAT, UDPFS, SMB and ETH are unconditionally defined for the only EE target (ps2.yaml:618-629), and the DS34 variant only adds DS34 (scripts/configure_ds34.py:36), so 82 directive lines in dash_devices.c and 4 in dash_files.c guard code that is always compiled. Unlike the code elsewhere, dashBootDeviceBit (lines 909-916) already uses ata/mmce/mx4sio/ilink without guards, so the files are not even consistent.
findings.fix: Delete the #ifdef/#endif lines for these macros in both files (keep the guarded code). If the owner wants the macros gone repo-wide, do it in one pass with the other dash_* files. findings.fix: Replace readIsoSystemCnf and its three helpers with readPs1SystemCnf on a PS1_IMAGE_READER {fd, 0, 2048}. Move the stricter checks neutrino needs (file-size bound, directory-record sanity) into readPs1SystemCnf so both callers get them, and keep parseIsoGameID.

findings.evidence: Read neutrino_gameid.c:1-260 and popstarter_vcd.c:1-257. Both search PVD from LBA 16 for 'CD001' type 1, read root record at offset 156 (LBA +2, size +10), walk records (len, flags +25, name_len +32, name +33) for SYSTEM.CNF and read its extent. findings.title: Cached card-image reader ctRead/ctOpen is a copy of mmce_backup.c fp_read/card_fingerprint
findings.problem: ctRead (45 lines) and mmce_backup.c fp_read (44 lines) are the same 4-way, 4 KB block cache line for line, differing only in names (CardIo/FpReader, CT_WAYS/MMCE_FP_WAYS, ct_cache/fp_cache); the struct and the open sequence (tags to -1, genOpen, size via lseek, fill McViewSource, mcViewOpen) are also repeated in ctOpen and card_fingerprint. Each copy keeps its own 16 KB static cache.
findings.fix: Keep one reader (struct, read callback, open/close) in one file and export it; have card_fingerprint call it with read-only access. Delete the other copy and its defines.
findings.justification: Replaces a duplicated 45-line cache plus open sequence with one shared copy; the export is a single declaration, so the net change is a removal.
findings.benefit: ~55 lines removed (INFERRED from the cited ranges). Sharing the 16 KB cache as well would save 16 KB .bss (4*4096, INFERRED), but only if no fingerprint runs while a card-tool image is open; not verified.
findings.evidence: Read dash_card_tool.c:35-145 and mmce_backup.c:31-42,204-278. Grep McViewSource/src.read over src: only dash_card_tool.c:121/136, mmce_backup.c:255/269, mmce_save_versions.c:114/126 (the last is an uncached reader). Body of ctRead and fp_read compared line by line: identical apart from identifiers.

findings.title: ctLibToCard re-implements dashCardImportMany (port < 0) for library .psu files

findings.title: Neutrino game profiles use two versioned slots, a checksum and a second full re-read after dashWriteFile already verifies
findings.problem: Each ~70-byte per-game options record is kept as NEUT-<id>-A.CNF and -B.CNF with a revision number and FNV checksum; a save reads both slots, writes the older one, then profileReadLatest re-reads and re-parses both slots to verify. dashWriteFile already re-opens and byte-compares the written file (dash_store.c:163-174), and losing a profile on an interrupted write only means the game launches with default options.
findings.fix: Store one NEUT-<id>.CNF written with dashWriteFile and read with dashLoadTextFile; delete profileChecksum, profileReadLatest, the slot/revision logic and the post-write re-read. Keep the strict sscanf/range validation. Old A/B files are simply ignored (or read the -A name once if migration matters). Update tests/test_neutrino_profiles.py.
findings.benefit: ~50 lines removed; one memory-card file per profiled game instead of two (each MC file costs a directory entry and at least one 1 KB cluster, INFERRED), and a save does 1 write + 1 verify read instead of 2 reads + 1 write + 3 reads.
findings.evidence: Read gui_neutrino.c:93-261 and dash_store.c:105-175. profileSave (232-261) calls profileReadLatest before and after dashWriteFile; profileReadLatest calls profileReadSlot twice. Grep profileChecksum/NTP1/NEUT-: only gui_neutrino.c and tests/test_neutrino_profiles.py:33.

findings.title: mc_card_export.c duplicates its own I/O and header helpers (write_exact_at/_new, read_exact_at/read_exact_fd, source_info_fd/pcsx2_source_info)
findings.problem: write_exact_at_new (137-161) is write_exact_at (109-130) with different open flags and an 'owned' flag, re-pasted with 4-space indents. read_exact_at (87-107) is open + the loop of read_exact_fd (224-237) + close. pcsx2_source_info (500-535) repeats source_info_fd's magic check, superblock field reads and geometry check (173-203); only the bytes-per-page used for the expected size differs (528 vs 512).

findings.title: cloudHttpDownloadFdInternal and read_response repeat the same 3-5 line cleanup at about 35 exit points
findings.problem: In cloudHttpDownloadFdInternal every error exit repeats its own cleanup: within lines 953-1277 there are 21 tls_free(&tls), 24 free(io_buf), 17 free(raw) and 10 mbedtls_sha256_free(&sha) statements spread over about 24 exits. read_response repeats free(raw) 13 times over 11 exits. The repetition makes each new check cost 4-6 lines and invites a missed free.
findings.fix: Initialise raw/io_buf to NULL and keep a flag for an opened TLS session and a started SHA context, then make each error path set_error and goto one fail label that frees what is set; do the same with one fail label in read_response.
findings.benefit: About 72 cleanup lines in the download loop collapse to ~24 gotos plus an ~8 line label, and ~10 lines go from read_response: ~50 lines net (INFERRED from the counts above). No size claim measured.
findings.evidence: Read cloud_http.c 558-684 and 953-1277 in full. awk count over 953-1277: tls_free(&tls) 21, free(io_buf) 24, free(raw) 17, mbedtls_sha256_free(&sha) 10; over 558-684: free(raw) 13. The function serves both the updater (self_update.c:204 via cloudHttpDownloadMem) and Drive recovery (cloud_google.c:1043, 1150), so it needs testing on both.

findings.title: Debug-build macros IOPTRAP, UDPTTY, POWERPC_UART (cannot link), SIO_DEBUG and NO_IOP_RESET are set by no build
findings.problem: No ps2.yaml target or script defines any of these. IOPTRAP, UDPTTY and POWERPC_UART load ioptrap_irx, udptty_irx and ppctty_irx, which exist nowhere in the repo or embed list, so turning them on fails to link; UDPTTY plus POWERPC_UART together would also redeclare 'int i, d' inside Reset(). The two SIO_DEBUG blocks at 1244-1251 are back to back.

Keep SIO_DEBUG, NO_IOP_RESET and ULE_DEBUG_BUILD, which need no missing blobs. Keep launchelf.h:36, which tests/test_project_branding.py checks.

findings.title: copy() repeats the per-device stat/attribute restoration for folders and files, each with an empty if-else chain

Differences: 1230 vs 1643 attribute constant; 1240 vs 1653-1658 (mctype_PSx check); 1673 mmce branch only in the file closure. findings.title: printXY_sjis repeats the Shift-JIS to ELISA index mapping and symbol table that dash_font.c also has
findings.problem: draw_text.c:266-292 converts SJIS to EUC and walks font404 to get the ELISA glyph index; dash_font.c:46-68 (elisaGlyphIndex, commented 'Same ... mapping as the classic renderer') does the same arithmetic. The five PlayStation-button codes (0x819B, 0x817E, 0x81A0, 0x81A2, 0x81A1) are hand-written as five copy-paste switch cases in draw_text.c:222-260 and again as an if-chain in dash_font.c:121-125.
findings.fix: Make elisaGlyphIndex non-static (or move it next to font404 in draw_text.c) and call it from printXY_sjis (glyph * 8 is the byte offset); replace the five switch cases with one small code-to-glyph table shared by both files.
findings.benefit: ~45 lines removed (INFERRED: 39 lines of switch cases become ~6, 27 lines of mapping become one call); a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read draw_text.c:206-332 and dash_font.c:39-144. Both compute code -= 0x4000 for >=0xE000, the same lead/trail shuffle, +0xA1A1, row*94 and the font404 subtraction loop; dash_font adds a lead/trail validity check and bounds n < 55016/8, while draw_text bounds n*8 <= 55008 (same limit). printXY_sjis callers: filer_browser.c:1815. Check before merging: glyph range edge (55008 vs 55016) and the y+1 nudge for code <= 0x829A stay in printXY_sjis.

findings.title: preloadCNFFd streamed-read fallback (128 KB buffer) for devices that fail lseek
findings.problem: After a failed SEEK_END/SEEK_SET (or a failed small malloc) the file is reopened and read in 4 KB chunks into a fresh 128 KB+1 buffer with a probe for oversize. No device in the repo is shown to need it (the comment only says 'some stacks may'); a malloc failure for a small CNF falls into a path that allocates more. Every other loader in this file (configWriteNetworkSnapshot, configStampMcFolderIcon) simply relies on genLseek.
findings.fix: Delete the fallback_stream path and return NULL when lseek or malloc fails, as configWriteNetworkSnapshot does.
findings.benefit: ~45 lines removed; a few hundred bytes of preloadCNFFd's 532 B .text (MEASURED symbol size; saving INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read config.c:435-527. Callers: preloadCNF (main_startup.c:178 SYSTEM.CNF on cdrom0) and loadConfig (config.c:938). INFERRED: that genLseek works on every device the CNF can be loaded from (mc, mass, hdd/pfs, cdrom, host); not verified on hardware or in driver code.

findings.title: dashDevicesStart is synchronous but callers use a callback plus deferred pend/pick state to get its result
findings.problem: dashDevicesStart runs startSync/probeMount on the UI thread and calls cb before it returns (dash_devices.c:765-773); `user` is NULL at every call site and both callbacks (pendProbeDone, pickStartDone) ignore mount and user and only latch ok. dash_files.c then keeps a pend struct, an 'Another device is still starting' guard, a per-frame dashFilesPoll from dash_main.c and a section-changed branch, although the result is already known when the call returns; dash_widgets.c does the same with pk.start_done/start_ok.
findings.fix: Drop DashProbeDone, cb and user; return the probe result directly (keep -1 for backed out and 1 for refused, e.g. return 2/0 for usable/not found or move refused to -2). Handle the result inline in startDevice and in the picker, and delete pend, pendProbeDone, dashFilesPoll (and its call and prototype), pickStartDone and the start_done/start_ok fields. Update tests/test_udpfs_retry.py:22 and test_device_input.py, which assert on the old call text.
findings.benefit: ~40 lines across dash_devices.c, dash_files.c, dash_widgets.c, dash_main.c, dash_internal.h (INFERRED from cited ranges); one function call per frame removed
findings.evidence: Callers (grep dashDevicesStart): dash_files.c:135 (pendProbeDone, NULL), dash_widgets.c:1209 (pickStartDone, NULL), dash_browser.c:694 (NULL, NULL). Read pendProbeDone dash_files.c:77-83 and pickStartDone dash_widgets.c:960-966: both (void)mount/(void)user. dashFilesPoll only called at dash_main.c:1450, same loop iteration as the input that started the device. INFERRED: dashWorkerAwaitAll/loading overlay cannot change the current section, so the section-mismatch branch dash_files.c:92-96 is unreachable.

findings.title: listDir ATA branch hand-rolls the retry loop that readGENERICWithFirstOpenRetry already implements
findings.problem: The ATA case of listDir (1994-2043) reads once, then polls fileXioDopen with a 100 ms busy backoff for 2000 ms (root) or 750 ms and re-reads, stopping on entries or on a non-root path. readGENERICWithFirstOpenRetry (345-381), already used for usb, mass, ilink and cf, does the same loop with the same root test semantics.
findings.fix: Replace the ATA body with loadAtaModules(), canonicalizeAtaPath() and n = readGENERICWithFirstOpenRetry(read_path, info, max, root ? 2000 : 750) (or a flat 2000 as the other BDM devices use).
findings.benefit: ~40 source lines removed; a few hundred bytes of .text INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Read filer.c 345-381 and 1994-2043. Differences: the helper returns at once for a non-root folder that opens but is empty (the ATA loop re-reads it once), and the helper checks isPcCardCfPath, which is false for ata paths. isSimpleDeviceRootPath matches the ATA root test for canonical ataN:/ paths. The MX4SIO branch 2069-2189 is a larger variant with alternate path forms and is not included.

findings.title: Format-new-image, copy-saves and verify-list sequence written three times (ctResize, ctGameCard, dashCardNewBlank)
findings.problem: ctResize 1069-1107 and ctGameCard 1152-1191 both: genOpen O_EXCL, mcCardFormat via ctAppend, close, then per save ctReadSave + ctOpen rw + mcCardWriteSave + ctClose, then reopen and require mcViewListSaves to count exactly the copied saves. dashCardNewBlank repeats the open/format/close part. findings.fix: Let ctResize call ctGameCard with a NULL id meaning every save (ctGameCard already takes the list and filters by id), and have dashCardNewBlank call the same format step with n = 0; merge the two source preludes into one helper that returns the identity and the name list.
findings.benefit: ~40 lines removed (INFERRED from the repeated ranges).
findings.evidence: Read 985-1128, 1144-1291, 1401-1506. The two save loops (1079-1096, 1159-1176) and the two list checks (1097-1107, 1177-1191) differ only in the id filter and the extra game-id check; refusal text at 1013 and 1239 is the same sentence.

findings.title: Two near-duplicate function pairs in hdd_header_injector.c: the source wait loops and the raw-range read/write

findings.title: main_startup.c small redundancies: one-entry ROMVER path loop, second ROMVER prefix parser, redundant #if, unused counter
findings.problem: uLE_InitializeRegion loops over a one-element romver_paths array and strncpy's the literal into path_buf before opening it. getRomverPrefixNumber re-parses the first four ROMVER digits as decimal, although initializeBootExecPath already parses them as hex into ROMVersion; for digit-only prefixes 'decimal >= 220' equals 'ROMVersion >= 0x220'. The outer #if defined(ETH) || defined(UDPFS) at 597/606 only wraps two inner #ifdefs. readSystemCnf counts var_cnt and scanSystemCnf returns a value, and neither is read.

findings.evidence: Read main_startup.c fully. romver_paths has one entry (217-219). getRomverPrefixNumber called at 292 and 754 only (Grep). shouldHideHddAtaDevices can run before initializeBootExecPath (bringUpBootDeviceStack at main_boot.c:51 precedes initializeBootDisplayDefaults at :52), so the lazy path must stay. var_cnt is written only at 180; the scanSystemCnf return is ignored at 181.

findings.title: mmce_igr.c re-implements its own install/inspect plumbing several times

findings.title: read_file in cloud_http.c re-implements dashLoadTextFile

The ca_len + 1 at 405 still works because the buffer is NUL-terminated.

findings.title: ember.c copyElf duplicates psu_functions.c psu_backup_copy_bytes (copy file, delete partial output)

They differ only in buffer size (32 KB vs PSU_COPY_BUFFER), memalign vs malloc, openPathForRead vs genOpen for the source and the return convention.
findings.fix: Keep one of them as a shared non-static helper (for example psu_backup_copy_bytes, returning 0/negative) and call it from ensureLocalEmber; delete copyElf.

findings.title: releaseJsonString and the asset size parse re-implement cloud_google.c json_string/json_int
findings.problem: dash_tools.c releaseJsonString (needle "key", strstr, skip to ':', whitespace, quoted value copy) is the same algorithm as the static json_string in cloud_google.c, which also handles escapes; the inline "size" parse in releaseAssetDigest (skip spaces and ':' then atoi) is json_int's body. Both files are linked into the same ELF and the dash_tools.c code is only built with ETH && WLE_NATIVE_CLOUD, where cloud_google.c is also compiled.
findings.fix: Make cloud_google.c json_string (and json_int) non-static with a prototype in cloud_google.h, delete releaseJsonString and call the shared one; replace the inline size parse with json_int on the asset slice. Results are equivalent for the fields used (status, target_commitish, digest, name), which are then validated anyway.
findings.benefit: ~33 source lines removed and one copy of the parser in .text (a few hundred bytes, INFERRED from the 31-line function at -Os)
findings.evidence: Read dash_tools.c:715-790 and cloud_google.c:61-121. Grep for the needle pattern snprintf(needle,...,"\"%s\"") over src/: only cloud_google.c:69,113 and dash_tools.c:723. ps2.yaml:506 compiles src/cloud_google.c unconditionally (no file-level #if; only WLE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID blocks at :207,238). releaseJsonString callers: dash_tools.c:760,772,864,968. Empty-string difference (releaseJsonString rejects n<=0) is covered by later checks: updateIsCommitId, strncmp sha256:, unknown status.

findings.title: The 15 MISC command names are listed three times (lang.c rename chain, lang.c rebuild, config.c initConfig)
findings.problem: updateLocalizedMiscPaths has a 15-arm else-if chain pairing each setting->Misc_* field with its LANG id, then 16 sprintf lines building the same fields again; initConfig repeats the 16 sprintf lines with LNG_DEF (and config.c:814 uses LNG instead of LNG_DEF for Build_Info, an inconsistency).
findings.fix: Add one static table of {offsetof(SETTING, Misc_x), LANG_x} and loop over it in all three places (dash_tools.c already addresses these fields by misc_offset). Keep the extra "Exploit Installer" legacy alias as one special case.
findings.justification: The same 15-entry list is written out three times (about 63 lines); one table plus three short loops is about 30 lines, so the change removes code, and a new MISC command then needs one table line instead of three edits.
findings.benefit: ~33 source lines removed net (INFERRED: 63 cited lines -> ~30); some .text from the unrolled sprintf calls (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read lang.c:361-434 and config.c:793-816; launchelf.h:286-300 shows the fields are all char[64]; LNG/LNG_DEF at launchelf.h:682-683 index by LANG_##name so a table of LANG ids works with both Lang_String and Lang_Default. dash_tools.c:1610 already uses (const char *)setting + t->misc_offset.

Public entries HddHeaderListSourcePartitions:350 and InjectHddPartitionHeaderFromSource:1112-1115 validate source_device/partition_name; dash_hdd.c:289,294,966,999 pass job/partition names.

findings.title: dashTextWrapScrollTimed is never called; the textWrap draw flag exists only for it
findings.problem: dashTextWrapScrollTimed appears only at its definition and its prototype; the linker discards it. Its measurement pass is the only caller of textWrap with draw=0, so once it is gone the draw parameter and the empty if(!draw) branch are dead and textWrap is a private copy of dashTextWrap.

findings.title: CT32 GSTEXTURE setup re-typed five times while dash_gfx.c already has setupTex (static)
findings.problem: Each copy writes the same memset/Width/Height/PSM=CT32/Mem/Filter/Delayed=1/gsKit_setup_tbw (and in two cases SyncDCache) sequence that setupTex in dash_gfx.c:196-207 implements, but setupTex is static and hard-codes GS_FILTER_LINEAR, so the other files repeat it (the scanline copy needs NEAREST).
findings.fix: Make setupTex non-static as dashTexSetup(tex, w, h, mem, filter), declare it in dash_internal.h and replace the five copies with one call each.
findings.justification: Exports an existing function instead of adding a new one; replaces five 7-9 line blocks with single calls, a net reduction of about 30 lines. The SyncDCache it adds to the art and image paths is harmless (the pixels must be flushed before the GS DMA upload anyway).
findings.benefit: ~30 source lines removed, a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED: five inlined field-store sequences become calls).
findings.evidence: Grep 'Delayed = 1' over src: dash_gfx.c:204, dash_art.c:414,538, dash_bg.c:438, dash_bg_geo.c:263, dash_image.c:136, plus dash_font.c:99,291,436 and dash_icons.c:852 which are T8+CLUT textures and are not included. Read every cited block; dash_art.c:409-415 skips the memset because slotFree already zeroed the slot.

findings.title: Copy before genFixPath is a dead store (genFixPath overwrites it); the fix-or-raw-path fallback is hand-written in 10 places
findings.problem: genFixPath always starts with strcpy(gen_path, uLE_path) (filer.c:956), so the strncpy done just before it in editor_file.c:80-81, 219-220, 285-286 and elf.c:90 is overwritten every time. The 'if genFixPath fails, copy the raw path' fallback is then repeated by hand at every listed site (elf.c even has two helpers, launchArgsCopyPath and launchArgsMakeOpenPath, only for it).
findings.fix: Delete the pre-copies. Optionally make genFixPath itself copy the raw path on failure (or add one genFixPathOrRaw in filer.c) and drop the per-site fallbacks and elf.c's launchArgsCopyPath/launchArgsMakeOpenPath.
findings.justification: One shared fallback replaces ten 2-4 line copies and two elf.c helpers, so the net is fewer lines.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines of dead stores; ~30 lines with the shared fallback (INFERRED from the cited ranges).
findings.evidence: Read filer.c:946-986: gen_path is written unconditionally at :956 before any return. Grep 'if (genFixPath(...) < 0)' over src: fallback-to-raw at editor_file.c:82,221,287, elf.c:91, dash_editor.c:315, hdd_header_injector.c:698,722,761,800, main_exploit_installer.c:1513; other sites return an error instead. launchArgsCopyPath callers: only elf.c:90,92; launchArgsMakeOpenPath: elf.c:211,247.

findings.title: Hide_Paths and Show_Titles settings have no consumer; only load/save/toggle code remains
findings.problem: setting->Hide_Paths and setting->Show_Titles are only parsed, defaulted, serialized and toggled (classic Configure menu and dashboard items whose help text says they affect 'the classic launch menu'); nothing reads them to change output. findings.title: VCD game-ID lookup opens the VCD twice more after validateVcd through single-use readVcd* wrappers
findings.problem: popstarter.c:77 opens the VCD in validateVcd, then buildPopstarterVcdGameID opens it again in buildVcdSystemCnfGameID and a third time in buildVcdPvdTimestampGameID, each via openPathForRead (which for hdd:pfs paths calls loadHddModules and mountParty, popstarter_path.c:265-267). readPs1SystemCnf already reads the PVD, so the PVD is read twice. readVcdIsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor and readVcdSystemCnf exist only to build a PS1_IMAGE_READER for these two single callers.

findings.title: cloudGoogleRecoverSnapshot and cloudGoogleRecoverSaveVersion copy the same claim/session/download/digest sequence
findings.problem: Both functions run the same steps with the same error strings: claim a RECOVER-CLOUD name, check result length, start the storage device, load the session, start the network, refresh the token, build the alt=media URL, re-check the names, open the .DOWNLOAD.PART file, call cloudHttpDownloadGoogleFd, close it and compare the SHA-256. The only differences are the extension, the size cap (CLOUD_RECOVERY_MAX_BYTES vs MMCE_SAVE_VERSION_MAX) and one word in an error message. About 45 lines appear twice.

findings.benefit: ~45 duplicated lines become one copy plus a ~10 line signature and two calls: ~30 lines net (INFERRED). .text size change not measured.
findings.evidence: Read 982-1182 side by side; dupes-blocks.tsv also pairs 1005-1028 with 1115-1136 (18 normalised lines), and the copy runs on to the digest check (1054/1161). findings.title: kelf_signer.c 3DES layer: des_cbc_crypt only ever runs one block with a zero IV, key_count 3 is never used, error returns are never checked
findings.problem: tdes_cbc_crypt calls des_cbc_crypt with size 8 and a zero IV for each stage of each block, so the CBC loop inside des_cbc_crypt is unused and subkeys are recomputed every 8 bytes. All 14 callers pass key_count 1 or 2, so the key_count == 3 branches (452-455, 470-473) are dead, and no caller checks the -EINVAL return (all sizes are constant multiples of 8).
findings.fix: Delete des_cbc_crypt; in tdes_cbc_crypt build the one or two subkey schedules once and call des_crypt_block directly per stage; drop the key_count 3 branches and make the function void.
findings.benefit: ~30 source lines removed and fewer des_make_subkeys calls per signing (INFERRED); a few hundred bytes of .text at most (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read every tdes_cbc_crypt call: 820, 822, 823, 920 (key_count 1); 835, 836, 843-846, 864, 898, 921, 1054-1060, 1066-1072 (key_count 2). None tests the return value. des_cbc_crypt is called only from tdes_cbc_crypt (445-471), always with size 8 and tmp_iv zero. Risk Med because it is the signing path; the self-test vector at 1109-1116 can be reused once to check.
