findings.title: Small simplifications in filer_actions.c timestamp and path helpers
findings.problem: (a) time_manip_custom_run casts _Modify to PS2TIME and copies six fields into an sceMcStDateTime of the same layout, with Resv2=0 duplicated in both branches. (b) In buildSasTimestampPayload every category other than 1 and 9 except exact 'SYS' has '_' at index 3, so the 11 strncmp calls equal effective[3]=='_'. (c) setSequentialTimestamp repeats setTunaFolderTimestamp then sets Sec=58. (d) compareTimestampFolderNames only forwards to stricmp for one caller. findings.title: libhdd hddUpdateInfo walks every APA partition entry only to compute hddFree, which nothing reads
findings.problem: hddUpdateInfo issues one fileXioDread per partition entry (main and sub) to compute hddFree, read only by hddGetInfo, which has no caller. hddCheckPresent triggers it on the HDD Manager's first scan, so that scan walks the directory twice (scanRun walks it again at dash_hdd.c:167-209) and sends HDIOC_STATUS three times. hddMakeFilesystem and hddFormat repeat the walk after each create/format, and dash_hdd rescans anyway.
findings.fix: Delete the directory walk and hddSize/hddFree from hddUpdateInfo (keep the HDIOC_MAXSECTOR devctl that hddMakeFilesystem needs) together with the uncalled hddGetInfo. In scanRun, derive present/formatted from the HDIOC_STATUS value it already holds (present: 0..2, formatted: 0), not from the two libhdd calls.
findings.benefit: Removes one full APA directory walk (one Dread RPC plus header read per partition entry, hundreds on a game HDD) from the first HDD Manager scan and from every create/format, and 2 HDIOC_STATUS RPCs per scan. Worker thread, behind the loading overlay (INFERRED timing). ~25 lines.
findings.evidence: Read libhdd.c:75-102 (both checks call hddUpdateInfo when !hddStatusCurrent, then HDIOC_STATUS), 253-293 (walk at 275-288 feeds only hddFree; hddSize only at 257, 269, 288), 130 and 454 (walk repeated after format/make). grep hddGetInfo|hddCheckPresent|hddCheckFormatted|hddMakeFilesystem|hddFormat over the repo: hddGetInfo only at libhdd.c:253 and libhdd.h:75; callers are dash_hdd.c:152, 155, 267, 285. dash_hdd.c:151 already stores HDIOC_STATUS in j->status, and scanRun walks hdd0: itself at 167-209; scan() is run after every change (afterChange).

findings.title: FAT chain step and FAT-cluster lookup written twice (nextOf vs chainNext, fatGet vs mcViewFatLocate)
findings.problem: nextOf in mc_card_write.c repeats chainNext in mc_card_view.c check for check (in-use bit, 0xFFFFFFFF end, mask, alloc_usable bound). fatGet and mcViewFatLocate both carry the same indirect-FAT lookup (ind_index/dbl, ifc_list bound, loadCluster32 of the ifc cluster, ifc_cache index), and mcViewFatGet re-checks the bound that its callers already ensure.
findings.fix: Export chainNext (for example as mcViewChainNext) and delete nextOf; implement fatGet as mcViewFatLocate followed by the FAT cluster load, so the indirect lookup exists once.
findings.benefit: ~20 lines removed (15-line nextOf, ~12 duplicated lookup lines, minus a 5-line export). Code size: a few hundred bytes of .text at most (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_view.c:74-118 and 501-527 and mc_card_write.c:61-75 side by side. nextOf callers: mc_card_write.c:86, 535, 685. mcViewFatGet callers: mc_card_write.c:65, 350 only (grep). INFERRED part: routing fatGet through mcViewFatLocate adds its 'FAT cluster below alloc_offset' check to read paths; the PS2 format places FAT clusters below the data area (mcCardFormat at mc_card_write.c:1058 lays it out that way), so valid cards are unaffected, but a damaged card would now be rejected one step earlier.

findings.title: elf.c isElfPayload/isLikelyEncryptedPayload re-implement classifyExecHeader; getMbrOpenPath re-inlines isHddPartyPath

findings.title: find_file_info allocates and lists a whole directory (2048 FILEINFO) just to read the running ELF's size
findings.problem: To learn the old ELF size for the free-space check, find_file_info memaligns sizeof(FILEINFO)*MAX_ENTRY (about 388 B x 2048 = ~776 KB) and runs getDir on the app folder, while the multi-MB update package is already held in RAM. If that allocation or the listing fails, find_file_info returns 0 and the free-space check at :341 is skipped silently.
findings.fix: Replace find_file_info with an open + genLseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END) + close on the elf path (the pattern validateVcd uses), and use that size in the check.
findings.benefit: ~18 lines removed; avoids a transient ~776 KB heap allocation and a full directory listing during the update (INFERRED: FILEINFO = 256 name + 66 title + 64 sceMcTblGetDir; MAX_ENTRY 2048).
findings.evidence: Read self_update.c:96-119 and :341-346. find_file_info has one caller (:341). FILEINFO at include/launchelf.h:560-565 (name[MAX_NAME=256], title[66], sceMcTblGetDir stats); MAX_ENTRY = 2048 at launchelf.h:205. Only stats.FileSizeByte of the match is used (:342,345). genOpen/genLseek size pattern at popstarter_vcd.c:22-26.

findings.title: read_response parses Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding up to three times and checks the header size twice
findings.problem: Once the header end is in the buffer, every later read iteration parses Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding again (595-599) and checks header_len and the body cap (602-611). After the loop, the header_len check is repeated (638-642), Content-Length is parsed again for the cap/truncation check (643-655) and a third time at 667, and Transfer-Encoding again at 658, although content_length and chunked already hold those values.
findings.fix: Parse the headers and do the two size checks once, the first time the header end is found; after the loop use content_length and chunked, and delete the repeated parses and the second header_len check.
findings.benefit: ~18 lines removed and no header rescans per TLS record of a large body (READ). The time saved is small (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read cloud_http.c 558-684. Header parses: Content-Length 595, 643, 667; Transfer-Encoding 597, 658; header_len > CLOUD_HTTP_HEADER_MAX at 602 and 638; body cap at 607 and 645. All callers (cloudHttpRequest 745, cloudHttpUploadFd 817) use the same function. tests/test_http_body_cap.py extracts header_value/decode_chunked from source, so re-run it.

findings.title: Four explicit ensureDashboardIpNetworkReady calls duplicate the one oauth_post makes immediately after; sync starts Ethernet before storage

findings.title: extract_sidecar walks every PSU record twice with the same validation code
findings.problem: extract_sidecar runs a full validation pass (255-269) and then a second pass (274-286) that repeats the same seek/read/length/padding checks line for line before looking for the record. In production self_update.c:306 has already validated the same RAM package with selfUpdateLocatePsuElf, whose loop (update_psu.c:84-96) performs the same record checks.
findings.fix: Make it one pass: in the single loop, remember the position and length of the record named name, check position == size after the loop, then seek to the remembered record and copy it. Drop the second loop.

findings.evidence: Read update_psu.c:227-333 and 67-181; the two loops 255-269 and 274-286 differ only in that the second checks record_is(entry, 0x8017, name) (the dupes-blocks lead 255-267 == 274-286, 13 normalised lines). self_update.c:306 calls selfUpdateLocatePsuElf before the SidecarMem calls at :327 and :333. tests/test_app_packages.py exercises sidecar extraction and would keep its coverage.

findings.title: Unconditional printf [PASTE] traces in subfunc_Paste ship in release builds
findings.problem: subfunc_Paste prints seven '[PASTE] ...' traces with plain printf, plus a trace_vmc_paste flag that exists only for two of them. The repo's DPRINTF macro is stripped in consumer builds (include/launchelf.h:164), but these printf calls are compiled into every build and run on every paste (per item when a vmc path is involved).
findings.fix: Delete the traces and trace_vmc_paste, or change them to DPRINTF so they vanish from release builds.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines removed; ~450 bytes of format strings plus 7 call sequences (~700 bytes .rodata/.text, INFERRED from the literal lengths)
findings.evidence: Read 2147-2277. grep 'define DPRINTF' include/launchelf.h:158-164 (empty in consumer builds). grep -rn '\[PASTE\]' over the repo: only these lines; no test reads them. String lengths counted by hand: 54+56+69+57+76+84+56 = 452 bytes.

findings.title: artRun opens every candidate artwork file twice: fileExists probe before dashPngLoadFile
findings.problem: fileExists does genFixPath + genOpen + genClose; tryDecode then calls dashPngLoadFile -> dashLoadTextFile (src/dash_store.c:105-119), which does the same genFixPath + genOpen and returns NULL cleanly when the file is missing. The probe adds nothing except an extra open/close for every candidate that exists, on the worker, against memory card / USB / HDD paths.
findings.fix: Delete fileExists and call tryDecode(j, cand) directly at line 375.
findings.benefit: 14 lines removed; one fewer open/close per found artwork file on the worker thread (INFERRED: each MC open is a slow IOP round trip).
findings.evidence: Read dash_art.c:151-163, 341-378, dash_png.c:226-238 (dashPngLoadFile returns -1 when dashLoadTextFile returns NULL), dash_store.c:105-124. Grep fileExists( over the repo: dash_art.c:151 and :375 are the only uses in this file (neutrino_iso.c has its own static copy; tests/test_neutrino_smb.py:125 refers to that one).

findings.title: loadUsbModules re-implements loadBdmCoreModules inline
findings.problem: Lines 1765-1780 load bdm_irx then bdmfs_fatfs_irx with the same have_bdm/have_bdmfs latching as loadBdmCoreModules (2465-2481), which loadMx4sioModules, loadIlinkModules, loadPcCardCfModules and loadAtaBlockDriver already use. The only difference is two extra 'USB BDM'/'USB BDMFS' loading messages.
findings.fix: Replace the inline block with 'if (!loadBdmCoreModules()) loaded_ok = 0;' and drop the two extra messages ('USB core IO' is already shown at 1750).
findings.benefit: ~13 lines removed; a few dozen bytes of .text (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read both blocks: same SifExecModuleBuffer calls, same (ID >= 0 && ret >= 0) latching, same order. Grep loadBdmCoreModules: init.c:381 prototype (visible before 1765), callers 2404,2444,2492,2516. Grep 'USB BDM' in tests: no hits.

findings.title: Imported save is read back twice: mcCardWriteSave verifies, then ctPutSave reopens and reads the whole save again
findings.problem: mcCardWriteSave step 6 already reopens the view (fresh mcViewOpen), reads the whole save into a second McSaveData and compares it with sameSave. ctPutSave then closes, reopens the image read-only and does the same full mcCardReadSave + mcCardSameSave again. Every single-save import (5 ctPutSave callers) therefore reads, mallocs and compares the full save data twice, synchronously on the UI thread under the loading overlay.
findings.fix: Delete the second read-back in ctPutSave (dash_card_tool.c:415-426) and return the mcCardWriteSave result once ctClose succeeded. Keep the verify inside mcCardWriteSave, which the batch paths (dash_card_tool.c:1088 and 1170) rely on.
findings.benefit: One full read of the save (all its data clusters through fileXio) plus one full-size malloc/compare removed per import; ~11 lines removed (INFERRED: count of dash_card_tool.c:415-426).
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_write.c:653-662 (reopen, mcCardReadSave, sameSave) and dash_card_tool.c:392-427 (ctPutSave: mcCardWriteSave at 408, ctClose, ctOpen, mcCardReadSave, mcCardSameSave at 417-425). grep ctPutSave: callers at dash_card_tool.c:523, 937, 1892, 2114, 2500. grep dashWorker in dash_card_tool.c: no matches, so these run on the UI thread (dashLoadingStatus, dash_ui.c:1406). INFERRED part: the post-close read catches no failure the in-function read misses, because both read through fileXio on the same device and ctClose's return is already checked at 409-413.

findings.title: Fixed sleep(1) on the UI thread after every ATA_BD load (HDD/ATA boot, first hdd0:/ata0: access, after each IOP reset)
findings.problem: loadAtaBlockDriver sleeps 1 s after ATA_BD starts. In EXFAT builds both loadAtaModules and loadHddModules (load_ps2hdd_stack(1)) go through it, from the dashboard device probe and the HDD/ATA boot path on the UI thread, so the screen stops for a full second once per IOP session. The ata0: probe that follows already waits up to 2000 ms for the device (dash_devices.c:611), and RiptOPL loads ATAD and its HDD modules back to back with no pause (src/sources/hddsupport.cpp:654-658).
findings.fix: Delete pauseAfterAtaBlockDriverLoad and its call; rely on the driver's own device init and the existing bounded probe. Verify HDD/ATA detection on hardware.
findings.benefit: 1000 ms less UI freeze on HDD/ATA boot and on first HDD/ATA access per IOP session (INFERRED from sleep(1)); ~7 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read init.c:683-744, 2500-2558, 2663-2688; dash_devices.c:594-611 (probeMount on UI thread, ata probe 2000 ms); main_startup.c:651-658 (boot device ATA/HDD). git log -S pauseAfterAtaBlockDriverLoad: only the initial import 944a2fc, no recorded hardware reason. Cross-repo: RiptOPL src/sources/hddsupport.cpp:654-658 loads ATAD then XHDD without a delay. INFERRED part: that no drive needs the settle window (needs hardware test).

findings.title: SMB3 share kind (kind 3, VERSION = 3) is a marker that is lost when the share is reopened in the editor
findings.problem: The editor offers SMB2/SMB3/SMB1 and writes VERSION = 3 for SMB3 (smbCnfBuildBlock kind 3), but the parser maps 3 to version 2 (smb_cnf.c:143), no code acts on the mark (both use connectSmb2), and the editor reloads kind = sh->version (dash_settings.c:535). Reopening an SMB3 share shows SMB2, and saving it again drops the VERSION line.
findings.fix: Delete the SMB3 choice: editor list becomes SMB2/SMB1, smbCnfBuildBlock accepts kinds 1 and 2 only, header comment updated. Keep the parser accepting VERSION = 3 as SMB2 for existing files. Adjust tests/test_smb_cnf_edit.py calls with kind 3.
findings.benefit: ~6 source lines and one editor option that does nothing; no measurable size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read smb_cnf.c:139-146, 475-537; dash_settings.c:526-540, 1020-1031, 1855-1864; grep 'kind' in dash_settings.c: 3869 shows label SMB3 for kind 3, 3437 template text says 3 only marks a server. smbSharesConnect (smb_shares.c:384) picks connectSmb2 for every version other than 1 and NFS. tests/test_smb_cnf_edit.py:64,82,143 build kind 3 blocks.

findings.title: elf.c launchArgSource is written but never read (1 KB .bss and a dead source parameter chain)
findings.problem: launchArgSource[MAX_PATH] is only cleared (41) and filled (151-154); no code reads it. The source argument of launchArgsFinishParse and launchArgsReadFromFd exists only to fill it, and the source parameter of LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer feeds nothing else.
findings.fix: Delete launchArgSource, its clear and copy, and the source parameter of the two static helpers; optionally drop source from LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer and its six callers.
findings.benefit: 1,025 bytes .bss (INFERRED: char[MAX_PATH], MAX_PATH = 1025 in launchelf.h:204); ~6 lines.
findings.evidence: grep -w launchArgSource over the repo: elf.c:35, 41, 152, 153 only (all writes). LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer callers: dash_editor.c:1167, dash_main.c:639, ember.c:354, editor.c:348, neutrino_iso.c:274; LaunchArgsLoadFromFile: dash_browser.c:2568, filer_browser.c:1568. Tests stub LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer with the source parameter (test_ember_retrogem_handoff.py:30, test_launch_iop_override.py:99, test_neutrino_menu_audio.py:61).

findings.title: copy() re-runs prepareTransferDeviceStacks at every recursion level although subfunc_Paste already did it
findings.problem: subfunc_Paste prepares both stacks once (filer_browser.c:2164) and copy() prepares them again for every file and folder (804). Each call re-walks all path checks and ensurePathDeviceStackReady; for host: that is initHOST() (filer.c:1720-1734), which opens host:elflist.txt and dopens host: over the network for every copied entry.
findings.fix: Call prepareTransferDeviceStacks in copy() only when recurses == 0 (or rely on subfunc_Paste's call and delete it from copy()); update tests/test_transfer_stack_preflight.py:176-177, which assert the call is in copy().
findings.benefit: ~2 host RPCs saved per copied entry on host:, fewer string compares elsewhere; ~6 lines (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:804, filer_browser.c:2156-2217 (only copy() caller), filer_device.c:105-228, filer.c:1720-1734 (initHOST). tests/test_copy_pipeline.py:113 models an IOP reset during preflight; whether a reset can happen between two entries of one paste was not traced (INFERRED).

findings.title: Launch-key launch writes LK_Title into the shared library entry (dash_home.c activateChip, dash_main.c runLaunchKey)
findings.problem: dashLibResolve returns &dashApps[i] when the launch-key path is already in the library, and both callers then copy LK_Title into a->title. The library entry is renamed in RAM: Home and Applications show the launch-key title after a failed or cancelled launch, and dashLaunchApp saves DASHLIB.CNF when art is dirty (dash_main.c:647-648), so the wrong title is persisted until a rescan of that device rebuilds it.
findings.fix: When dashLibResolve returns a library entry, copy it into the local tmp before overriding the title (tmp = *a; a = &tmp) in runLaunchKey; dashLaunchApp already works on its own copy. Let activateChip call runLaunchKey (make it non-static) instead of repeating the same branch, so the fix is made once.
findings.justification: Adds one struct copy per launch-key start; it is the smallest way to stop a launch from renaming a library entry, and sharing runLaunchKey removes the duplicate branch in dash_home.c, so the net line count goes down.
findings.benefit: Fixes a user-visible rename of library entries that can be persisted to DASHLIB.CNF; about 5 lines removed net (duplicate branch replaced by one call). INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Read dash_home.c:214-222 (DashApp tmp, *a = dashLibResolve(p,&tmp); dashStrCopy(a->title, LK_Title...)), dash_main.c:959-969 (same pattern), dash_lib.c:471-482 (returns dashLibFind result, a pointer into dashApps, when found). dash_main.c:592-682 dashLaunchApp: copies app, line 647-648 dashLibSaveCache() if dashArtTakeDirty(), returns on cancel (634-635, 652-655) or failed launch (670-681). Home rows point into dashApps (dash_home.c:69), so the changed title is shown. LK_Title is user-settable (dash_settings.c:2247-2249, config.c:1088). grep runLaunchKey: dash_main.c:959 definition, callers 1005/1081/1111/1125; compile.yml:398-399 stack-chain check and tests/test_background_only_hotkeys.py:60 stub use the name, so keep the name when exporting it.

findings.title: Cloud menu re-reads config/token files on the UI thread right after queuing MMCE status jobs (redundant in-function refreshes)
findings.problem: dashToolsSyncAllMmceCards calls dashToolsRefreshMmceStatus on every exit (628, 634, 662, 687, 698, 711) and cloud-menu case 5 calls it at 1440; each queues mmceStatusRun (MMCE scans plus cloudGoogleIsLinked token-file reads on the worker, 403-426). Control returns to the dashToolsCloudBackup loop top, which at once reads WLE-CLOUD.CNF, the CA and token files on the UI thread (1368-1378) while that job, and any settings save queued at 612 or 1464, is still running, against the rule in dash_worker.c:7-10. Both callers already refresh after these functions return (dash_settings.c:3305, 3345).
findings.fix: Delete the seven in-function dashToolsRefreshMmceStatus calls (628, 634, 662, 687, 698, 711, 1440) and start each dashToolsCloudBackup loop pass with dashWorkerAwaitAll, returning if the user backs out.
findings.justification: The added await (2 lines) closes the remaining overlap with the settings save that chooseMmceBackupRoot and the disconnect path queue just before the loop reads files; it returns immediately when nothing is queued. The change is still -5 lines net.
findings.benefit: -5 lines net; one MMCE status scan fewer per in-menu action; the UI no longer does file IO while a job it queued runs. Practical damage of the overlap INFERRED (fileXio RPCs are serialised by the SDK).
findings.evidence: grep dashToolsRefreshMmceStatus: dash_tools.c 483, 515, 628, 634, 662, 687, 698, 711, 1440; dash_settings.c 1817, 2117, 3305, 3337, 3345. Callers of dashToolsSyncAllMmceCards: dash_tools.c:1444, dash_settings.c:3304 (+3305 refresh). dashToolsCloudBackup called from dash_tools.c:1642 and dash_settings.c:3344 (+3345 refresh). Read cloud_google.c:214-241, 258-308, 403-455, 558-574: GetClientConfig, Configured, IsLinked and HasLocalToken all open/stat files via dashLoadTextFile/wleExists (genOpen -> fileXioOpen, filer_fileops.c:531-556). Other UI code honours the rule, e.g. dash_widgets.c:1129 skips polling while dashWorkerIoBusy. tests/test_cloud_menu.py:64 already stubs dashWorkerAwaitAll.

findings.title: wle_igr.c: the HDD driver stack is reloaded on every one of up to 24 path-resolution retries
findings.problem: resolve_app_path calls hdd_target_path on each attempt (151-154, WLE_IGR_TRIES = 24, 250 ms apart). Each call runs SifExecModuleBuffer again for ps2dev9, bdm, bdmfs_fatfs, ata_bd, ps2hdd and ps2fs (122-134), then calls fileXioInit (136). If the first mount fails because the drive is still spinning up, every retry loads six more module copies instead of retrying only the mount. Unlike the other device families, main() (228-255) has no hdd branch that loads the drivers once.
findings.fix: Load the HDD modules once in main(): add hdd0/hdd1 to the ata branch and start ps2hdd/ps2fs with their arguments there. Reduce hdd_target_path to the path split and the pfs0: mount. This also removes the second copy of the ata_bd/bdm load sequence.
findings.benefit: Saves up to 23 x 6 redundant IOP module loads and the IOP memory and time they take on the HDD IGR path (INFERRED). About 5 fewer lines.
findings.evidence: Read wle_igr.c in full. HDD boot paths reach this helper: src/mmce_igr.c:463-470 (is_bdm_relaunch_path includes hdd) and 542-556 install it. INFERRED part: what a second load of ps2dev9/ps2hdd returns (likely NO_RESIDENT_END, which start_module accepts). Either way the loads repeat on every retry.

findings.title: configStampMcFolderIcon writes the same 14990-byte icon three times (list/copy/del.icn) to the user's memory card
findings.problem: After a successful settings save, the folder stamp writes mc_list_icn under list.icn, copy.icn and del.icn because the shipped icon.sys names three different files, though embed_blobs.S:65-66 says they are byte-identical. That is two extra 14990-byte files and two extra file creates on a slow 8 MB card for every stamped folder. The repo's own makeicon.c writes one icon name into all three icon.sys slots, so one file is enough.
findings.fix: Put "list.icn" in the copy and del name slots of res/memory-card/icon.sys (offsets 324 and 388), write only list.icn in configStampMcFolderIcon, and drop copy.icn/del.icn from res/memory-card and the release packages.
findings.benefit: About 29980 bytes less memory-card space and 2 fewer card file writes per stamped folder (MEASURED: list/copy/del.icn are 14990 B each in inventory); ~3 source lines removed
findings.evidence: Read config.c:371-433. inventory/Launchstation.tsv: res/memory-card/list.icn, copy.icn, del.icn 14990 bytes each, icon.sys 964. od of icon.sys shows the names list.icn at offset 260, copy.icn at 324, del.icn at 388. embed_blobs.S:63-67 embeds only icon.sys and list.icn and notes copy/del are identical. makeicon.c:408-410 strcpy's one iconname into view, copy and del. Callers of configStampMcFolderIcon: config.c:786, dash_settings.c:2298, dash_store.c:597.

findings.title: readCD rejects and spins down a DVD-Video/ESR or audio disc that finishes detection during its 500 ms wait
findings.problem: When the disc is still detecting at entry (611), the loop waits for uLE_cdDiscValid, which accepts SCECdCDDA and SCECdDVDV; the range check that follows (619) treats every type above SCECdPS2DVD as invalid, calls uLE_cdStop (stops the drive, init.c:1404) and returns an empty listing. If detection had already finished before entry the check is skipped and the same disc lists. Trigger: insert an ESR-patched disc (reported as DVDV, init.c:1396-1401) or a DVD-Video and open cdfs: right away; the first listing is empty and the drive spins down.
findings.fix: After the wait, return 0 only when the last uLE_cdDiscValid() call failed; delete the range check and the uLE_cdStop call.
findings.benefit: First cdfs listing after inserting a DVD-Video/ESR disc works; about 3 lines removed (INFERRED: the 4-line check becomes one test of the loop's last result).
findings.evidence: Read filer.c:605-655 and init.c:1359-1408. The enum order SCECdPS2DVD 0x14 < SCECdCDDA 0xFD < SCECdDVDV 0xFE is from ps2sdk libcdvd-common.h (INFERRED: the SDK is not in the clone; tests/test_launch_driver_messages.py:65-66 uses stub values). LIBCDVD_LEGACY is not defined by ps2.yaml, so this readCD is the compiled one; include/snippets/readCD.h:12-24 has the same logic but is not built. readCD is reached from listDir (2044-2048).

findings.title: Cancelling the name prompt of Paste-with-rename still pastes under the original name and replaces a same-named file
findings.problem: With PasteMode PM_RENAME, copy() asks for a new name; when keyboard() returns -1 (cancel, which classicKeyboard returns when the dashboard keyboard is dismissed) it copies the original name back and carries on. For a file the destination is then removed and recreated without a prompt (genRemove and O_TRUNC at 1382-1383), so cancelling the rename the user chose to avoid a name clash overwrites the existing destination file, and a Move completes under the original name.
findings.fix: When keyboard() returns a negative value, return COPY_KEPT_DESTINATION (nothing written, nothing for a Move to delete) instead of reverting to the original name; keep the revert only for an empty name.
findings.justification: Replaces the fallback branch with an early return; today a cancelled prompt silently overwrites user data.
findings.benefit: A cancelled rename no longer overwrites a destination file (READ); no size change.
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:816-823 (keyboard(newfile.name, 36) <= 0 -> strcpy(newfile.name, file.name)), 873 (out built from newfile.name), 1374-1391 (genRemove(out), then genOpen with O_TRUNC|O_CREAT, no prompt; folders instead get the newdir -17 prompt at 1049-1074). gui.c:144-262 keyboard returns -1 on cancel; dash_widgets.c:663-668 classicKeyboard returns -1 when dashModalKeyboard fails. Dashboard Paste-rename reaches it through opPaste -> filerPasteModeInto(..., rename) (dash_browser.c:894, filer_browser.c:2321-2324). subfunc_Paste treats COPY_KEPT_DESTINATION as kept (filer_browser.c:2214-2216).

findings.title: ELISA Shift-JIS atlas allocates 512x1024 (512 KB) but only 864 rows hold glyphs
findings.problem: ELISA_GLYPHS is 6877; at 64 glyphs per 8-pixel row that is 108 rows = 864 texel rows, yet elisaAtlasReady memaligns, clears and uploads 512*1024 bytes and sets Height 1024. The buffer is never freed (dashFontShutdown has no caller), so after the first Japanese save title the extra rows are held in EE RAM and in the VRAM pool for the rest of the run.
findings.fix: Use a height of 864 (rows = (ELISA_GLYPHS + 63) / 64 * 8) for the memalign, memset, SyncDCache and Height; the font atlas in the same file already uses a non-power-of-two height (FONT_TEX_H 340).
findings.benefit: 512*(1024-864) = 81,920 B EE RAM and about 64 KB of VRAM pool (512 vs 448 KB in 8 KB T8 pages) once any SJIS title has been shown (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read dash_font.c:39 (55016/8 = 6877), 80-101 (memalign 512*1024, glyph row = glyph/64*8, Height 1024), 586 (v = gi/64*8, max 107*8+8 = 864). ceil(6877/64) = 108. Callers of elisaAtlasReady: dashSjisTitle only (dash_font.c:130), used by dash_card_tool.c, dash_ps1_card.c, dash_browser.c. grep dashFontShutdown: only definition and include/dash_internal.h:404. Non-power-of-two Height already used for font_tex (dash_font.c:24,284). VRAM page arithmetic is INFERRED.

findings.title: RunLoaderElfInternal: sprintf into the 256-byte stack bootpath overflows on long HDD/DVR PFS paths
findings.problem: bootpath is char[256] on the stack but sprintf writes party + ":pfs:" + the PFS path into it with no bound (elf.c:776,778,798,800). For an HDD launch main_actions.c:402-404 builds party "hddN:PART" and filename "pfs0:/rest" from a path of up to MAX_PATH (1025), so bootpath receives strlen(path)+4 bytes: any hdd0:/ ELF path of 252 or more characters overflows the stack and can corrupt locals such as handoff_path, which is dereferenced right after (elf.c:782).
findings.fix: Declare bootpath as char[MAX_PATH] (exec_target and exec_arg0 already are) and use snprintf(bootpath, sizeof(bootpath), ...) at the four sites.
findings.benefit: Closes a stack overflow on the ELF launch path; stack use +769 bytes (INFERRED: 1025-256), no code size change.
findings.evidence: Read elf.c:728-831: bootpath[256] at :730, sprintf at :776, :778, :798, :800, no length check before. Caller main_actions.c:854 RunLoaderElf(fullpath, party, path, t, x) with party/fullpath built at :402-404 by snprintf into MAX_PATH buffers from the selected path (dashboard launches reach it via dashLaunchApp -> ExecuteMainAction, dash_main.c:669). The same function serves popstarter.c:102, neutrino_iso.c:401 and ember.c:391. MAX_PATH = 1025 (include/launchelf.h:204).

findings.title: choose_custom_output_path passes keyboard(name, 36) for char name[36]; the dashboard keyboard writes one byte past the array
findings.problem: keyboard()'s max is a character count, so the buffer needs max+1 bytes (classic gui.c:249 inserts while len < max; dashboard kbInsert dash_widgets.c:345 inserts while len < max_len). name is char[36] and is passed with max 36. DashRun installs the dashboard keyboard override (dash_main.c:1358), which accepts 36 characters, and the terminating NUL is written at name[36], past the stack array. Reached when a dongle console (COH/Python) exports a signed custom ELF (2398-2399 -> export_custom_payload 1539 -> choose_custom_output_path).
findings.fix: Pass sizeof(name) - 1 to keyboard().
findings.benefit: Removes a 1-byte stack overflow (INFERRED: 36 characters + NUL = 37 bytes into char[36]). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read main_exploit_installer.c 959-1009 (name[36], keyboard(name, 36) at 981) and 2393-2403 (dongle export path). gui.c 143-164: keyboard() calls keyboardOverride when set; classic path caps at i < max && i < 33 (gui.c:249, 308), so it stays in bounds. dash_widgets.c 442-529: modalKeyboard limits max_len to 255 and calls kbInsert (341-350), which inserts while strlen < max_len and moves the NUL to len+1. classicKeyboard 663-668 forwards max unchanged; dashClassicUiInstall(1) at dash_main.c:1358 in DashRun; the installer is entered from dash_main.c:475 -> dashExploitInstaller. Other keyboard(tmp, 36) callers use MAX_PATH buffers (editor_file.c:256, filer_browser.c:1094).

findings.title: dashBgSceneClouds applies the drift direction twice: no cloud moves left and even-indexed clouds leave the screen for good (cloud 0 is never shown)
findings.problem: x = fmodf(dir * t * sp + i * 211, span) followed by x = span - x when dir < 0. While the argument is positive, span - (i*211 - t*sp) grows with t, so 'left' clouds also drift right. Once t*sp > i*211 the argument is negative, fmodf returns a negative value, and x - 180 stays in [820, 1820), off the 640-wide screen. Cloud 0 is gone at t > 0, and after about 211 s of scene time only the 4 odd clouds remain (2 of 5 in SUBTLE). Reachable by choosing the 'Drift clouds' background (dash_themes.c:114,119).
findings.fix: Drop dir from the fmodf argument (fmodf(t * sp + i * 211.0f, span)); the existing mirror then gives the intended leftward drift.
findings.benefit: Scene shows all 9 (FULL) or 5 (SUBTLE) clouds drifting both ways as designed; one-token change.
findings.evidence: Read dash_bg_ps2.c:795-822. C fmodf keeps the sign of the dividend. span = 1000 (DASH_VW 640 + 360, dash_internal.h:17). Cloud rx is at most 270 (line 812), so at x >= 820 the glow (radius rx, dash_gfx.c:815-823) starts at x >= 550 with its edge alpha, and cloud 0 (rx <= 180) never reaches the screen. Scene selectable: bg_ids/bg_names in dash_themes.c:112-119, dispatched at dash_bg.c:524-525. No test references dashBgSceneClouds (grep tests/).

findings.title: dashBgSceneClouds: clouds with dir = -1 are drawn off screen after the first minute
findings.problem: For even i, x = fmodf(-t*sp + i*211, span) becomes negative once t*sp > i*211 (immediately for i = 0, within ~53 s for i = 8); fmodf keeps the sign, so x = span - x lies in [span, 2*span) and after -180 the centre is at 820..1820 on a 640 px screen. Five of nine clouds (three of five in SUBTLE) then sit off screen and also move right instead of left. The scene is selectable as "clouds" (src/dash_themes.c:114, dispatched at src/dash_bg.c:524-525).
findings.fix: Take the modulo of the positive term, x = fmodf(t * sp + i * 211.0f, span), and keep the existing mirror (span - x) for dir < 0.
findings.benefit: Fixes a visible scene defect (more than half the clouds missing); 0 lines changed in count.
findings.evidence: Read dash_bg_ps2.c:795-822. DASH_VW 640 (include/dash_internal.h:17), span = 1000. dir = (i&1)?1:-1 so even i have dir -1; C fmodf result has the sign of the dividend. Rendered radius rx <= 270, so a centre >= 820 leaves at most a sliver at the right edge for the first ~90 px of travel, then nothing. Grep BG_CLOUDS|"clouds" in src: dash_bg.c:524, dash_bg_ps2.c:795, dash_themes.c:114.

findings.title: dash_ps1_card.c keeps 8 KB of tool-only state in .bss for the whole run
findings.problem: p1_saves, p1_titles, p1_details, p1_items and p1_head are static arrays used only while the PS1 card tool is open. The three card buffers are already allocated in p1Hold and freed in p1Drop, but these 8 KB stay resident from boot to exit.
findings.fix: Allocate these arrays in the same p1Hold memalign block as the card buffers (one larger allocation) and drop them with it in p1Drop.
findings.benefit: 8092 B of .bss returned to the heap while the tool is closed (MEASURED: evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv:74, dash_ps1_card.o .bss 8092).
findings.evidence: Read dash_ps1_card.c:29-36 and every use: p1_saves/p1_titles/p1_details/p1_items only in p1CardTool :592-653; p1_head in p1Load call :600, p1Safety :150, p1Commit :176, p1CopyAs :588. All run between p1Hold :719-731 and p1Drop :733-737 (dashPs1CardTool :739-748, dashPs1CardNew :750-759). Sizes: PS1_CARD_HEAD_MAX 3904 (mc_save_export.h:52), 15*96 + 15*64 + 17*16 (DashMenuItem dash_internal.h:902-908) + 15*sizeof(Ps1CardSave) (mc_ps1_card.h:66-74), totalling the measured 8092.

findings.title: loadConfig copies CNF values with strcpy/sprintf into fixed SETTING fields without a length bound
findings.problem: Values come straight from LAUNCHSTATION.CNF (up to the file size; the primary read path in preloadCNFFd has no cap) and are strcpy'd into MAX_PATH (1025) fields or sprintf'd into the 64-byte Misc fields. A hand-edited line longer than the field overwrites the following SETTING members at boot; a NEUTRINO_ELF value over about 1267 characters runs past the end of the malloc'd SETTING and corrupts the heap. Titles, PathPad and the SMB login in the same loop are already bounded.
findings.fix: Replace each strcpy(field, value) and sprintf(field, "%s%s", ...) here with snprintf(field, sizeof(field), ...), as the neighbouring LK_Title/PathPad/SMB branches already bound their copies. Same line count.
findings.benefit: Closes a heap/struct overflow reachable from a user-editable boot config at no size cost; INFERRED arithmetic: neutrino_file starts at offset 26916 of a ~28184-byte SETTING
findings.evidence: Read config.c:883-1112 and launchelf.h:279-340 (field sizes), launchelf.h:204 MAX_PATH = 1025. Values are produced by get_CNF_string, which only stops a value at CR/LF/NUL (config.c:148-151). preloadCNFFd primary path allocates the whole file (config.c:446-462), fallback caps at 128 KB (441, 483-503). Offset arithmetic: CNF_Path 1025 + LK_Path 17x1025 + LK_Title 17x72 + LK_Flag 68 + 16x64 Misc + 6x1025 = 26916; struct end about 28184 after the ints, colors and two 32-byte SMB fields (INFERRED, no sizeof measured). Bounded branches for comparison: 1050-1053, 1088-1089, 1098-1099.

findings.title: makeicon: tex_compresRLE copies its result into a second malloc, and the texture buffer is never freed (leak per icon)
findings.problem: tex_compresRLE mallocs a 32 KB output buffer, then mallocs a second buffer of the compressed size, copies into it and frees the first. make_icon returns on every path (success 364, errors 344/368) without freeing tex_buffer, so each folder icon created through filerCreateFolderIcon (filer_browser.c:2455) leaks the compressed texture; the next call overwrites the pointer. None of the three mallocs is checked (memset/write on NULL at 338/246).
findings.fix: In tex_compresRLE free the old tex_buffer and keep new_tex as tex_buffer (no second malloc or memcpy). Free tex_buffer (and set it to NULL) before every return in make_icon, and return -1 if a malloc fails.
findings.justification: The leak is real on every icon creation, and the NULL checks guard the only allocations in this path; the change is a few lines and removes one malloc and a copy.
findings.benefit: Fixes a leak of the RLE texture (a few KB, INFERRED from 16384 u16 pixels of mostly black runs) per icon written; removes one transient malloc and memcpy per icon.
findings.evidence: Read makeicon.c:236-256 and 337-368: tex_buffer assigned at 252 and 337, freed only at 251 inside tex_compresRLE; no free in make_icon. Grep tex_buffer: only makeicon.c. Callers of make_icon: filer_browser.c:1497 and 2455 (filerCreateFolderIcon).

findings.title: showDetails: len += snprintf can exceed body[640], then sizeof(body)-len underflows and the Metadata line is written past the stack buffer
findings.problem: Each append adds snprintf's would-be length. Worst case: Location+File 320 (dev 47, path 255), Author 48, Version 33, Category 34, Artwork 265 (art 255) = 700 > 640. Line 134 then calls snprintf(body + 700, (size_t)(640 - 700), ...), a huge size, writing up to 289 bytes past body on the UI-thread stack. Trigger: Details on an app with path+art lengths of about 450-600 chars (deep USB/HDD folder or an absolute cover= in title.cfg) and filled author/version/category.
findings.fix: Enlarge body to 1024 bytes: every field is bounded (worst case 700 + 288 Metadata line + NUL = 989), so no append can pass the end and the arithmetic cannot underflow.
findings.justification: Changes one constant; costs 384 bytes of UI-thread stack while the Details dialog is built. Smaller than adding a clamp after each of the six appends.
findings.benefit: Removes a stack buffer overflow (crash) on rare long paths; no code added (INFERRED: arithmetic from DashApp field sizes).
findings.evidence: Field sizes from include/dash_internal.h:34-37,692-698 (path/art 256, author 40, version/category 24). dev[48] filled by dashLibDeviceLabel (dash_lib.c:167-227, longest 'Internal HDD: '+39 chars, truncated to 47). meta from dashLibMetadataPath (dash_lib.c:363-369, dir <=255 + 'title.cfg'). art reaches FOUND only below 256 chars (dash_art.c:371, dash_lib.c:572 via nextField). cover= with ':' is copied as given (dash_lib.c:318-319). Reachable from dashAppActions case 4 (dash_apps.c:285-287).

findings.title: Active MMCE backup/export name buffers (40 and 48 bytes) truncate the no-RTC stamp: names lose .mcd/.ps2 and later backups are refused
findings.problem: When sceCdReadClock fails or stat != 0, the stamp is 00000000-000000-S plus 10 digits of Timer()/1000 (27 chars). MMCE0-ActiveCard-<stamp>.mcd is then 48 chars but name[40] keeps 39: the extension and the last 5 digits are cut, and because Timer() counts ms since boot the kept digits are 00000 for the first 27.7 hours. The first backup is written with no .mcd, so activeHistoryMatch never sees it (no dedupe, no pruning); every later attempt truncates all 100 suffixes to the same existing name and fails with 'Could not create a unique backup history name'. The PCSX2 export (name[48]) loses the final '2' and writes a .ps file.
findings.fix: Declare both name buffers as char name[MAX_NAME] (dash_browser.c:1557 and 1627). Nothing else changes.
findings.benefit: Fixes blocked active-card backups and wrongly named exports on consoles without a valid RTC reading; no lines added (INFERRED how often the RTC read fails; the code at 1272-1273 says it must still work).
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c:1262-1341 (stamp, history match, stamped names) and callers 1555-1573 (name[40], activeHistoryName) and 1625-1644 (name[48], ext ps2). Length arithmetic: prefix 'MMCE0-ActiveCard-' = 17, fallback stamp 17 + 10 digits = 27, '.mcd' = 4 -> 48 chars + NUL; RTC stamp is 15 chars so the RTC path just fits (17+15+3+4 = 39). Timer() returns ms since boot (src/timer.c:8-11). activeHistoryMatch (1290-1302) requires a '.mcd' extension. mmce_backup.c:50-71 builds the same stamp for its own history. Frequency of a failing RTC read on real consoles is INFERRED.

findings.title: Classic TextEditor: per-keystroke buffer leak, unbounded row table, mark-delete underflow and unchecked save writes (editor appears unreachable)
findings.problem: Each inserted char mallocs a new text buffer but the free of the old one sits inside a comment (editor_input.c:372,647), leaking TextSize+256 bytes per key until malloc returns NULL and strcpy crashes. editor_rules.c:26 writes Editor_nRowsWidth[Editor_nRowsNum] unbounded; the array has 2048 entries (editor.c:11) and 512 KB files are accepted. Deleting a mark made right-to-left uses del1=-MARK_SIZE from the cursor at the low end, writing before the buffer and strcat-overflowing it. Saves ignore genWrite after O_TRUNC and report success. INFERRED unreachable: the dashboard sends MISC/TextEditor to dash_editor.c.
findings.fix: Delete the classic editor together with the dead-code finding for it (dash_editor.c replaced it; dash_main.c:470-472). Only if it is kept: un-comment the free at editor_input.c:372 and :647, stop adding rows at MAX_ENTRY in editor_rules.c:26, compute mark deletes from Mark[MARK_IN] instead of Editor_Cur, and treat a short genWrite as a failed save.
findings.justification: Only for the keep-it fallback: each check closes one cited leak or overwrite with a one-line bound or comparison; deletion adds nothing.
findings.benefit: If deleted: lines counted by the dead-code finding, 0 here. If kept: removes a whole-buffer leak per keystroke, two heap/.bss overwrites and a silent truncation of the saved file (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: TextEditor callers: main_actions.c:231 (executeBrowserSelection), :771 (Misc_TextEditor), filer_browser.c:1554 (classic browser R1 menu, only when cnfmode is FALSE, filer_browser.c:1293). getFilePath(..,FALSE) only at main_actions.c:221,234,738,774,886; ExecuteBrowserFrom has no caller. dashRunMisc intercepts MISC/TextEditor and MISC/FileBrowser (dash_main.c:466-473) before runMiscCommand -> ExecuteMainAction; runLaunchKey and the PC command poll pass only ':' paths to dashLaunchApp (dash_main.c:965, 787). Remaining route: Execute(dashCfg.igr_after_path) main.c:240 with a hand-edited DASHBOARD.CNF. MAX_ENTRY = 2048 (include/launchelf.h:205); 512 KB limit editor_file.c:90.

findings.title: First-run welcome dialog opens during the auto-launch countdown, which then cannot be cancelled
findings.problem: The intro check uses boot_phase != 1, so it fires while boot_phase is 2 (auto-launch countdown). dashModalMessage blocks and takes all input, so 'Press any button to stay' (bootUpdate needs in->any) cannot cancel, while bootDraw keeps showing the countdown underneath. If the user reads past the deadline, the auto key launches on the next frame after the dialog closes. Trigger: from_boot with LK_Path[SETTING_LK_AUTO] set and intro_done 0, i.e. first boot with an existing auto-launch config, or after 'show welcome again' (dash_settings.c:3295-3298).
findings.fix: Show the welcome only when boot_phase is 0 (change the condition to !boot_phase), so it appears after the countdown is cancelled, or not at all when the auto launch happens.
findings.benefit: Auto-launch countdown stays cancellable on the first boot (minor bug fixed, no size change).
findings.evidence: boot_phase is file-static; every use read in dash_main.c (:39, :741, :772, :868, :1072-1153, :1411-1426, :1486, :1517, :1527), none in modal code. bootBegin :1084-1087 sets phase 2 when Init_Delay is 0 and LK auto is set; :1114-1117 after the delay. bootUpdate :1119-1126 cancels only on in->any from the main loop. dashRenderScene :1216 calls bootDraw, so the countdown is drawn under modals. intro_done defaults to 0 (dash_store.c:248). Whether the closing button press is flushed was not traced, hence Med.

findings.title: copy() re-prepares both device stacks for every nested file and folder; on host: each call costs 2-3 PC round trips
findings.problem: subfunc_Paste prepares the source and destination stacks once (filer_browser.c:2164), yet copy() calls prepareTransferDeviceStacks again at every recursion level, once per copied file and folder. For host: that runs initHOST(), which opens host:elflist.txt and, when it is absent, opens and closes the host: directory: 2-3 blocking network requests per entry on the UI thread, and a transient failure there aborts the copy midway. getFileSize() and delete() call ensurePathDeviceStackReady per entry the same way.
findings.fix: Call prepareTransferDeviceStacks in copy() only when recurses == 0 (once per clipboard item); nested levels use the same two devices. getFileSize() and delete() can leave the check to their top-level callers.
findings.benefit: Removes 2-3 host: requests per nested entry: a 1000-file host: copy saves about 2000-3000 requests, seconds of UI-thread time (INFERRED at ~1 ms per LAN round trip); other devices only save flag checks.
findings.evidence: Read filer_device.c:105-228: for host: ensurePathDeviceStackReady calls initHOST(); other devices are flag checks (loadHddModules init.c:2663-2670, isSmbDriverLoaded init.c:998-1002, loadUsbModules init.c:1740-1757). filer.c:1720-1737: initHOST = load_ps2host + fileXioOpen(host:elflist.txt), else fileXioDopen/Dclose(host:). The only level-0 caller of copy() is subfunc_Paste (filer_browser.c:2208), which already called prepareTransferDeviceStacks at 2164. Child levels pass the parent's in/out, same device prefixes (filer_copy.c:1117-1118). copy() runs on the UI thread (opPaste, dash_browser.c:877-894). readHOST also calls initHOST per listing (filer.c:1747), twice per copied folder.

findings.title: dashDevicesStart keeps using the caller's DashDevice after dashWorkerAwaitAll, which can rebuild the File Browser device array under it
findings.problem: The File Browser root passes d = &fb.devs[fb.sel] to dashDevicesStart (dash_browser.c:679,694). startSync(dev->mount) first calls dashWorkerAwaitAll, whose pump runs completion callbacks on the UI thread; usbMaskRescanDone (when a late second USB drive appears) and dashNetConfigWarmDone both call dashBrowserRefreshRoot, which re-runs openDir("") and overwrites fb.devs in place. probeMount then reads the mount string from the overwritten slot, so a row shifted by the new USB row is probed instead of the one the user chose (for example MX4SIO instead of iLink, which also switches the SIO2 stack). dash_browser.c:689 already notes that openDir rebuilds fb.devs, but only the browse path is copied.
findings.fix: At the top of dashDevicesStart copy *dev into a local DashDevice and use the copy for the title, the UDPFS check, startSync and the callback.
findings.justification: Adds one local copy (188 bytes of stack) and changes four dev-> uses; it closes a real wrong-device probe that the caller's existing path copy does not cover, and is smaller than making every caller pass a copy.
findings.benefit: Fixes a wrong-driver load and possible unwanted MMCE/MX4SIO stack switch in a boot/after-misc-command timing window; net 0 lines (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c:670-709 (activate passes &fb.devs[fb.sel]), dash_devices.c:723-773 (startSync awaits before probeMount(mount)), dash_worker.c:221-229, 251-257, 298-310, 340-344 (await pumps finish() which runs done callbacks), dash_devices.c:99-112,178-182 (rescan job submitted every 500 ms until hotplug is armed; done callback refreshes root), dash_main.c:1242-1246,1303 (net config warm done refreshes root), dash_browser.c:475-521,3573-3583 (root refresh rewrites fb.devs via dashDevicesList). grep 'fb.ndevs = ' and 'dashBrowserRefreshRoot()' over src: only those writers. Reachability depends on a USB mask change or the boot net-config job finishing during the await (timing not reproduced on hardware).

findings.title: dashPngDecode does a 64-bit division per source pixel to map columns and rows
findings.problem: dx = (u64)x * dw / w is computed for every source pixel (and dy per row). The R5900 has no 64-bit divide, so each one is a __udivdi3 call (the builtin is linked into the ELF). A 2048x2048 PNG means about 4.2 million calls. That time lands on the worker (art, theme) or on the UI thread behind the loading overlay (image viewer, dash_image.c:111). The operands never need 64 bits: x, y < 2048 and dw <= w, dh <= h <= 2048, so the products stay below 2^22.
findings.fix: Use 32-bit unsigned arithmetic for dx and dy (drop the u64 casts). Optionally hoist dx into a per-column table computed once per image.
findings.benefit: Removes one 64-bit division call per source pixel: about 4.2M calls for a 2048x2048 image, 1M for 1024x1024 (INFERRED; per-call cycle cost not measured).
findings.evidence: Read dash_png.c:93-203: w,h <= DASH_PNG_MAX_DIM 2048 (:16, :93); dw/dh only shrink (:115-128). evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-archive-members.tsv:181 shows __udivdi3 from libclang_rt.builtins-mips64el.a linked into wLaunchELF (first requester main_title.o). That dash_png.o calls it for these lines is INFERRED from the u64 operands and the R5900 lacking DDIVU; no disassembly was available. Callers and threads: dash_art.c:343/513 (worker jobs), dash_image.c:111 (UI thread with dashLoadingBegin).

findings.title: dashTextFit and textWrap re-measure text quadratically on every frame
findings.problem: When a label does not fit, dashTextFit tries each cut from the full length downward and for every cut re-runs glyphPrefixLength and dashTextWidthN over the whole prefix (O(n^2)); textWrap calls dashTextWidthN from the line start for every byte (O(L^2) per line). Both run on the UI thread every frame: one dashTextFit per non-selected file-browser row (dash_browser.c:3363), list rows in settings/tools/apps, and dashTextWrap bodies in modals (dash_ui.c:1218). A 100-byte name fitting 40 characters costs about 60 iterations of ~140 glyph steps.
findings.fix: Measure once going forward: in dashTextFit accumulate glyph advances and stop at the last glyph boundary where width + ellipsis fits; in textWrap keep a running line width and add only the newly completed glyph's advance per step.
findings.benefit: Per-call cost from O(n^2) to O(n); roughly 10k glyph steps saved per overflowing row per frame (INFERRED from the loop structure, not timed)
findings.evidence: Read dash_font.c:506-545 (dashTextWidthN and glyphPrefixLength both walk from the start), 688-715 (cut loop calls both per cut), 785-830 (inner loop calls dashTextWidthN(line_start, q-line_start+1) per byte). Per-frame callers checked: dash_browser.c:3357-3363 (per row in the list draw), dash_ui.c:1218 (modal body), plus 70+ other dashTextFit/dashTextWrap call sites in dash_*.c draw code (grep count). Cycle cost not measured.

findings.title: delete() and getFileSize() allocate a full 2048-entry listing (~0.9 MB) per recursion level, so deep trees fail with -ENOMEM partway
findings.problem: Each folder level of delete() memaligns (MAX_ENTRY+1) FILEINFO and getFileSize() MAX_ENTRY FILEINFO, kept for the whole subtree (the comments at 310 and 1981 say about 900 KB). The heap is at most ~25 MB, so a folder chain about 20-28 levels deep runs out: delete returns -ENOMEM after removing everything it reached first, and every retry stops at the same depth, so such a tree can never be deleted from the console. Reached from the dashboard Delete (dash_browser.c:1100) and Get Size (dash_browser.c:1183).
findings.fix: Let delete() list a small batch per level (for example 64 entries, ~28 KB) by passing a capacity to getDirComplete/listDir. delete() already re-lists a folder until it is empty (the do/while on more at 1988-2004, with the files[MAX_ENTRY] progress sentinel moved to files[capacity]), so only the allocation size and the sentinel index change. getFileSize() cannot re-list, so it can keep the full listing; it already reports 'At least ... error -12'.
findings.justification: Adds only a capacity argument to the existing listing call. It removes a real depth limit on delete and cuts the per-level heap from ~0.9 MB to ~28 KB, reusing the re-list loop delete() already has.
findings.benefit: Deletes trees of any depth; peak heap per level ~0.9 MB -> ~28 KB (INFERRED: 2048 x FILEINFO, 'about 900 KB' per comment at 310/1981; heap <= 25.46 MB per BUILD-EVIDENCE.md section 7, itself INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read filer_actions.c:298-369 and 1944-2047. getDirComplete (filer.c:2246-2266) lists up to MAX_ENTRY-1 entries and sets *more; MAX_ENTRY=2048, MAX_NAME=256 (launchelf.h:201-205); FILEINFO = name[256] + title[66] + sceMcTblGetDir (launchelf.h:560-565). Callers: dash_browser.c:1100 (opDelete, stops on first ret<0 and shows 'Not everything could be deleted'), dash_browser.c:1183 (Get Size), filer_browser.c:1372/1389/2042, filer_copy.c:1080. Heap: evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:200-207 (_heap_size=-1, ~25.46 MB max, INFERRED). Exact depth at which memalign fails depends on runtime allocations and was not measured.

findings.title: readHOST elflist.txt parser drops the last entry of a list without a trailing newline and can overrun FILEINFO.name
findings.problem: The parser ends the buffer with a synthetic newline (1782) and returns hostcount - 1 (1804), which only cancels the empty entry made when the file itself ends with a newline (an empty line opens as the folder host:). A list without a trailing newline loses its last ELF, every blank line adds a nameless folder, and a list with no valid line returns -1. Lines are buffered up to MAX_PATH-1 characters (1799) and makeFslPath copies up to 1024 bytes into info[].name, which is 256 bytes, so a line over 255 characters that opens overruns the entry's title and stats.
findings.fix: Skip empty lines, return hostcount, and cap a buffered line at sizeof(info->name) - 1 characters (ps2host truncates paths to 255 anyway, iop/ps2host/hostlink.h:68).
findings.benefit: Correct elflist.txt listings (last ELF no longer hidden, no blank entries) and no name overrun; no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence:
Read filer.c:1740-1805: trace 'a
b' (no final newline): lines a, b -> hostcount 2 -> returns 1. 'a
b
': third empty line -> host_path 'host:' -> fileXioDopen('host:') -> nameless folder -> returns 2. That Dopen('host:') succeeds is INFERRED from initHOST (1731-1734) and the root branch (1807), which rely on it. FILEINFO.name is char[MAX_NAME] (launchelf.h:562, MAX_NAME 256 at :201); makeFslPath bound MAX_PATH-1 (1687). readHOST reached from listDir (2051-2052) for host: paths. git log -S 'return hostcount - 1': from the initial import 944a2fc.

findings.title: scanRun queries HDIOC_STATUS three times and, on the first scan, libhdd walks the whole APA table before scanRun walks it again
findings.problem: scanRun reads HDIOC_STATUS into j->status, then calls hddCheckPresent and hddCheckFormatted, which each issue the same devctl again; on the first call of the run hddStatusCurrent is 0, so hddUpdateInfo also Dopen/Dreads every APA header (one disk read per partition segment, the driver caches only a few headers, iop/ps2hdd_osd/hdd.c:218) right before scanRun's own identical walk (172-208). Runs on the worker behind 'Reading the HDD'.
findings.fix: Derive both flags from j->status as libhdd does: present = status >= 0 && status < 3, formatted = status == 0, and drop the two libhdd calls. hddMakeFilesystem/hddFormat still call hddUpdateInfo themselves when needed (libhdd.c:306-307, 116-117).
findings.benefit: Two devctl RPCs per scan and one full header walk on the first open per run; with hundreds of HDL partitions that is likely seconds of extra wait (INFERRED, not measured)
findings.evidence: Read dash_hdd.c:151-156 and 167-209; libhdd.c:75-102 (both helpers call hddUpdateInfo when !hddStatusCurrent, then HDIOC_STATUS; present = 0..2, formatted = 0), 262-293 (Dopen hdd0: + Dread loop). grep hddCheckPresent|hddCheckFormatted|hddGetInfo over src/: only dash_hdd.c:152,155, so the first scan is the first libhdd call. hdd_fio.c:760-777 Dread reads headers via apaCacheGetHeader; hdd.c:218 cacheSize=3. The time per header read is not measured.

findings.title: wipe_mc_folder_contents loops forever when a nested sub-folder path is longer than 63 characters
findings.problem: For a sub-folder entry wipe_mc_folder_contents calls wipe_mc_folder (1217), which first calls mc_folder_exists. That helper builds 'mcN:/<path>' in a 64-byte buffer and returns 0 ('missing') when snprintf truncates (1102-1103), so wipe_mc_folder returns 0 without deleting (1235-1236). The loop handles only the first entry per pass (break at 1223), rescans (1199-1201), gets the same sub-folder again and never ends. Trigger: Delete update folders on a card where an update folder holds a two-level sub-folder tree longer than 63 characters. It runs on the dashboard UI thread (dash_exploit.c:160), so the console hangs.
findings.fix: In the sub-folder branch call wipe_mc_folder_contents(port, child) and then delete_mc_path(port, child) directly: mcGetDir has just listed the entry, so the existence check and its 64-byte path are not needed there.
findings.benefit: Removes a possible permanent UI hang during the exploit install, and saves one fileXioDopen per sub-folder (INFERRED). Net lines about 0.
findings.evidence: Read 1097-1110, 1184-1244 and the call path wipe_existing_update_folders 1246-1266 <- prepare_needed_folders 1650-1654 <- install_selected_ps2_updates 1967 <- install_for_plan 2491. Path arithmetic: 'mc0:/' (5) + 'BIEXEC-SYSTEM' (13) + '/' + a + '/' + b + NUL > 64 when a + b >= 44; MC names allow up to 31 characters each, so the first level always fits and depth 2 can overflow. genDopen (filer_fileops.c:615-676) is a plain fileXioDopen for mc paths, so the false 'missing' comes from the truncation or a dopen error. Confidence Med because nested folders inside B?EXEC-SYSTEM are unusual.

findings.title: iconSdf is 30 KB of -O2 code that runs only once at start-up
findings.problem: The rasterizer switch iconSdf makes up 30,060 of the 37,192 B .text of dash_icons.o; it has about 234 calls to small SDF helpers (sdSeg 104, sdBox 44, sdCircle 29, sdTriP 19, sdBoxOutline 17, sdRing 15), and the main target is compiled at -O2, so the helpers are expected to be inlined at each call site. The code runs only inside dashIconsInit, once per boot.
findings.fix: Mark iconSdf (and dashIconsInit) __attribute__((cold)), which both GCC and Clang compile for size, or mark sdTri/sdBox/sdSeg noinline. Keep it only if a build shows a real .text drop.
findings.justification: Adds one attribute; it targets a measured 30 KB start-up-only function, and optimizing it for size is the cheapest way to shrink it without rewriting the icon set. The cost is slightly slower rasterization at boot.
findings.benefit: iconSdf 30,060 B .text MEASURED (sizes tsv); the saving is INFERRED (estimated several KB of ELF and RAM) and was not built; the boot-time cost is also not measured.
findings.evidence: evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:83 and sizes tsv: 30060 .text iconSdf; BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:88: dash_icons.o .text 37,192; BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:107: wLaunchELF objects compiled with -O2 (no opt in ps2.yaml:485-641). Call-site counts from sed over dash_icons.c:274-752. iconSdf callers: dash_icons.c:794 and 825 only, inside initClipboardIcons/dashIconsInit; dashIconsInit is called once from dash_main.c:1287 and returns early once icons_ready is set (dash_icons.c:807). Inlining was not confirmed by disassembly.

findings.title: runLaunchKey writes the launch-key title into the shared library entry
findings.problem: dashLibResolve returns &dashApps[i] when the ELF is in the library, and runLaunchKey then copies setting->LK_Title over a->title. After a boot or SELECT+button launch through a titled key, the library entry keeps the key's title (shown on Home/Applications, out of title sort order) if the launch fails. If dashLaunchApp saves the cache (dash_main.c:647-648, art dirty), dashLibBuildCache writes that title to DASHLIB.CNF and it survives reboots until a rescan.
findings.fix: Apply the title to a copy: when dashLibResolve returned a library entry, memcpy it into tmp first and set tmp.title, then launch &tmp (dashLaunchApp already works on its own copy).
findings.justification: Adds one memcpy. It is the smallest change that keeps a per-key label from overwriting the library title in RAM and in DASHLIB.CNF.
findings.benefit: Library titles and DASHLIB.CNF no longer pick up launch-key labels (minor persistent display bug fixed).
findings.evidence: Read dash_main.c:959-972 (runLaunchKey), :1072-1128 (callers from boot), :979-1019 (quick launch caller). dash_lib.c:454-482: dashLibFind returns &dashApps[i], dashLibResolve returns it before using transient. dash_lib.c:604-640: dashLibSaveCache marks SAVE_CACHE dirty; dashLibBuildCache writes a->title; dashLibLoadCache :583-601 reads it back and sorts by title (titleCmp :484-490). dashLaunchApp :601 copies the app, so launching from a copy changes nothing else.

findings.title: dashPickPath memset resets pk.gen, so a listing job left over from the previous picker session is applied to the new one
findings.problem: pickListDone applies a listing when pk.active and j->gen == pk.gen. Exiting the picker with a listing still in flight (Triangle while a slow device is read) bumps gen, but the next dashPickPath memsets pk, restarting gen at 0, so the old job's gen can equal the new session's gen. The worker runs jobs FIFO, so the old listing completes first: pk.entries are filled with the previous folder's names under the new pk.dir and pk.loading is cleared until the new job finishes; choosing an entry then returns pk.dir + a name from another folder (dash_widgets.c:1225-1236).
findings.fix: Keep the generation across sessions: save pk.gen before the memset at line 1099 and restore it after, so the counter never restarts.
findings.justification: Two-line change; it makes the existing stale-listing guard (comment at line 1340) hold across picker sessions instead of only within one.
findings.benefit: Removes a wrong-path selection window after reopening the picker while a previous listing is still queued or running (INFERRED, timing-dependent).
findings.evidence: Read dash_widgets.c:922-955 (gen check at 927, entries filled 936-949, loading=0 at 951), pickOpen 968-1032 (pk.gen++ at 972, job gets j->gen = pk.gen at 1022, submitted to the worker at 1026), dashPickPath 1097-1105 (memset(&pk) at 1099) and exit 1340-1344 (pk.gen++ then free). dash_worker.c:209-258: one job at a time, FIFO queue, completion callbacks run from dashWorkerPump, called at the end of dashGfxPresent (dash_gfx.c:446), so a callback from the old session can run inside the new session's frame loop. Example: old session gen 1 device list, gen 2 job for mass0:/ in flight, Triangle; new session gen 1 device list, user opens mc0:/ (gen 2, queued behind the old job).

findings.title: genFixPath sprintf into party[MAX_NAME] overflows the stack for an hdd0:/ or dvr_hdd0:/ path whose partition part exceeds about 250 characters
findings.problem: loc_path (MAX_PATH) takes everything after 'hddN:/', is cut at the next '/', and sprintf(party, "%s%s", hdd_device, loc_path) (1062) or "dvr_hdd0:%s" (1090) writes it into the 256-byte stack buffer party without a bound. APA names are at most 32 characters, so only hand-edited or corrupted text reaches it, for example LAUNCHSTATION.CNF LANG_FILE or CNF_Path (MAX_PATH fields copied by config.c:1048,1059) passed to genFixPath at boot by lang.c:472 and main_modules.c:13.
findings.fix: Use snprintf(party, sizeof(party), ...) at both sites and return -1 (bad path) when the result does not fit.
findings.justification: Adds one length comparison per site; it closes a stack overflow reachable from config text, and a partition name that long cannot exist, so failing the path is correct.
findings.benefit: Removes a boot-time stack overflow on a malformed config path; about 2 lines added (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read filer.c:946-1107: party[MAX_NAME] (948, MAX_NAME 256 at launchelf.h:201), loc_path from uLE_path + 6 (1051) or + 10 (1079), sprintf at 1062 and 1090. uLE_related copies non-uLE paths unchanged (main_fileops.c:51-53). Config fields CNF_Path/lang_file are char[MAX_PATH] (launchelf.h:281,303), filled by strcpy at config.c:1048,1059; callers genFixPath(setting->lang_file) lang.c:472 and genFixPath(setting->CNF_Path) main_modules.c:13.

findings.title: recoverCardFromPath prepares device stacks after the folder picker without waiting for the picker's in-flight listing job
findings.problem: Every other op calls prepareOp() (wait for the worker) after dashPickPath, but recoverCardFromPath calls it before (2224) and then, after the picker, does UI-thread IO (recoveryTargetPath: up to 999 x 2 wleExists) and prepareTransferDeviceStacks, which can load drivers or reload stacks. dashPickPath can return while its own folder listing is still running on the worker (dash_widgets.c:1340: 'a listing still in flight ... frees itself'), e.g. when 'Use this folder' is chosen right after opening a slow SMB/HDD folder, breaking the worker rule in dash_worker.c:7-17. opBackupActiveMmce, opExportActiveMmcePcsx2, opBackupCard and opConvertCard similarly stat the destination after the picker but before prepareOp.
findings.fix: In recoverCardFromPath call prepareOp() again right after dashPickPath returns; in the four other ops move the existing prepareOp() call above the wleExists/name checks that follow the picker.
findings.justification: One added call in recoverCardFromPath; it closes the one path in this file that can start or reload IOP drivers while a worker listing may still be reading.
findings.benefit: Removes a rare race between a worker folder read and driver/stack preparation on the UI thread; +2 lines, the other four are reorders.
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c:2208-2289 and the other ops at 1492-1517, 1555-1585, 1625-1656, 1678-1715, 1740-1781 (prepareOp after the picker, wleExists before it in four). dash_widgets.c:1087-1110, 1191-1217 (Use this folder returns at once, even while pk.loading) and 1340-1346. dash_widgets.c:997-1003 shows the picker itself awaits the worker before preparing a device. filer_device.c:178-218: prepareTransferDeviceStacks calls ensurePathDeviceStackReady, which loads USB/MMCE/ATA modules and may reload the source stack. Whether a concurrent fileXio call or driver load actually corrupts the in-flight read is INFERRED.

findings.title: dashPngDecode leaks the interlaced full-image buffer and row table when libpng fails mid-image
findings.problem: For interlaced images the decoder mallocs full (w*h*4, up to 256*256*4 = 256 KB) and rows (h pointers) as plain locals. A corrupt or truncated interlaced PNG makes png_read_image call png_error, pngErr longjmps to the handler at :77-84, which frees only row, acc, acc_n and dst. full and rows are lost. Covers, theme images and files opened in the image viewer come from user devices, and each failed open leaks again.
findings.fix: Declare full and rows with the other volatile pointers at the top of the function and free them in the setjmp handler, setting them to NULL after their normal frees.
findings.justification: Adds two frees and two declarations. Without them each corrupt interlaced PNG leaks up to 257 KB of EE heap per decode attempt (image viewer re-opens, slideshow over a folder). Freeing in the existing handler is the smallest fix.
findings.benefit: Up to 256 KB + 8 KB (rows) of EE heap no longer leaked per failed interlaced decode (INFERRED: w*h <= 65536 enforced at :96, 4 bytes per pixel; h <= 2048 pointers).
findings.evidence: Read dash_png.c:43-224. pngErr :43-47 longjmps; png_read_image :153 runs after full/rows are allocated at :141/:146 and before free(rows) :154 / free(full) :178. Handler :77-84 frees only row/acc/acc_n/dst. Callers: dash_art.c:343 (artRun worker job), dash_art.c:513 (themeTexRun worker job), dash_image.c:111 (image viewer, UI thread); grep dashPngLoadFile/dashPngDecode over src include: no other callers.

findings.title: dash_png.c leaks the interlaced full-image buffer and row table when libpng longjmps inside png_read_image
findings.problem: full (up to 256*256*4 = 256 KB) and rows are block-local, non-volatile and not freed by the setjmp handler, which frees only row/acc/acc_n/dst. A truncated or CRC-damaged interlaced PNG up to 256x256 used as cover/artwork makes pngReadMem or libpng call png_error during png_read_image, and both buffers leak on every such decode (dash_art.c:343/513, dash_image.c:111).
findings.fix: Declare full and rows at function scope as volatile pointers initialised to NULL and free them in the setjmp handler (and set them NULL after the normal frees). Fold this into the loop merge of finding 4.
findings.justification: Adds about 3 lines; it is the smallest change that stops a leak of up to ~257 KB of EE heap per damaged interlaced image, which accumulates across art loads.
findings.benefit: Stops a leak of w*h*4 + h*4 bytes (<= 257 KB, INFERRED from the 256*256 cap at line 96) per failed interlaced decode.
findings.evidence: Read dash_png.c:25-35 (png_error on truncated input), 43-47 (error handler longjmps), 77-84 (handler frees only row/acc/acc_n/dst), 139-154 (full/rows locals, png_read_image). Callers: dash_art.c:343, 513 and dash_image.c:111 via dashPngLoadFile.

findings.title: Safety copies are numbered and pruned by base name only, so same-named images share one sequence and delete each other's copies
findings.problem: ctSafetyCopyOf names copies <base>-NNNN.mcd, where base is the image name without extension cut to 47 chars, and the prune keeps 10 across all files matching that base. Images 'X.mcd' and 'X.bin' (or X.vmc/.mc2) in one folder share a sequence on any device. On MMCE all images use one folder, mmceN:/WLE-Safety/, so same-named images in different folders collide too; ctSplitGameId itself makes WLE-GameID/<source>/<ID>/<ID>-1.mcd for each source card. Ten writes to one image delete every safety copy of the other, and the names do not say which card a copy is from.
findings.fix: Make the base unique per image: keep the full file name including its extension (drop the dot strip at 275-276), and on MMCE also add a short hash of the full image path. Then numbering and pruning see only that image's copies.
findings.justification: Adds a few lines (a path hash for MMCE). The concrete problem is that the 'keep the newest 10 safety copies of this card' guarantee breaks for same-named images: older verified copies of another card are deleted. A per-image base fixes it with no new folder layout.
findings.benefit: Stops one card's writes from pruning another card's safety copies; about 3 net lines added (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read ctSafetyFolder 233-245 (MMCE: fixed mmce%d:/WLE-Safety/, else the image's own folder), ctSafetyNumber 248-260 (matches by base prefix plus 4 digits plus .mcd), ctSafetyCopyOf 266-336 (base = name minus extension, max 47 chars; high = max number over the folder; prune loop deletes the lowest number while count > CT_SAFETY_KEEP=10). Every write path calls it via ctSafetyOnce (379-389). ctSplitGameId 1281-1284 and 1312-1313 make <ID>-1.mcd under a per-source folder on the same MMCE unit. ctAllCandidate 1653-1654 accepts MCD/PS2/VMC/MC2/BIN, so same-base images in one folder are plausible. How often users hit this is INFERRED.

findings.title: PrepareMbrLaunchPayload reads xosdmain into fixed RAM at 0x01000000 that Launchstation's own heap and stack may occupy
findings.problem: The payload is read straight into RAM from 0x01000000 up to the end of EE RAM (elf.c:669-687) before the launch is committed. The app heap runs from _end (0x797bd4) to the stack with _heap_size=-1, so any heap block (live, or free with bin pointers) above 16 MB is overwritten; the failure paths after the read (secrman load/SecrInit/decrypt, elf.c:698-711; CleanUpForKeepIopExec cancel, main_actions.c:389) return to the dashboard with that memory corrupted. A payload larger than about 16 MB - 128 KB would also overwrite the main-thread stack at the top of RAM during the read loop.
findings.fix: Before reading, return -1 when the heap break (sbrk(0)) is above MBR_PAYLOAD_LOAD_ADDR, and cap payload_size64 so the read ends below the main-thread stack instead of at GetMemorySize().
findings.justification: The fixed address has to stay (loader.c preserves that window and the target ELF loads low), so the only way to avoid clobbering live heap and the stack is to refuse when the heap already reaches the window; two comparisons on an existing error path, no new code path.
findings.benefit: Prevents heap/stack corruption on PSX xosdmain launches that fail or are cancelled after the read (INFERRED: needs more than ~8.4 MB of heap in use). About +3 lines.
findings.evidence: Read elf.c:648-716 and the only caller main_actions.c:378-394 (PSX only; isMbrLaunchPath main_actions.c:109-115 = xfrom:/BIEXEC-SYSTEM/xosdmain[.elf] or hdd0:__system:pfs:/BIEXEC-SYSTEM/xosdmain.elf). evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md section 7: _heap_size = -1, _end = 0x797bd4, heap estimate subtracts a 128 KB main stack at the top of RAM. loader/loader.c:199-226 parses mem: and preserves that region. INFERRED part: heap usage at launch time was not measured, so whether blocks exist above 16 MB is not shown.

findings.title: Apps screen treats dashStoreToggleFavorite/TogglePinned failure (-1, list full) as a removal and shows 'Removed from Favorites'/'Unpinned'
findings.problem: Both toggles return -1 when 48 entries already exist (DASH_MAX_FAV) and change nothing. dash_apps.c tests only r > 0, so -1 shows 'Removed from Favorites' or 'Unpinned from Home'. Home handles the same return correctly with 'Favorites full' (dash_home.c:318-320). Trigger: 48 favorites, press Square (or Options > Add to Favorites / Pin to Home) on a non-favorite app.
findings.fix: At the three call sites, show 'Favorites full' (or 'Pins full') when r < 0, as dash_home.c:319-320 does.
findings.justification: Adds one branch per site; the current message tells the user an app was removed when nothing changed.
findings.benefit: Correct feedback when the list is full; about 4 lines added.
findings.evidence: Read dash_store.c:807-833 (return -1 when nfav/npin >= DASH_MAX_FAV, return idx < 0 otherwise); DASH_MAX_FAV 48 at dash_internal.h:42. Grep dashStoreToggle(Favorite|Pinned) over src: dash_apps.c:278,282,454 (r > 0 only) and dash_home.c:318 (handles r < 0).

findings.title: copy() and filerGetGameTitle() join paths into 1025-byte stack buffers with sprintf/strcat and no length check
findings.problem: Each recursion level builds in, out and tmp (char[MAX_PATH], 1025) as the parent path plus a listed name with sprintf, and filerGetGameTitle builds dir and tmpdir with strcpy/strcat (path + name + '/' + name for the PS1 probe). Names come from listings (FAT, exFAT and SMB allow 255 chars; FILEINFO.name is 256) and nothing bounds the total, so a source tree whose path passes about 770 chars (four nested 190-char folder names) overflows copy()'s stack buffers on the UI thread, and long names overflow tmpdir on the worker when the browser lists titles. delete() and getFileSize() bound the same joins with snprintf and return -ENAMETOOLONG.
findings.fix: At copy() entry, after newfile is set, return copyDiagFail(-ENAMETOOLONG) when strlen(inPath) + strlen(file.name) + 2 or strlen(outPath) + strlen(newfile.name) + 2 (plus room for the PSU name suffix in PSU backup mode) exceeds MAX_PATH. In filerGetGameTitle build dir and tmpdir with snprintf and return -1 when they do not fit.
findings.justification: A stack overflow (crash or silent corruption, EE threads have no stack protector) on input a user can have: deep trees with long names. One bound check at copy() entry covers all five joins, the same pattern delete()/getFileSize() already use.
findings.benefit: Closes a stack overflow on long paths; about 4 lines added (READ).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:560-682 and 752-1300. MAX_NAME 256, MAX_PATH 1025 (launchelf.h:201-205); FILEINFO.name[MAX_NAME] (launchelf.h:562). Child levels receive the parent's in/out as inPath/outPath (filer_copy.c:1117-1118, 1133, 1164), so each level adds a name and a slash. moveRecord checks its own join (filer_copy.c:180) but runs after the sprintf at 849. filer_actions.c:314-317 (getFileSize) and 1972-1973 (delete) bound the same joins with snprintf. filerGetGameTitle runs on the worker for browser listings (dash_browser.c:321) and from copy() (filer_copy.c:949, 1050). Confidence Med: needs unusually long names.

findings.title: mcCardWriteSave writes save data one 1 KB cluster per lseek+write RPC pair, copying each through a bounce buffer
findings.problem: Each data cluster is memset+memcpy'd into buf and written with its own writeAt call; the card tool's write callback ctWrite does genLseek (fileXioLseek64) plus genWrite (fileXioWrite) per call. A 1 MB save costs 1024 writes = 2048 EE-to-IOP RPCs on the UI thread. writerAlloc hands out the lowest free clusters in ascending order (mc_card_write.c:374-386), so a chain is usually a few runs of consecutive clusters that could each be one write.
findings.fix: In step 1, write each run of consecutive chain clusters with one writeAt straight from fl->data (no memset/memcpy), and send only the final partial cluster through buf with its zero padding.
findings.justification: Adds about 4 lines to the write loop. The concrete problem is per-cluster RPC pairs and a 1 KB bounce copy for every cluster of every imported save; grouping consecutive clusters is the smallest change that cuts the call count by the run length without a new buffer or cache.
findings.benefit: Write calls per save drop from one per KB to one per contiguous run (often 1-3 per file); removes the per-cluster memcpy. Time saved INFERRED, not measured (roughly 2 RPCs per KB of save data).
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_write.c:408-416 (writeAt/writeCluster, 1024-byte writes), 569-590 (per-cluster memset, memcpy, writeCluster), 374-386 (writerAlloc scans upward from w->scan). dash_card_tool.c:96-117 ctWrite: genLseek then genWrite loop per call, no write cache. filer_fileops.c:690 genLseek -> fileXioLseek64, :747 genWrite -> fileXioWrite.
