Callers mcCardWriteSave at dash_card_tool.c:408, 1088, 1170 run on the UI thread (no dashWorker use in that file). Timing per RPC not measured.

findings.title: Recursive copy() keeps a full 2048-entry listing (896 KB) at every folder level
findings.problem: Each folder level memaligns MAX_ENTRY FILEINFOs (2048 x 448 B = 896 KB) for its listing and holds it while all its subfolders are copied, so a tree d levels deep holds d x 896 KB of listings although a typical folder has a few dozen entries. copy() allows 15 nested levels (MAX_RECURSE 16), about 13 MB. getFileSize() and delete() repeat the same per-level allocation.
findings.fix: List into one MAX_ENTRY scratch buffer shared by all levels (getDirComplete writes it only before the children run and again after they return), then memalign only nfiles entries for the level and copy them; do the second listing at line 1179 into the scratch and compare it with the level's copy. getFileSize() can use the same scratch.
findings.justification: A 5-level copy holds about 4.4 MB of mostly empty listings out of a heap of about 25 MB (evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:207), on top of up to 2 MiB of copy buffers, and deeper trees approach 13 MB and can fail with -ENOMEM. One shared scratch keeps the peak at 896 KB plus the entries really listed, for about 6 more lines.
findings.benefit: Peak heap of a d-level copy drops from d x 917,504 B to 917,504 B plus the used entries (INFERRED: FILEINFO 256 + 66 + 64-byte-aligned 64-byte stats = 448 B, x MAX_ENTRY 2048).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:742-760 (comment: MAX_ENTRY entries are about 900 KB), 911-935, 1122-1192; files[] is read inside the child loop (1163-1164) and overwritten by the second listing only after it (1179). MAX_ENTRY 2048 (launchelf.h:205); FILEINFO layout launchelf.h:560-565, sceMcTblGetDir 64 bytes aligned 64 as mirrored in tests/test_copy_psu_listing.py:104-106. MAX_RECURSE 16 (include/filer_shared.h:40), refusal at recurses + 1 >= MAX_RECURSE (filer_copy.c:797). compile.yml:383-386 also states each level's listing is about 900 KB. filer_actions.c:310-311 (getFileSize) and 1981-1984 (delete) allocate the same per level. INFERRED part: the heap size (BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:207 estimate) and that deep copies run short.

findings.title: Settings reads files on the UI thread without dashWorkerAwaitAll (S_LANGUAGE language reload, SMB2.CNF reads in the share editor)
findings.problem: dash_worker.c:6-10 says the UI thread does no IO while a job runs, and pathApplied guards Load_External_Language with dashWorkerAwaitAll (2122-2125, 'these read files on the UI thread'). The S_LANGUAGE choice calls the same function (1919) with no guard; it opens and reads setting->lang_file when one is set (lang.c:469-486). The share editor reads SMB2.CNF with dashLoadTextFile (566-567, 3483-3484), and smbSharesSnapshot (496) can re-read LAUNCHSTATION.CNF or mc0/mc1 SYS-CONF (smb_shares.c:81-121, 216-219), with no worker check, while a queued job such as an earlier Save (cfgSaveRun, 2286-2298) may be using the same card.
findings.fix: Before each read, call dashWorkerAwaitAll and stop when it returns 0, as pathApplied does: in the S_LANGUAGE case, in smbedWriteFile's base == NULL branch, before the S_SMBED_TEXT read, and before smbedLoadPick at 3786.
findings.justification: Each guard adds about 2 lines. It is the documented mechanism (dash_worker.c:15-17) already used at 2124 and 2559 for the same kind of read, and it stops libmc/fileXio being used from two threads at once, which the worker rules forbid.
findings.benefit: Removes a race between UI-thread card reads and worker writes during Settings edits; about +8 lines (4 guards x 2). Harm on hardware INFERRED, not reproduced.
findings.evidence: Read dash_worker.c 1-22 (rules), dash_settings.c 2109-2138 (guarded pathApplied), 1912-1920 (unguarded S_LANGUAGE), 551-606 and 3427-3504 (SMB editor reads), 3780-3787 (smbedLoadPick on page open), 2286-2350 (cfgSave on worker). lang.c 452-488: Load_External_Language uses genOpen/genRead when lang_file is set. dash_store.c 105-139: dashLoadTextFile does genOpen/genRead with no worker check. smb_shares.c 81-121, 199-222: smbSharesConfigured/Snapshot call smbReadConfig when the cache is cold or mc1 is pending. Other UI-thread IO sites check dashWorkerIoBusy (dash_main.c:1266, dash_sound.c:171).

findings.title: BGM.ADP and custom effect files are read on the UI thread at boot and after every IOP reset
findings.problem: readAdpSidecar opens and reads the whole file synchronously (up to 1 MB music, plus eight effect files when Custom sounds is on). Its callers run in the dashboard main loop: the boot init (dash_main.c:1520-1521), dashSoundMaintain every frame after an IOP reset (1484), and after misc commands and failed launches (356-358, 676-678). The shipped BGM.ADP is 284,656 B and sits beside the ELF, often on a memory card, so no frame is drawn while it is read. The worker exists so the cursor never waits for IO (dash_worker.c:3-4).
findings.fix: Read the sidecar files in a dashWorkerSubmit job and do the audsrv uploads in its completion callback, which already runs on the UI thread. The boot-time call can stay where it is; the gain is mainly the re-reads after IOP resets and with Custom sounds on.
findings.justification: The stall is real: a file read of about 278 KB per IOP reset runs on the render thread. Using the existing worker queue (one submit, one run function, one done callback, about 20 lines) is the smallest change that keeps rendering going. No new mechanism is added.
findings.benefit: Removes a frame stall of roughly 0.3-1 s per sound re-init when BGM.ADP is on a memory card or USB 1.1 (INFERRED from 284,656 B at a few hundred KB/s; not measured).
findings.evidence: Call paths read: dash_main.c:1517-1521 (boot init on the UI loop; the comment at 1512-1516 accepts the freeze during Init_Delay), dash_main.c:1484 dashSoundMaintain each frame -> dash_sound.c:275-276 dashSoundInit + dashBgmStart -> loadBgmSidecar 452-474 -> readAdpSidecar 407-450 (genOpen/genLseek/genRead). uploadSamples 143-149 reads 8 files when dashCfg.custom_sounds. dashSoundShutdown frees bgm_data before each IOP reset (init.c:2193), so bgm_loaded=0 forces a re-read. Size from inventory/Launchstation.tsv:608. Throughput is not measured (INFERRED).

findings.title: Orphan 'endfunc' banners and headings for functions that moved out of draw.c and editor.c
findings.problem: draw.c keeps empty banners for loadFont, drawChar, drawChar2, printXY, printXY_sjis and transcpy_sjis, which now live in draw_text.c. editor.c keeps 'ends menu', 'endfunc Virt_KeyBoard_Entry', 'endfunc KeyBoard_Entry' and 'ends Window_Selector' banners for code split into editor_menu.c/editor_input.c. dash_widgets.c:362-363 is a heading with no code under it.
findings.fix: Delete these comment-only blocks.
findings.benefit: ~46 comment lines removed; no binary change.
findings.evidence: Read the cited ranges: comment lines only. Grep 'int loadFont|void drawChar|int printXY' finds the definitions in draw_text.c:67,107,142,159,206,333. editorMenu/editorSelectWindow are in editor_menu.c:6,139 and editorVirtualKeyboardEntry/editorKeyboardEntry in editor_input.c:169,428. Grep 'endfunc' in tests: only banners of filer_actions.c, filer_browser.c and init.c are used as slice markers, none of the cited ones.

findings.title: Stale banner comments in filer.c describe code that moved or never existed
findings.problem: 383-403 holds a commented-out debug buffer, an #ifdef DVRP block containing only comment rules, and an unmountAll description ending in 'ends unmountAll' although unmountAll lives in filer_mount.c:155. 889-903 lists gen* functions (including a nonexistent genInit) and says 'endfunc genLimObjName', which is in filer_fileops.c:186. 1581-1582 says 'endfunc addRootUsbDeviceEntries' after pollRootMemoryCardDevices. 2490-2494 says 'End of file: filer.c' with 85 lines of code after it. 48-52 are blank.
findings.fix: Delete these comment blocks.
findings.benefit: ~45 source lines of misleading comments removed; no ELF change.
findings.evidence: Grep unmountAll definition: src/filer_mount.c:155; genLimObjName definition: src/filer_fileops.c:186; genInit: no definition anywhere (only the comment at filer.c:896). Read the cited ranges.

findings.title: wle_stricmp and wle_strnlen reimplement newlib strcasecmp and strnlen
findings.problem: launchelf.h carries static inline copies of ASCII case-insensitive compare and strnlen, aliased by macro to stricmp/strnlen. The EE build already calls newlib's strcasecmp/strncasecmp directly (dash_card_tool.c:1715, cloud_http.c:509), so the library versions are linked and available; strnlen has only two callers.
findings.fix: Replace the helpers with '#define stricmp strcasecmp' (include strings.h) and use newlib strnlen; change ember.c:206 to strcasecmp.
findings.benefit: ~36 lines removed from the umbrella header included by every EE file; negligible ELF change (INFERRED).

findings.title: remoteCommandPoll stacks a second 3 s throttle under the dashboard's 500 ms one, stats before opening, and has a never-built #else stub

ETH and EXFAT are always defined (ps2.yaml:624,629), so the #else stub at :101-107 is never compiled.
findings.fix: Keep one throttle: drop next_remote_poll/REMOTE_COMMAND_INTERVAL_MS here (and next_poll in pc_game_receiver.c) and set the dash_main.c gate to the wanted interval, or the reverse. Delete the fileXioGetStat call and the #if/#else wrapper.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines removed across the two pollers; one fewer fileXio RPC per poll (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep remoteCommandPoll|next_remote_poll: only caller dash_main.c:775 (pollRemotePcCommandImpl, under #ifdef ETH) reached from :1460 inside the 500 ms gate at :1458-1461. remote_control.c:49-51 3000 ms gate. ps2.yaml:624 ETH, :629 EXFAT; configure_ds34.py only adds DS34 (brief section 2). remote_control.c:53 stat result st is never read.

findings.title: artRun probes each candidate with fileExists before dashPngLoadFile, which already does the same genFixPath+genOpen and fails on a missing file
findings.problem: fileExists opens and closes the file, then tryDecode -> dashPngLoadFile -> dashLoadTextFile runs genFixPath and genOpen on the same path and returns NULL when it is missing (dash_store.c:115-119). For missing candidates both cost one failed open; for the found file the worker does an extra open/close, which is slow on memory cards and network devices.
findings.fix: Delete fileExists and call tryDecode(j, cand) directly at line 375.
findings.benefit: One open+close less per discovered artwork file on the worker thread; 14 lines removed (READ).
findings.evidence: Read dash_art.c:151-163, 341-378 and dash_png.c:226-238 (dashPngLoadFile -> dashLoadTextFile, -1 on NULL) and dash_store.c:105-146 (genFixPath, genOpen, NULL on failure). Grep fileExists in src/dash_art.c: definition at 151 and the single call at 375.

findings.title: save_refresh_token re-reads and re-parses the staged token although dashWriteFile already verified it byte for byte
findings.problem: dashWriteFile writes the file and then reads it back and compares every byte, returning -1 on any difference (dash_store.c:163-174). save_refresh_token then reads the same WLE-CLOUD.TOK.NEW a second time, parses it and compares the token (333-344). A byte-identical file always parses to the same token, so this check can never fail when dashWriteFile succeeded. It only costs one more 8 KB allocation and a memory-card read per link.
findings.fix: Delete the read-back block 333-344 (and the now unused verify, saved, saved_len locals). The wider TOK.NEW staging scheme could also go, since losing the token only means linking again, but that is optional.
findings.benefit: ~14 lines removed and one card read per Google link (READ). Dropping the whole staging scheme would remove roughly 30 more lines (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read cloud_google.c 248-355 and dash_store.c:148-175 (dashWriteFile: write, close, reopen, memcmp in 1 KB blocks, check EOF). The text written at 323 is fixed format, so token_kv parses it deterministically. tests/test_native_cloud.py:122-128 assert the staging strings (TOK.NEW, dashWriteFile/dashLoadTextFile on token_stage_path, Stage_Complete). Only the dashLoadTextFile(s->token_stage_path assertion at :125 still matches through load_session:288, so the tests keep passing.

findings.title: waitUntilTimer/hddHeaderDelay spin on Timer() with an empty loop body instead of sleeping
findings.problem: waitForClipboardSourceDevice (filer_browser.c:240-264) runs after an IOP reset since the copy. The EE runs at 100% and no lower-priority thread can run. hddHeaderDelay is the same empty spin, used between source polls at hdd_header_injector.c:315 and :419.
findings.fix: Delete both helpers. Between probes call DelayThread(SOURCE_DEVICE_WAIT_INTERVAL_MS * 1000), and DelayThread(HDD_HEADER_SOURCE_POLL_MS * 1000) in the injector. The loops already check the deadline, so the next_check clamp at 257-259 can go too.
findings.benefit: About 12 lines removed (two 4-8 line helpers plus the clamp). The CPU is free during waits of up to 6 s. The UI looks the same, because the thread is blocked either way (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read filer_browser.c:120-124 and 240-264, and hdd_header_injector.c:91-98 and the grep hits at :315 and :419. grep for waitUntilTimer and hddHeaderDelay finds only those call sites. timer.c:8-11: Timer() reads GetTimerSystemTime, which does not block. dash_browser.c:791-798 (prepareOp: 'classic file operations run on the UI thread with the worker idle') and 877-895 (opPaste -> filerPasteModeInto). DelayThread is already used for waits, for example init.c:1601-1602.

findings.title: Auto-start device id-to-bit mapping written twice (six choiceInfo cases and a setChoice ternary)
findings.problem: choiceInfo has seven cases that differ only in the DASH_DEVA_* constant (S_DEVA_UDPFS leaves out the boot-device test, which is harmless because dashBootDeviceBit never returns UDPFS, dash_devices.c:895-918). setChoice maps the same ids to bits again with a 6-way ternary.
findings.fix: Add one small static id-to-bit function, use it in setChoice in place of the ternary, and collapse the choiceInfo cases into one case group: cur = (dev_auto & bit) || dashBootDeviceBit() == bit.
findings.justification: The helper replaces two copies of the same mapping: 23 + 6 lines become about 8 + 6 + 1, a net removal of about 11 lines, and a device added later needs one edit instead of two.
findings.benefit: ~11 lines removed net (INFERRED from cited ranges); negligible size change
findings.evidence: Read dash_settings.c:1130-1152 and 1729-1768; read dash_devices.c:895-918 (dashBootDeviceBit returns USB/HDD/ATA/MMCE/MX4SIO/ILINK or 0, never UDPFS).

findings.title: Exploit install repeats file and folder probes: custom ELF and PS2KEYS.dat checked again before signing, mc_folder_exists twice per folder
findings.problem: reload_custom_payload_source parses PS2KEYS.dat again (KelfSignValidateKeys) and opens the ELF again to measure it (KelfSignGetOutputSize, 1077-1082), right before prepare_custom_signed_payloads calls KelfSignElfToMemory, which parses the keys and reads the whole ELF anyway (kelf_signer.c:1014-1018) and reports its own failure. prepare_needed_folders calls mc_folder_exists (1664) and then ensure_mc_folder, which calls mc_folder_exists on the same folder again (1163-1164).
findings.fix: Delete lines 1077-1082 and the signed_size variable in reload_custom_payload_source; keep the two ensurePathDeviceStackReady calls. Delete the check at 1163-1164 in ensure_mc_folder and call ensure_mc_folder only when folder_assets_to_write[i] was set (folder missing); mcMkDir's -4 result is already accepted.
findings.benefit: One keys-file parse and one ELF open/seek/tail read less per custom install; one memory-card directory open less per needed folder (up to 4). INFERRED, tens of ms. About 9 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read main_exploit_installer.c 1059-1090, 1159-1171, 1423-1449 (build_custom_payload_to_memory reports Exploit_Custom_ELF_Sign_failed), 1642-1672, 1944-1969. kelf_signer.c 734-742 (KelfSignValidateKeys -> parse_key_store), 764-793 (KelfSignGetOutputSize opens, seeks and reads the ELF tail), 924-979 and 981-1020 (KelfSignElfToMemory: parse_key_store at 1014, load_elf_into_output at 1018 reads the full ELF). grep reload_custom_payload_source: only the definition and the call at 1954.

findings.title: PS2TIME in filer_shared.h duplicates ps2time in psu_types.h
findings.problem: Both headers declare the same 8-byte memory-card timestamp (u8 unused/sec/min/hour/day/month, u16 year) under two names; PS2TIME is used in filer_actions.c and filer_browser.c, ps2time in the PSU headers.
findings.fix: Keep one typedef (psu_types.h's ps2time), include psu_types.h from filer_shared.h and rename the PS2TIME uses, or make PS2TIME a one-line typedef of ps2time.
findings.benefit: ~9 lines removed; no ELF change.
findings.evidence: Read both structs: identical member order and types (aligned(2) on PS2TIME matches the natural u16 alignment). git grep -nw PS2TIME: filer_shared.h:15, filer_actions.c:1283,1322, filer_browser.c:1067,1825,2032,2074,2091 (+tests). ps2time in iop/oldlibs/ps2ftpd is a separate IOP type and not affected.

findings.title: hddHeaderTextEditor global function pointer and editorForHeader wrapper for a single caller
findings.problem: The only caller of EditHddPartitionHeaderSystemCnf (dash_hdd.c:966) sets hddHeaderTextEditor to editorForHeader, which only forwards to dashTextEditor, and resets it to TextEditor afterwards; the TextEditor default is never used.
findings.fix: Call dashTextEditor directly from EditHddPartitionHeaderSystemCnf (or pass the editor as a parameter); delete the global, its extern, editorForHeader and the two assignments.
findings.benefit: ~9 lines removed; one global and one indirect call gone.
findings.evidence: Grep hddHeaderTextEditor over repo: hdd_header_injector.h:16, hdd_header_injector.c:826,858, dash_hdd.c:965,967. Grep EditHddPartitionHeaderSystemCnf: only dash_hdd.c:966. dashTextEditor(const char *) declared dash_internal.h:1067.

findings.title: p1Base duplicates ctBaseName from dash_card_tool.c; lkLabel repeats the same basename code
findings.problem: p1Base and ctBaseName are byte-for-byte the same 8-line function (basename after last '/' or ':'); lkLabel open-codes it again. dash_ps1_card.c already includes dash_card_tool.h.
findings.fix: Make ctBaseName non-static with a prototype in dash_card_tool.h (or a dash_internal.h helper), delete p1Base and use it in dash_ps1_card.c and lkLabel.
findings.benefit: ~9 lines removed net (8 + 3 removed, 1 prototype and include added), one copy of a tiny function (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep "strrchr\([a-z_]+, ':'\)" over src: dash_card_tool.c:187-191 identical to dash_ps1_card.c:40-44; dash_main.c:1029-1032 same logic. Other matches (neutrino_iso.c, elf.c, editor.c) differ (copy into buffers / handle both).

findings.title: prepareExploitSignerIop repeats its post-reboot re-init sequence in both branches
findings.problem: The failure branch (849-859) and the success path (864-874) run the same seven steps: SifInitRpc, SifLoadFileInit, initsbv_patches, clearIopModuleState, iop_reset_generation++, ensureCoreIoStackReady, DS34 load, setupPad. The success path only adds SifIopSync and clearing the PCCF ownership first.
findings.fix: Do the SifIopSync and PCCF clear only when ret > 0, then run the shared re-init once, then return 0 if ret <= 0, else load SECRSIF as now.
findings.benefit: ~9 lines removed (INFERRED from the cited ranges)
findings.evidence: Read init.c:821-882. tests/test_pccf_owner.py:101-103 requires SifIopSync to come before 'pccf_bus_owned = pccf_loaded = 0' in this function, which the restructure keeps.

findings.title: FILEOP_TRACE definition block in filer.c is unused there
findings.problem: filer.c defines FILEOP_TRACE from ULE_DEBUG_BUILD but never tests it (no #if FILEOP_TRACE in filer.c). The same 8-line block is pasted in filer_copy.c, filer_mount.c and filer_fileops.c, and no build defines ULE_DEBUG_BUILD, so FILEOP_TRACE is 0 in every build.
findings.fix: Delete the block in filer.c. Optionally keep a single copy of the block in a header the other three files already share instead of three pasted copies.
findings.benefit: 8 lines removed from filer.c (up to 24 more if the other copies are merged); no ELF change.
findings.evidence: Grep FILEOP_TRACE over src include: in filer.c only the definition lines 157-162; uses exist only in filer_copy.c, filer_mount.c, filer_fileops.c. Grep ULE_DEBUG_BUILD in ps2.yaml, scripts, workflows: none (brief section 2 agrees).

findings.title: dashPickPath: pickParent ignores its size argument and the 'go to parent' block is written twice
findings.problem: pickParent takes int size only to cast it to void (line 1084). Both callers (Back at 1164-1170, the Up row at 1218-1223) do the same four steps: copy pk.dir to a local buffer, pickParent, pickOpen, sel = 0.
findings.fix: Drop the size parameter and fold the copy + pickOpen into pickParent (pickUp), so both call sites become one call plus sel = 0.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines removed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep pickParent over the repo: dash_widgets.c:1066 (definition), 1167, 1221 (calls); no test extracts it.

findings.title: DI_RECENT icon is rasterised into the atlas but never drawn

findings.fix: Delete the DI_RECENT enum entry and its iconSdf case.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines removed; one 64x64 SDF tile no longer rasterised at boot and a few hundred bytes of iconSdf code (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Loop over every DI_ name in dash_internal.h:434-506 with git grep -lw over src include igr loader, excluding dash_icons.c and dash_internal.h: only DI_VIEW_CAROUSEL, DI_PAD_BADGE, DI_RECENT unreferenced. No arithmetic reaching DI_RECENT found (git grep for DI_x + / + DI_ patterns). Tests do not mention DI_RECENT.

findings.title: McViewSave.title_break is written in two places and never read; icon.sys header parse duplicated
findings.problem: title_break is set by ctPsuInfo (2320, 2323-2324) and by mc_card_view.c (311, 314-315); no production code reads it, only the host test print at tests/mc_card_view_host.c:44. ctPsuInfo's icon.sys check and title copy repeat mc_card_view.c's.

findings.title: Needless indirections: install_for_plan forwarding wrapper and main_history evictedEntry temp copy
findings.problem: install_for_plan only unpacks plan into install_selected_ps2_updates and has one caller (2491). processHistoryList copies the evicted entry into a local only to pass it as a const pointer to appendEvictedHistoryEntry; the original is not modified until the memset after the call.
findings.fix: Delete install_for_plan and call install_selected_ps2_updates directly; pass newEntry to appendEvictedHistoryEntry and delete evictedEntry and the memcpy.
findings.benefit: ~7 lines removed; 24-byte stack copy avoided (INFERRED: sizeof(OSDHistoryEntry) = 16+4+2+pad)
findings.evidence: grep install_for_plan: definition 2277 and call 2491 only. main_history.c:67 appendEvictedHistoryEntry takes const OSDHistoryEntry *; 145-149 memcpy then call then memset.

findings.title: Unreachable and duplicate branches in dash_font.c glyph handling
findings.problem: glyphAdv returns the same value for c >= ELISA_CODE and c >= 0x100 in two separate branches. Its c < FONT_FIRST remap and the same remap in drawRun can never fire: both get codes only from nextGlyphs, which already maps c < 0x20 to ' ' (line 361) and otherwise yields '?', 0x100+ pad codes or ELISA codes. The forward declaration of facesInit at line 316 is unused because facesInit is defined at 398 before its first use at 562.
findings.fix: Merge the two glyphAdv branches into one 'c >= 0x100' test, delete the two c < FONT_FIRST remaps and the facesInit forward declaration.
findings.benefit: ~7 lines removed; negligible ELF change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read nextGlyphs dash_font.c:328-365 (all outputs), glyphAdv callers 523 and 652 (both fed from nextGlyphs via g[k]), drawRun 574-577. ELISA_CODE is 0x10000 (line 40) so the first glyphAdv branch is a subset of the second. facesInit uses: 316 (decl), 398 (definition), 562, 901.

findings.title: colA copied in dash_bg_geo.c and dash_bg_ps2.c; TAU_F defined but unused in dash_bg_geo.c
findings.problem: The 5-line static colA (set alpha with clamp) is byte-identical in both files, and both define TAU_F; dash_bg_geo.c never uses TAU_F (lines 1-333 read).
findings.fix: Delete TAU_F from dash_bg_geo.c. Move colA once into dash_internal.h as a static inline next to dashColorA (line 63) and delete both file copies.
findings.benefit: ~7 lines removed; no ELF change (INFERRED: static helper inlined either way).
findings.evidence: Grep 'static DashColor colA|define TAU_F' over src: dash_bg_geo.c:10,12 and dash_bg_ps2.c:48,50 only. Read both copies (identical bodies). dashColorA at dash_internal.h:63 multiplies alpha, so it is not a drop-in replacement; colA sets it.

findings.title: ctBaseName is a copy of dash_ps1_card.c p1Base
findings.problem: Both return the path component after the last '/' or ':' with identical bodies; dash_card_tool.h is already the header shared between the two files.

findings.benefit: ~7 lines removed (INFERRED).

findings.title: dashSinf/dashCosf are out-of-line forwarders to sinf/cosf
findings.problem: dashSinf and dashCosf only return sinf(x) and cosf(x). Because they are defined in dash_gfx.c, the ~90 call sites in the background, art and UI files pay an extra cross-file call per evaluation in per-frame animation code.
findings.fix: Replace the two prototypes with static inline definitions (or #define to sinf/cosf) in dash_internal.h and delete the two functions from dash_gfx.c; callers stay unchanged.
findings.benefit: ~7 net lines removed; removes one call frame per sin/cos in per-frame background code (INFERRED, not measured)
findings.evidence: Grep -w dashSinf|dashCosf over src/Launchstation: definitions dash_gfx.c:63,68; prototypes dash_internal.h:322-323; callers in dash_bg_ps2.c, dash_bg_geo.c, dash_bg.c, dash_art.c, dash_ui.c. tests/test_orb_seamless.py:38-39 defines its own static stubs, so a header inline needs that test checked.

findings.title: dash_devices.c exports with no outside user: dashMcPresent (test-only), dashDiscStatus, dashDevicesAutoProbe
findings.problem: dashMcPresent has no production caller (only tests/test_device_input.py:394-395); dashDiscStatus is only called at dash_devices.c:443 and dashDevicesAutoProbe only at dash_devices.c:796, yet both are exported through dash_internal.h.

findings.title: smb2Connect_out_t is never written by smb2man; the EE passes a dummy out buffer
findings.problem: The header says ctx is 'not written: kept so the EE's call is unchanged'; smb2man_connect_devctl (iop/smb2man/smb2man.c:1491, called at 1552) takes only the input struct. The EE still declares, zeroes and passes the out struct, while the NFS connect beside it passes NULL, 0 (smb_shares.c:256).
findings.fix: Delete smb2Connect_out_t and pass NULL, 0 as the out buffer, as NFS_DEVCTL_CONNECT does; update tests/smb2man_live/drive.c:58 the same way.
findings.benefit: ~7 lines removed; one 4-byte devctl out buffer less per SMB2 connect (INFERRED).

findings.title: time_manip_automatic_run re-implements sasFolderTimestamp inline
findings.problem: The SAS loop body at 1841-1844 is exactly sasFolderTimestamp (1734-1737): build effective name, category, payload, setSasTimestamp. The effective/payload buffers and category local exist only for this copy.
findings.fix: Call sasFolderTimestamp(name, &stats._Modify) in the loop and delete the three locals.
findings.benefit: ~7 lines removed; also drops ~2 x (MAX_NAME+8) bytes of stack in that frame (INFERRED from the declarations)
findings.evidence: Read 1729-1738 and 1840-1845: same four calls with the same arguments. effective, payload and category are used nowhere else in time_manip_automatic_run (1800-1886).

findings.title: Classic browser R1 handlers: GetSize prints an unterminated sizeC buffer, and NEWICON's DoneIcon copies a possibly uninitialised tmp1
findings.problem: GetSize: sizeC[21] is filled backwards from sizeC[20] (sizeP starts at &sizeC[21]), so no NUL follows the last digit inside the array. sprintf('%s', sizeP) reads stack bytes past the array, so garbage digits can be appended to the message. NEWICON: if the first keyboard() is cancelled (1463-1464), DoneIcon runs strcpy(tmp, tmp1). On the first R1 action of a browser session, tmp1 has not been written, so this reads uninitialised stack memory. Both paths are reachable only from the classic browse mode (cnfmode 0), which docs/dashboard.md:96-97 says no dashboard entry opens.
findings.fix: If the classic browser is kept, replace the sizeC block (2124-2131) with a single ' mcTsz=%llu' sprintf, as lines 1841 and 2068 already do, and replace the dummy strcpy at 1499 with an empty statement after the DoneIcon label. If the classic browser is deleted as dead code, both go with it.
findings.benefit: About 6 lines removed. Fixes an out-of-bounds read and an uninitialised read, both latent because the code is practically unreachable (READ; reachability INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read filer_browser.c:2022-2136 and 1457-1500. In browseFilePath, tmp1 is first written at 1356/1369/1386/1465/1513/1553/1567, all after their own menu choice. grep sizeC: only 2126-2127. getFilePath(.., FALSE) callers: main_actions.c:221, 234, 738, 774, 886. Misc_FileBrowser and Misc_TextEditor are intercepted by dashRunMisc (dash_main.c:466-473). ExecuteBrowserFrom has no caller. main.c:240 Execute(igr_after_path) is the only other route; its path is picked with ext ELF (dash_settings.c:2074).

findings.title: McView version, cardtype and cardflags are filled in but never read; has_ecc and title_break are read only by a test
findings.problem: mcViewOpen copies the superblock version string, card type and flags into McView, but nothing in the repo reads v->version, v->cardtype or v->cardflags (mcCardFormat and mcCardReadIdentity take the identity from the raw superblock). has_ecc duplicates page_stride == 528 and is read only by tests/mc_card_view_host.c:37; McViewSave.title_break is read only by that test (line 44) and also set in dash_card_tool.c:2320-2324.
findings.fix: Delete the version, cardtype and cardflags fields and their assignments. Optionally also drop has_ecc (the test can print page_stride) and title_break with its two fillers, adjusting the host test output.
findings.benefit: ~6 lines removed (up to ~14 with has_ecc/title_break); 15 bytes per McView (INFERRED: char[13] + 2 x uint8_t).
findings.evidence: Grep '\b(has_ecc|cardtype|cardflags|title_break)\b|(\.|->)version\b' over src/Launchstation excluding iop/: McView fields written only at mc_card_view.c:216, 229-230, 246-247; no reader in src/, include/ or tests/ for version/cardtype/cardflags (other hits are unrelated structs). has_ecc read only at tests/mc_card_view_host.c:37; title_break read only at tests/mc_card_view_host.c:44.

findings.title: dashHomeRebuild is a forwarding wrapper placed after the end-of-file banner, with a duplicate prototype in dash_apps.c
findings.problem: dashHomeRebuild only calls the static homeRebuild and sits below the 'End of file' banner. dash_apps.c:12 re-declares it although dash_internal.h:733 already does and dash_apps.c includes that header.

findings.evidence: Grep dashHomeRebuild: definition dash_home.c:562, prototypes dash_internal.h:733 and dash_apps.c:12, callers dash_apps.c:91,459, dash_main.c:719, dash_settings.c:1781,1810,2259,2590,2601,3291; test stubs only. Grep homeRebuild in tests: test_home_focus.py:80-120 extracts the static function by its signature.

findings.title: isWritablePath in dash_themes.c duplicates isWritableDevice in dash_store.c

No #if/#ifdef TMANIP anywhere; no tests reference either name.

findings.title: Dead bits in dash_editor.c: constant-empty status ternary, needless details[] buffer, avoidable forward declaration
findings.problem: editorScene formats '%s' with 'ndocs > 1 ? "" : ""', which is always empty. switchDocument snprintf's 'unsaved' or '' into a 128-byte details[8][16] stack array only to turn '' back into NULL. docNew is forward-declared because it is defined after its only earlier user docOpenPath.
findings.fix: Drop the trailing %s and its argument; set items[i].detail = docs[i].dirty ? "unsaved" : NULL and delete details[]; move docNew above docOpenPath and delete the forward declaration.

findings.title: Set_Language repeats the table copy and MISC path rebuild that Load_External_Language does right after it
findings.problem: Every dashboard caller runs Set_Language then Load_External_Language. Both release the external buffer, memcpy the whole Lang_String table and run updateLocalizedMiscPaths, so each language change does that work twice. The only standalone Set_Language callers are in the classic Config_Startup screen (config_startup.c:113,146), see finding 1.
findings.fix: Reduce Set_Language to storing the normalised language, or have the callers set setting->language and call Load_External_Language only.
findings.benefit: ~5 source lines removed and one redundant table copy plus MISC rename pass per language change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: grep Set_Language|Load_External_Language over src: dash_settings.c:1918-1919 and 2561-2562 call both in sequence; config_startup.c:113,146 call Set_Language alone after clearing lang_file; Load_External_Language (lang.c:452-569) with an empty lang_file does exactly what Set_Language does (464-467, 567-568).

findings.title: setPartyList has no caller

findings.title: Functions used only in their own file are exported (filer.c readers, filer_actions.h timestamp helpers)
findings.problem: readMC, readXFROM, readCD, readVMC, readHDD, readHDDDVRP, readGENERIC, readHOST, readUDPFS, readSMB and setDVRPPartyList are non-static but used only in filer.c; readSMB is still declared in filer_shared.h. filer.c also re-declares dashWorkerOnThread locally (222) although dash_internal.h:997 declares it. filerCanSetCustomTimestamp and time_manip_custom are declared in filer_actions.h but used only inside filer_actions.c.
findings.fix: Make these functions static, delete the readSMB prototype from filer_shared.h and the two declarations from filer_actions.h; turn the readGENERIC forward declaration into a static one.

Grep filerCanSetCustomTimestamp/time_manip_custom: only filer_actions.h and filer_actions.c. findings.title: Folder-date tools redo whole-list work: date editor re-sorts every frame with struct copies, A-Z/Z-A dating is O(N^2 x 60)
findings.problem: The dashboard date editor calls filerDateEditorSync every frame (dash_browser.c:2473, UI thread); it runs two stricmp scans and the insertion sort, which copies each FILEINFO into a temporary and back even when nothing moves (782 and 788). setSequentialTimestamp steps one second at a time, position x 60 calls per folder, so A-Z/Z-A ordering of N folders costs 30 x N x (N-1) step calls on the UI thread before any progress is drawn (1853). With the usual few dozen MC-root folders both costs are small; they grow with folder count (N=500: ~7.5 M step calls).
findings.fix: In tsEdit call filerDateEditorSync only when an input changed the selection or a date. In sortCustomDateEditorFolders skip an element already in order before copying it. In setSequentialTimestamp subtract position minutes from 23:59:58 arithmetically (as setSasTimestamp does with decrementSasTimestampDate) instead of the per-second loop.
findings.benefit: Removes per-frame O(N) struct copies (~0.9 KB per folder per frame) and makes A-Z/Z-A dating O(N) instead of O(N^2 x 60) step calls (INFERRED from the loops; no timing measured).
findings.evidence: Read filer_actions.c:775-837, 1080-1083, 1526-1539, 1800-1886 and dash_browser.c:2430-2536 (tsEdit loop: filerDateEditorSync at 2473 every iteration, dashGfxPresent at 2534). opTimestamps (dash_browser.c:2542-2557) runs time_manip_organize on the UI thread after prepareOp. Folder count is bounded by getDir at MAX_ENTRY-2 (filer.c:2235-2238). Step count: sum over i<N of i*60 = 30*N*(N-1); the instruction cost per step is INFERRED.

findings.title: genFixPath strips the '/' after the device with an overlapping strcpy at four sites (undefined behaviour)
findings.problem: Each site does strcpy(gen_path + (sep - gen_path), sep + 1) with sep inside gen_path, i.e. copies a string onto itself shifted by one byte; overlapping strcpy is undefined in C. It works today only because the copy runs forward byte by byte for these misaligned pointers (INFERRED from newlib's strcpy). The mx4sio site (1031-1032) copies from uLE_path into gen_path and is not affected.
findings.fix: Replace the four identical three-line blocks with one small static helper that finds the separator and shifts the tail with memmove, called from the four branches.
findings.justification: The helper replaces four copies of the same three lines (net about 2 lines fewer) and makes the shift well defined.
findings.benefit: Defined behaviour for every usb/mass/ata/cf path; about 2 lines removed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read filer.c:966-1032: fatfs_sep/pathSep are strchr(gen_path, '/') at 975, 989, 1014, 1023, and the strcpy destination is the same pointer, source one byte later. The non-EXFAT branch (995-998) and mx4sio (1031-1032) take the separator from uLE_path, a different buffer. EXFAT is defined (ps2.yaml:629), so 989-991 is the compiled mass branch.

findings.title: Crystal light streak is cut off at 47% brightness: lifetime 2.2 s but fade computed over 2.6 s

findings.title: Text Editor docInsert deletes the selection before checking the 512 KB limit, so a refused paste loses the selected text
findings.problem: docInsert calls docDelete on the selection first and only then docReserve(n); when len - selection + n exceeds ED_MAX_SIZE (paste of a long clip over a selection in a file near 512 KB) the toast says the text is too large, but the selection is already gone and the document is marked dirty.

findings.title: filerGetGameTitle leaves two bytes of a rejected PS1 header in the title, and copy() uses them for the .psu name
findings.problem: The PS1 probe reads the first 2 bytes of the candidate save straight into out and returns -1 when they are not SC, leaving those bytes (and stale bytes after them) in out. The browser callers clear the title on failure, but copy() runs transcpy_sjis on the title whatever the result: a PSU backup with titles shown (or PSU_HugeNames) of a folder that holds a same-named, 8 KB-multiple file that is no PS1 save is named after those bytes, and the folder-conflict prompt shows them as the save title.
findings.fix: Read the 2-byte magic into a local buffer (or clear out[0] at finish when ret < 0) so a failed lookup always leaves an empty title.
findings.benefit: Correct .psu name and prompt in that case; no size change (READ).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:560-682: out[0] = 0 at 569, genRead(fd, out, 2) at 653, strncmp(out, SC) failure goes to finish at 655, finish does not clear out. Callers: dash_browser.c:321-322 and filer.c:2477-2479 reset title[0] on ret < 0; filer_copy.c:949-954 calls transcpy_sjis(cp, file.title) after any return, and 1050-1051 transcpy_sjis(tmp, newfile.title) likewise. np[0] is non-empty in that case, so the revert at 959-960 does not apply.

findings.title: loadExternalModule reports a failed embedded load as success (raw module ID used as a flag)
findings.problem: def_OK holds the return of SifExecModuleBuffer, which is negative on failure, so 'if (def_OK) return 1' also returns 1 when the embedded ps2kbd/DS34 module failed to load (and the start result in dummy is ignored). have_ps2kbd or have_ds34 is then latched for the IOP session, startKbd marks the keyboard open, and no retry happens; the header comment at 1523-1531 promises 0 in that case.
findings.fix: Set def_OK to (ID >= 0 && dummy != 1) instead of the raw ID.
findings.benefit: Correct 'not loaded' result for the keyboard/DS34 fallback; one-line change, no size change.
findings.evidence: Read init.c:1523-1556 and both callers (loadDs34Modules 1716-1723, loadKbdModules 2108-2119); grep loadExternalModule over src: definition, prototype at 360 and these three calls only. Elsewhere the file treats ID < 0 or ret == 1 (MODULE_NO_RESIDENT_END) as failure (comments at 641, 1192, 2899).

findings.title: loadFont accepts a truncated .fnt file and reports success with a partly stale FontBuffer
findings.problem: loadFont only rejects files larger than 4700 bytes; it never checks a minimum size or the genRead results. A file shorter than 100 bytes is checked against uninitialised FontHeader bytes, and a file with a valid header but shorter than 1018 + 3584 = 4602 bytes leaves the tail of FontBuffer from the previous font while returning 1. Reachable from Settings when the user picks a font file (dash_settings.c:2128) and at startup (main_startup.c:716).
findings.fix: Reject sizes below 4602 in the same size test at line 80 (accept only 4602..4700).
findings.justification: One extra comparison in an existing condition; it turns a truncated copy of a font file into the existing default-font fallback instead of mixed glyphs.
findings.benefit: Avoids corrupted glyphs from a truncated font file; no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read draw_text.c:67-106: size test line 80 (> 4700 only), genRead of 100-byte header line 86 unchecked, header bytes 0,1,70,72,83 tested 87-91, genRead(FontBuffer + 512, 3584) at offset 1018 line 94 unchecked, return 1 line 96. FontBuffer is u8[256*16] (font_uLE.c:4). Callers: dash_settings.c:2128, 2565, main_startup.c:716, config_startup.c:173, config.c:1611, main_actions.c:786.

findings.title: mcViewListSaves and describeSave re-walk the directory chain from its first cluster for every entry (quadratic)
findings.problem: Both loops call dirEntry(v, first, i), which uses chainRead from the first cluster, so entry i costs i/2 chainNext FAT lookups plus one full cluster read; a root of L entries costs about L*L/4 FAT lookups and L cluster reads instead of L/2. The file already has walkDir (lines 383-409), written for exactly this ('instead of re-walking the chain per entry'), used by the fingerprint and rootFind but not by the listing, which the card tool runs on the UI thread after every open and operation.
findings.fix: Drive the root loop of mcViewListSaves and the loop of describeSave with walkDir callbacks, as rootFind (mc_card_write.c:139-151) does.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: root of 600 entries (large 64 MB card) ~90,000 cached FAT lookups and 600 cluster reads become ~300 of each; on typical 8 MB cards (under ~150 entries) the gain is milliseconds. About the same line count.
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_view.c:121-156 chainRead (skip = offset/1024 chainNext steps from 'first'), 165-178 dirEntry (chainRead at i*512), 288-319 describeSave and 321-360 mcViewListSaves (dirEntry per i), 381-409 walkDir comment and code. grep mcViewListSaves: UI-thread callers dash_card_tool.c:451, 1005, 1102, 1180, 1231, 1486, 1566, 1745; mmce_save_versions.c:408, 411. Arithmetic: sum over i<L of i/2 = L*L/4.

findings.title: tsChoose never shows its fifth detail string (Tuna Date)
findings.problem: details[] has five entries, the fifth being "set selected MC folder to 2099", but the loop uses i < 4 ? details[i] : NULL, so the *Tuna Date row (passed as the fifth label when allow_tuna is set, filer_actions.c:1406-1415) never gets its detail and the string is dead.
findings.fix: Use the array size instead of 4 (or delete the fifth string if the row should stay bare).
findings.benefit: Trivial UI fix or a few bytes of dead .rodata (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c 2401-2416 and filer_actions.c 1405-1429: items[] has 5 labels, count = TIMESTAMP_ORGANIZE_COUNT when allow_tuna, passed to filerTimestampUi->choose = tsChoose (dash_timestamp_ui at 2538).

findings.title: tsChoose shows the detail text only for the first four folder-date choices; the *Tuna Date row never gets its detail
findings.problem: details[] has five strings, including 'set selected MC folder to 2099' for the fifth choice, but the loop assigns items[i].detail only for i < 4. selectTimestampOrganizationMode passes five items (TIMESTAMP_ORGANIZE_COUNT = 5, filer_actions.c:385-390) whenever the Tuna option is allowed, so that row is shown without its explanation.
findings.fix: Bound the detail lookup by the array size (5) instead of the literal 4.
findings.benefit: Cosmetic correctness: the fifth detail string becomes visible; no size change.
findings.evidence: Read dash_browser.c:2401-2416 and 2538-2557 (dash_timestamp_ui installed for time_manip_organize). filer_actions.c:385-390 enum gives TIMESTAMP_ORGANIZE_COUNT 5; 1406-1429 builds five items and calls filerTimestampUi->choose(..., items, count) with count 5 when allow_tuna.

findings.title: Crystal light streak ends at 2.2 s but is drawn on a 2.6 s path, so it vanishes mid-screen at about 47 % brightness
findings.problem: dashBgUpdate resets streak_t once it passes 2.2 s, but sceneCrystal computes p = streak_t / 2.6. The last drawn frame has p = 0.846: centre x = 680, a 240 px radius glow covering x 440-640, alpha 110*sin(0.846*pi) = 51 additive. It disappears in one frame instead of fading out off-screen. Visible in Crystal with effects at 100 %.
findings.fix: Use the same duration in both places (reset at 2.6f).
findings.benefit: Removes a visible pop in the Crystal scene; one constant changed.
findings.evidence: Read dash_bg.c:184-197 (streak lifetime 2.2) and 330-336 (p = streak_t / 2.6f, sx = -200 + p * (DASH_VW + 400)). DASH_VW 640 (dash_internal.h:17); dashGlow radius semantics at dash_gfx.c:815-823. That the pop is noticeable on a TV is INFERRED.

findings.title: FTP status loop sleeps 100 ms per frame, so the screen runs at about 8 fps and short OK/Back taps are lost
findings.problem: Each pass of DashFtpServer's UI-thread loop does a status RPC, draws, presents (vsync) and then DelayThread(100000). Input is edge-detected from one pad sample per pass (dash_ui.c:52-59, pad.c:62), so a press and release inside one ~117 ms pass never produces in.pressed; the user has to press again or hold. It is the only 100 ms sleep in the dash_* screens.
findings.fix: Drop the DelayThread (dashGfxPresent already waits for vsync) and query ftpSessionQuery only every few frames, e.g. every 6th pass, so the RPC rate stays about 10 Hz.
findings.benefit: Input sampled every frame instead of every ~117 ms and smooth animation on the FTP screen; about the same line count (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read dash_ftp.c:90-120 (ftpSessionQuery, ftpFrame -> dashGfxPresent, dashInputPoll, DelayThread(100000)); ftp_session.c:28-65 (exchange waits in 1 ms steps for the reply). dash_ui.c:35-59 dashInputPoll reads one sample via readpad; pad.c:62 new_pad = newly pressed bits since the previous sample. grep DelayThread over src/dash_*.c: only dash_ftp.c:119 sleeps 100 ms. The tap-length claim is INFERRED.

findings.title: Unbounded strcpy/strcat/sprintf path joins into MAX_PATH buffers in newdir, make_title_cfg and setHddCommonFolderTimestamp
findings.problem: These join a caller path (up to MAX_PATH-1 = 1024 chars) and a name (up to 255) into a 1025-byte stack buffer with no length check, while the rest of the file (delete 1972, getFileSize 314/352, Rename 2176-2182) checks snprintf and returns -ENAMETOOLONG. A copy into a destination whose path plus folder name exceeds 1024 bytes (newdir from filer_copy.c:1048/1081) or a title.cfg in a folder deeper than 1015 chars overruns the stack. Needs very long paths, so practical risk is low.
findings.fix: Replace each strcpy+strcat (or sprintf) pair with one snprintf into the buffer and return -ENAMETOOLONG (make_title_cfg: set the error message) when the result does not fit, as delete() already does at 1972.
findings.justification: Adds a length test per join, but each strcpy+strcat pair becomes a single snprintf, so line count does not grow; it closes a stack overflow on over-long paths using the pattern already used elsewhere in the file.
findings.benefit: Removes 8 unbounded writes into 1025-byte stack buffers; about 4 lines saved by merging strcpy+strcat pairs (INFERRED from cited lines).
findings.evidence: Read all cited lines. MAX_PATH=1025, MAX_NAME=256 (launchelf.h:201-205). getHddParty writes dir with snprintf(dir, MAX_PATH, "pfs0:%s", ...) (gui_hdd0_format.c:37), then newdir/setHddCommonFolderTimestamp strcat the name. Callers of newdir: dash_browser.c:1157 (name limited to 36 by dashModalFilename at 1151), filer_browser.c:1440, filer_copy.c:1048/1081 (outPath + newfile.name, MAX_NAME). make_title_cfg callers: dash_browser.c:1217, filer_browser.c:1589. Trigger needs a path over ~770 chars, which no device listing here produces in normal use.

findings.title: filerGetGameTitle's .psu scan turns a large entry size into a backward seek and can loop up to 2^31 times
findings.problem: psu_pad_pos is an int computed from the u32 entry size read from the file, so a size of 0x80000000 or more becomes a negative SEEK_CUR offset that moves back to an earlier header, and the loop is bounded only by the first header's count (also from the file, up to 0x7FFFFFFF). A malformed .psu keeps the title scan re-reading the same headers, stalling the browser listing job on the worker (dash_browser.c:321) or the classic listing (filer.c:2477) whenever titles are shown.
findings.fix: Declare psu_pad_pos as u32 so the seek always goes forward; a bogus size then seeks past the end and the next header read fails.
findings.benefit: Removes a hang on malformed .psu files; no size change (READ; the trigger needs a crafted or corrupt file).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:560-628. psu_header.size is u32 (include/psu_types.h:32); PSU_content = PSU_head.size (613) bounds the loop; psu_pad_pos = (size + 0x3FF) & -0x400 (622) is stored in int (565) and passed to genLseek(fd, psu_pad_pos, SEEK_CUR) (623), whose offset is s64 (filer_fileops.c:680). Example: header 2 with size 0xFFFFFC00 gives -1024 and returns to header 1 at offset 512 every pass. The restore path checks entries against the file size first (psu_restore_check_entries, filer_copy.c:1024); this title path does not.

findings.title: Devices grid refresh issues a PC CARD CF devctl RPC from the UI thread every 0.5 s, even while a worker job runs
findings.problem: devUpdate calls devRefresh every 0.5 s, and dashDevicesList calls getPcCardCfCapacitySectors (a fileXioDevctl SIF RPC) whenever the PCCF driver is loaded. This is UI-thread IO without the dashWorkerIoBusy() gate that dash_main.c:1472 applies to the other device polls (dash_worker.c:7-10 rule), so the frame waits on the shared fileXio RPC while a worker copy or listing is in flight. Only consoles with the CF driver loaded (early Japanese models) are affected.
findings.fix: In dashDevicesList skip the capacity devctl while dashWorkerIoBusy() is true (show the PROBE_PCCF result already recorded by probeMount instead).
findings.justification: One added condition removes a periodic blocking RPC from the render thread; it follows the existing gate used for the other device polls and is smaller than caching the capacity.
findings.benefit: Removes up to 2 RPCs/s from the UI thread on the Devices screen; avoids frame stalls during background IO on CF-equipped consoles (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read dash_files.c:467-472, 574-594 (devRefresh every 0.5 s), dash_devices.c:404-439, init.c:3172-3200 (fileXioDevctl PCCF_CONTROL_STATUS), dash_main.c:1468-1481 (other polls gated by !dashWorkerIoBusy()), dash_worker.c:1-22. The stall length depends on the fileXio RPC being serialised against the worker's in-flight call (INFERRED, not measured).

findings.title: getExternalFilePath dereferences NULL for an hdd0:/PART or dvr_hdd0:/PART path without a file part (boot-time crash from a hand-edited CNF)
findings.problem: For 'hdd0:/NAME' the code builds party='hdd0:NAME', then p=strchr(party,'/') is NULL, so sprintf prints '(null)' and *p=0 stores to address 0; the DVR branch is identical. USBKBD_FILE and KBDMAP_FILE are copied from the CNF unchecked (config.c:1039-1042) and startKbd runs on every boot, safe mode included (main_modules.c:54), so such a value crashes each start until the CNF is fixed elsewhere. Paths picked in the file browser always contain the file part.
findings.fix: When p is NULL, fall back to genFixPath(argPath, filePath) and return (one check per branch).
findings.justification: One NULL test per branch closes a store to address 0 reached from a config value at boot; nothing simpler prevents it.
findings.benefit: Removes a boot crash loop on a malformed keyboard path (INFERRED consequence of a NULL store on the EE).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:1412-1463, 1533-1556, 2108-2119, 2919-2953; config.c:1039-1042; main_modules.c:18-59. grep usbkbd_file|kbdmap_file: set by config.c:1040/1042, config_startup.c:160/162 (file browser), dash_settings.c:2041/2044 (file picker); read only by init.c loadKbdModules/startKbd. Callers of getExternalFilePath: loadExternalFile and loadExternalModule only.

findings.title: make_title_cfg ignores the genWrite result, so a failed or short write leaves a truncated title.cfg with no message
findings.problem: genWrite's return is discarded and _msg0 is only set when the open fails. On a full memory card or USB stick the file is created (O_TRUNC) but the write can fail or be short, leaving an empty or cut title.cfg that OPL then reads, and the user sees no error: both callers only show a message when _msg0 is set (dash_browser.c:1219, filer_browser.c:1589).
findings.fix: Compare genWrite's result with the buffer length and set an error message in _msg0 when it differs.
findings.justification: Adds one comparison and one message; the problem is a silent corrupt title.cfg on a full or failing device, and checking the one write is the smallest way to report it.
findings.benefit: Failed title.cfg writes are reported instead of silently leaving a truncated file (no size change; ~2 lines added).
findings.evidence: Read filer_actions.c:1917-1936. Callers: dash_browser.c:1212-1222 (opTitleCfg toasts only if fb.msg[0]), filer_browser.c:1589. Menu entry is enabled only for .ELF names (filer_browser.c:447-450), so the strlen-4 at 1923 is safe.

findings.title: HDD scan allocates 1400 HddPart entries (about 246 KB) and keeps them while the HDD Manager is open
findings.problem: scanRun mallocs sizeof(HddPart) * MAX_PARTITIONS (180 B * 1400, launchelf.h:206) and scan() keeps the whole block as hm.parts even when the disk has a few dozen partitions; during a rescan (after every create/remove/rename) the old and the new 246 KB blocks are alive together.
findings.fix: After the Dread loop, shrink j->parts to j->n entries with realloc when j->n > 0 (keep the original block if realloc fails).
findings.justification: Adds about three lines; it frees roughly (1400 - n) * 180 bytes of EE heap for as long as the HDD Manager is open, the simplest way short of changing the scan to two passes.
findings.benefit: 180 B * 1400 = 252,000 B allocated; with 100 partitions about 234 KB returned to the heap while the screen is open (INFERRED: struct size from field layout)
findings.evidence: Read dash_hdd.c:84-94 (HddPart: name[33], 7 ints/u32, GameInfo), include/hdl_rpc.h:9-15 (GameInfo 33+65+13+int = 116 B) -> 64 + 116 = 180 B; launchelf.h:206 MAX_PARTITIONS = 1400; dash_hdd.c:162 malloc, 373-376 hm.parts takes the block, 1335 freed only on exit, 596-601 afterChange rescans. Struct size is computed by hand, not from a map file.
